title: Könnte gut sein
body:
Ist aber an allen Ecken und Enden noch unfertig und voller kleiner, ärgerlicher Bugs und Schlampereien:

Nach dem Upgrade zu Premium landet man in einer Sackgasse und man muss die App neu starten, weil der ‚du hast jetzt viele tolle Features Screen‘ nicht mehr weggeht

Ich bekomme trotz upgrade sporadisch angezeigt, dass ich den Free Account verwende.

Die Online Version zeigt trotz login ohnehin nur den Free Account und weiß nicht, dass ich gerade bezahlt habe.

Will ich einfach auf die normale Any.do Website und habe ich mich zuvor eingeloggt kann ich dort nicht mehr hin - werde immer weitergeleitet.

Themes die mir beim Upgrade versprochen werden gibt es in der Web und Desktop Version gar nicht.

Das sind lauter kleine Schwächen die auf schlampige Umsetzung / ein überstürztes Release hindeuten. Und das sind nur die Dinge die man auf den ersten Blick sieht.
Diese Schwächen deuten darauf hin, dass sich niemand die Mühe gemacht hat das wirklich mal zu testen bevor man es auf die Menschheit los lässt.

So einer zusammengeschusterten App vertraue ich meine Daten nicht an.

title: Any do is going downhill
body: When I first downloaded Any do about a year ago it was great! I don’t like having to click so many times to switch between calendar and to do lists! And there are so many new features which just aren’t helpful and clutter the interface. And the bugs are terrible! At least half the time when I open Any do I have to force close the app and reopen because the calendar keeps loading as 2022 instead of 2023. Sometimes the calendar loads as 2012 or another random past year! Now my Any do widget on my Home Screen isn’t loading! Unfortunately I think it may be time to delete Any do as it’s become an app that hinders my day rather than helps me organise my life.

title: Easy to create shared tasks but problems inviting
body:
Using this app to help me get support from friends and family. 
Love the calendar integration. 
Would love to share a calendar as well within the app so that someone can help assist with carer duties by taking someone to an appointment.
Tasks can easily be created, but when you share them, it’s not easy to see who you’ve shared it with. I have a list with over 20 invitees and you can’t scroll down the list to assign the task to someone as they cannot be found. 
And when adding someone to the list after the list has been shared, you need to resend invites to everyone again? There’s no function to just invite new people to a list. Those already invited and joined get another email and are duplicated on the list! 
Please fix this bug!

title: On the right track, love the core concept, sadly execution fails
body:
I've been using this app on and off for years, I keep trying other options, yet always keep wanting to come back due to the simplicity.

The today, tomorrow, upcoming & someday approach helps me to keep priority without adding burden of dates and times (this is my fav feature).

However sadly the following frustrations in day to day use keep me from returning permanently:

1 - Automatically remove completed tasks, rather than a two step process, this is such an odd decision, especially with things like shopping lists (support tell me no plans to change this feature).

2 - New features that are advertised don’t seem to show up in the app.  For example drag and drop of sub tasks (with this feature sub tasks are useless), listed in release notes for months yet still no where to be seen (either in beta or normal release).  Shopping list feature also still missing, but listed clearly in release notes. (Support told me these features are rolling out slowly, I’m not sure over months is within this definition).

3 - At least a passable desktop experience for windows and mac, not just a stupidly spaced out "web app" that doesn't make sense (support suggest this will be fixed in 2019).

title: Pretty good
body:
This app has a lot of things going for it. Great UI, loads of features.

One thing that I really dislike is the way you have to assign a time to a task if you want to assign a day to it. Why can't I just say I want to complete something on Wednesday at some point? I am a teacher so my schedule changes week to week, things move at the last minute and it is a hassle having to assign a time to things. The feature is great if I want to add a push notification to remind me to do something like change the date on the whiteboard before first bell but a pain for something like sending an email which I will do whenever I get a spare 5 minutes.

Also not a fan of the new Plan Day feature. I don't use it anymore since it automatically adds a reminder to a task that I bump to a new day. In my line of work, I have heaps of short tasks. If I bump 5 tasks to tomorrow, it automatically gives them to 9:00am with a reminder. Literally the last thing I want is 5 reminders coming in at 9:00 when the kids are arriving. And it completely defeats the whole point if i them have to go in to each task to remove the reminder.

I also dislike the convoluted process of deleting a repeated task. Should just be able to swipe to delete rather than go into a task, change the repeat to a once off task then tick off the task.

I wish there was a way to see if a task was overdue. Could be as simple as having the text in read. Or having an overdue heading in the Sort by: Time view. At them moment you have to go right in to a task.

title: Many bugs
body:
There are several issues that must be addressed if the app is to continue to be successful:

First, On the sign in screen, currently the emphasis for sign in choice is placed upon signing in through Google or Facebook. There should be a button placed alongside these to with the option to sign in by email address like what is offered on the web version. This is needlessly confusing as annoying.

Second, there is an error prevalent at the moment pertaining to the naming of folders, settings and links. It seems as though the correct titles for these elements are not being displayed in favour of what looks to be mid-development placeholders. This really needs to be addressed.

Third, in both the app and web versions, reordering sub tasks is not possible. This is a huge drawback for the app in general.

With these issues still prevalent, what could be a fantastic app really fails to be of much use.

- need ability to change sounds (too quiet)
- sharing a task with someone needs to preserve date & time

title: Love it.. If only it could DO my jobs
body:
I'm still disorganised but that's not Any.DOs fault. This app provides all the tools you need to remind yourself of your tasks as and when you need to do them. All you have to do then is do as you are told. Easier said than done for the pathologically lazy.

My only suggestion for the next version would be that Any.DO actually does my work for me. That would be nice.

I'm actually writing this review instead of doing something that Any.DO so faithfully reminded me of. 

The alert took 30 seconds (if that) to enter and set a reminder thanks to the elegance of the user interface and a good 10 minutes to avoid responding to by jumping on an invitation to write a review.

title: Almost perfect
body:
This is still my favourite productivity app: I love the design, the simplicity, the fact that I can drag and drop tasks into the order I want, that it syncs with Chrome, and it's FREE! However, I was hoping my gripes from the previous version would be fixed in this version, but these ones still persist:

• I love that you can turn the phone landscape to easily drop tasks onto particular due dates, but when you turn it back to portrait the tasks within "Upcoming" are not displayed in chronological order. If you drag them around to put them in chronological order, they forget the date you just assigned them and revert to some kind of default (end of the month it seems). This is the most frustrating thing about the app at the moment: it's brilliant for Today, Tomorrow and Someday tasks, but Upcoming is always disorganised.
• Task order does not sync between iPhone app and the Chrome add on.

Really looking forward to the update where these are addressed, then it will be perfect!

title: Fantastic.
body:
I'm a lists person. Sometimes, though, I forget that -- and countless hours can be spent lazing about because I'm too lazy to make my lists. Any.Do allows you to add to your lists as you go, add sub tasks, sort them into folders, share tasks (and related sub tasks) with friends, and there is the option to prioritise (mark as red) the important tasks. The best part is that Any.Do moment reminds you to take a quick minute each day to sort your tasks out.

You can set alarms, and reminders for when you arrive/leave specified locations. 

Clean, clear, simple and beautiful. 

Hello, productivity.

title: Cadê a revisão de tarefas?
body: Muito bom ver um app evoluindo e oferecendo novidades. Porém, excluíram a melhor funcionalidade do app, que era de revisar todas as atividades do dia, uma a uma, e dar alguma ação a elas. Não entendi a redundância de, para as tarefas estarem em “Meu dia”, eu ter que colocá-las manualmente todos os dias, sendo que já atribui data anteriormente. Posso não estar sabendo usar as novidades mas o app perdeu pela metade sua funcionalidade pra mim. Antes das mudanças, era o melhor que havia encontrado pra ajudar a organizar a vida de alguém com TDAH. Agora, tá como os demais, que necessitam que a gente empregue energia para organizá-los pra conseguir que eles nos ajudem a nos organizar.

title: Melhor app
body: Eu nunca faço avaliação de Apps, mas este eu fiz questão. Estava passando por um momento muito difícil na vida pessoal do qual me vi tenho que tomar muitas decisões inclusive sobre a vida de de outra pessoa por motivos de saúde em 2018. E este app me ajudou muito a lembrar das coisas que precisava fazer. No momento que eu lembro que tenho que fazer algo ja anoto e deixo. Durante o dia ou toda manhã ja vejo o que preciso fazer e assim o stress de ter esquecido de fazer algo diminuir. Coisas que achava que tinha prioridade sem ter, foram se revelando e foi diminuindo a pressão do meu dia! Recomento e é um excelente investimento.

title: Excelente!
body:
Uso a versão gratuita e acho o aplicativo formidável. Destaco três pontos: 1) tarefas por localização: para quem visita clientes ou cidades, você pode programar o lembrete da tarefa ao se aproximar do local. 2) Compartilhamento de tarefas: isso permite você delegar tarefas enquanto se desloca. 3) Planejamento diário: o App  tem um momento diário para planejamento.

Pontos ruins: 1) algumas tarefas somem, eh verdade. E não tem como fazer backup. 2) A impressão das tarefas eh defeituosa.

Bem, está aí, eu recomendo!!!!!!

title: O melhor.
body:
Uso há mais de um ano, e a cada atualização fica melhor.
Você pode criar pastas de tarefas para fazer, a cada tarefa/task você pode criar sub-tarefas dentro dela, marcar data para o fazer. Ver as tarefas ordenadas por "hoje", "amanhã", "em breve" ou "algum dia". Pra mim, é ótimo e no iOS que estou usando, as tarefas aparecem na barra de resumo do dia, sabe, aquela em que mostra a temperatura do dia? Então, nessa aí. E por lá, nessa barra eu posso também já selecionar o que eu já fiz. Enfim, perfeito.

title: APP ÓTIMO - Falta Tags
body:
Gosto muito do Any.do, acho sua interface pratica e o any.do moment sensacional.

Como App para utilização off-line no celular acho o melhor.

Alguns pontos ainda devem ser melhorados:

- sincronização ainda da bugs
- acho a organização em pastas meio confusa ainda (visualmente)
- sinto falta da funcionalidade de Tags para filtrar atividades similares. (Ou a possibilidade de ver a divisão de dias dentro da categoria)
- ainda acho a interface WEB bem ruim e notei que pararam de atualizar a extensão do Chrome que utilizava.

Mesmo assim, ganha 4 estrelas pela praticidade e facilidade de uso no celular e recurso de criar tarefas a partir de e-mails.

title: Wonderful! However...
body:
Great app, I totally recommend. It really improved my organizational skills.
However, the last update brought a major setback:
by re-rearranging the edit (pencil) and important (!!) icons, they lost accuracy in relation to the touch screen. Now you touch one of them and open the other, or simply go back to the main screen, having to touch them multiple times in order to make it work!
The update before that had actually made so much better; you it's messed with a good thing and made it worse!
Please fix that!! 

The other innovations from the last update are wonderful, though.

title: Fantastic app!! Some suggestions. App fantástico!!! Algumas sugestões
body:
SUGESTIONS:

- I would like to have a search engine for me to find my task easily

- I would like to type with my iphone in the horizontal position. It is much easier.

- The editing system should be better. When i want to write a word on the begining of my task notation, I have to roll until I get to the begining and then type it there.

SUGESTÕES:
- Faltou uma janela de busca para conseguir encontra tarefas que eu quero editar com facilidade.

- Faltou poder escrever com o iphone deitado.

- precisa melhorar o sistema de edição de notas. atualmente preciso ir arrastando ate onde eu quero começar a escrever. Seria melhor se eu pudesse clicar exatamente onde eu quero editar. 

Tirando isso é um app fantástico!!!

title: Muito bom
body: Comecei a usar o app recentemente. É ótimo, permite adicionar tarefas por voz e adorei o recurso de revisão diária, chamado Any.DO Moment. Falta na minha opinião maior flexibilidade para tarefas repetitivas (cada "x" dias, repetir "x" dias após conclusão, entre outros). Sinto falta também de um app para iPad e Mac, a extensão para Chrome é bacana, mas um tanto limitada. A sincronização não é constante, você precisa fechar e reabrir o app, mas funciona e é rápida! Ah, o design minimalista é sensacional, acho até que a Apple tenha se inspirado no Any.DO para desenvolver o iOS 7.

Abs,

title: Altamente recomendado!
body:
Este é um daqueles aplicativos indispensáveis para iOS. E se ainda não faz parte desta seleta lista, deveria fazer.

Mais minimalista impossível! O Any.DO é uma excelente ferramenta para guardar lembretes. Sua interface simples e limpa - mas sem deixar de ser intuitiva, ajuda a organizar as tarefas do dia-a-dia com muita mais facilidade.

Possui recurso para criação de lembretes por voz, inclusive, em português do Brasil. Traz ainda integração com a central de notificações, com a agenda do iPhone - sendo possível ligar ou enviar SMS e, também, com o calendário.

- Lag that doesn’t allow you to complete or move around items
- Inability to complete Todos (when checking an item off, it unchecks itself immediately afterwards)
- My recurring tasks often skipping certain a recurrence (or disappearing completely forever)
- Using “Sort items by time” rarely works (all the items appear out of order)

title: Planner sound can not be turned down
body:
A great feature of the any.do app is the daily planner. It allows you to pick and choose the tasks to be done today. It really helps plan out the day. When I get up in the morning my routine is to plan the day out and I have found the Any.do has simplified the task enormously. The big issue is that when working in the planner there is no volume control and despite the volume of my iPad being muted the tones are at top volume. So loud they will wake up light sleepers in other rooms. Once you have started the daily planner you are stuck in it until all tasks are sorted with each task making a high picked sound. There is no being discreet with this app.
Hopefully this issue gets a fix like a volume button in the planner but otherwise this app gets full thumbs up for simplicity and effectiveness. I have used many apps and switched to this one because it was compatible with Alexis but found it to be one of the better apps to keep my bust day organized. Iron out the really loud tone and it’s five stars for me.

title: Overhyped. Buggy. Limited Functionality.
body:
I really wanted to like this app. So much so that I committed to a year of premium service and switched wholesale from my other productivity tools.

Overall I've been really disappointed with the experience. The app is very buggy and seems very immature given how long the tool has been around. In particular syncing can be hit and miss. Sub tasks can't be reordered so anyone who likes organization and hierarchy will struggle. Setting due dates is laborious as is using location based reminders- unless you already have the address in your contacts. If you use the term 'call' when creating a to-do the app will link to a contact's phone number but often links to incorrect phone numbers belonging to alternate contacts. 

Any.do moment is a great feature but without a useful app behind it, I've found it quickly becomes gimmicky. Far easier just to set an alarm to prompt the planning of your day. 

So with 7 months of paid service I'm switching back to my previous free service as its more effective. 

Coles notes? A pretty app that places more emphasis on interface than actually getting things done. Save your money.

title: High functioning
body:
Any.do works well. I have some minor cosmetic/procedural gripes, nothing that can't be fixed with an update

Things I love 
- ability to sort by date, priority, or category
- integration with (their) calendar 
- subtasks (although I would prefer it still show up as one task)
- beautiful clean interface
- ability to invite others to tasks

Small tweaks I'd appreciate 
- fuller integration with Cal - I would love scheduled any.do events to show up in Cal, and be 'cross-off-able' in Cal
- when you set a task, you have to 'x' out of it, which feels bizarre - like you're deleting it 
- when I add a new task, I'd like the options for inviting, subtasks, etc to already be open under the task, not have to click them. I find I have to add the task first, then go back to edit it.

title: Best to-do app out there
body:
This app is exactly what my little OCD brain was looking for in a to-do app. Quickly add items to one of several lists like personal, work, "someday" (LOVE that one!), etc. Tap to view whole item, tap the pencil icon to edit, and swipe to delete (which strikes and greys item out, throwing it to the bottom of the list for you). Delete it completely when ready. 
  Turn device to landscape and it ALSO shows your calendar in list mode, a feature that seemingly disappeared in Calendar's regular view mode for ios7! [side note: in calendar, you now have to hit the search icon to look at things in list mode]. What I love about this is, you can edit your calendar items in any.do and it syncs the update in your regular calendar!
  Wonderful layout and design, Customizable settings (including high-contrast), definitely worth downloading!

title: Beautiful, very useful app.
body:
I love this app! Visually, it's beautiful. The interface is clean, polished, and sleek. It's a pleasure to navigate through it.

In terms of functionality, it does almost everything you would want a task app to do. The "Any.Do Moment" feature is brilliant and helps you to keep on top of your day. 

But, what really puts this app over the top is the Chrome desktop app. If you use Gmail and Chrome, you can download the desktop app which syncs your computer and mobile device. It integrates so well that it basically turns your inbox into a personal assistant. With one click you can turn an email into a "to do" item or tell the app to remind you to take action on an email at a certain time. Very useful.

I just have a few minor quibbles, which I hope will be resolved through updates. First, it doesn't let you choose unique reminders like every Friday or every third Saturday of the month, etc. It would be helpful to have that because that would actually reflect how people do certain things in their life.

Second, it seems difficult to delete a task once you have created it. Maybe it's just me, but as far as I could see, the only way to delete a task is to mark it as "done" and then remove it. There should be a way just to delete it. 

Overall, great app. I have used a number of task apps, and this is by far my favourite.

title: Interactive
body:
One of Any.Do's best features is that it doesn't have to wait to be opened up to start interacting with the user. The handy 'notifications' that it sends when the phone is off, along with a subtle noise is great for people who need a little push to do something on their list, or for anyone who is forgetful... And since the notifications are available to have times set for them, this feature can be fully taken advantage of.

title: Best to do app I've used
body:
The best feature of this to do app is being able to easily move tasks between the following categories:

Today
Tomorrow
This week 
Later

If you turn it over to landscape mode you are also able to drag a task to any other date in the month. This is great for splitting up your tasks into manageable chunks and also for planning your days and schedule accordingly. 

The shared task sync between other users does not seem to appear to work well or consistently, otherwise I'd give this app 5 stars. Also it occasionally does not shift the day forward.

Another great new feature is the option to plan your day on a regular basis each morning, confirming your set tasks for the day or deferring them to another time.

title: Honest Review: "Perfect"
body:
For its simplicity this application is efficient & very powerful. It is very smooth synchronizes perfectly between both my iPhone & iPad. 

The GPS allows you to set reminders when you arrive or exit a location, as well as the standard essential functions you would expect from a reminders app. 

While typing it will allow has the functionality of predictive-text, completing phrases while you insert them. 

You can sort your tasks by creating personal folders, or use the embedded mini-engine "AnyDo" which allows you to quick set tasks in sequences of "Today", "Tomorrow", "Someday", etc. In time you'll find this little jewel quite useful for quickly sorting items. You also have the ability to re-use deleted tasks. 

Overall, if you are searching for an app that is simple & powerful; it delivers!

title: Best in Class
body:
By far the best app of it's type, great interface that is quick and easy to use. 

Love how quickly you can add a new task (by voice); how you can easily mark something as important; and how easily you can put off a task until the next day/week/someday by simply dragging it down.

Unfortunately it's greatest strength is also it's weakness. The simplicity often comes at the cost of flexibility & advanced features. 

I don't like the Upcoming category. If I want to do a task sometime in the next week I'm forced to either place it in upcoming or I have to set a specific day & time.

Complaints aside, this app is awesome and easy to use. Most importantly it's effective at helping you get things done.

title: Keeping it simple for better or worse...
body:
First thing first, Any.Do sports a simple, intuitive (as long as you're used to iOS UI conventions) and responsive interface. While the cloud synchronization is quick and works as intended, this app stays fully functional without a network connection. 

There is a good balance between the number of features and keeping everything breezy, but some stuff is missing:

- Default parameters for new task.
- Being able to switch in landscape while creating a task (I have a hard time with the portrait keyboard).
- A way to assign a task to both a folder and a date while it is created.

Keep up the good work! Can't wait for the HTML5 version of the service!

title: Quite the app!
body:
I have been in need for a great task app, and I find that this one is very easy to use, professional looking, and has a simple design that isn't contesting. 
There are just a few things that are stopping me from using this app over others:
- I wish I could see the notes within each task right away when I open them, or at least an overview of the notes. Even just having the times they are due displayed without me having to open them would be nice. 
- it would be nice to have the option to add photos to the app. 
- it would be a bonus to have a monthly calendar view to show the number of tasks within each day. 

This app is fantastic, professional, and sleek, and I am going to continue to use it. I would of course, like to see some of the suggested tweaks implemented. Great job!

title: The design isn’t great, sync is terrible
body:
Switched from Wunderlist, mainly for the grocieries function.
Would have liked to use it on an ipad+iphone, with one list shared w my wife. Tried to use it for months, now I’ve deleted it.

The design is not very intuitive, the app tries to push its functions into your face, instead of letting you choose what you want to do. This is annoying, but I would have lived with it.

Sync has been horrible, for a long time now. Doesn’t snyc between my devices, or my wives, if it does, not fully, and always veery slow. I just  keep trying to refresh/snyc. Sometimes items get stuck on 1 device. Super bad. It’s not like it has to snyc crazy amounts of complex data....never had this with any other apps. Network connection is strong.

Now it started crashing. Doesn’t start at all. Tried to restart the phone. Updated the app on every device to the latest. Still the same, crashes right after start. So that was it for us.

So long, and thanks for all the fish.

title: Kein Sync mit Apple Apps
body:
Intuitive, einfache und stylische App, dass muss man den Entwickler lassen. Wieso ich die App aber wieder gelöscht habe und es nur 3 Sterne gibt ist, weil es keinen Sync zu Apples iCal gibt, bzw. Erinnerungen-App. Ohne einen Abgleich fehlen mir jegliche Einträge auf dem Desktop und somit fehlt die komplette Übersicht über Termine, sprich Aufgaben/Erinnerungen. Und nein, Chrome Extension ist keine Lösung für mich, da ich erstens Chrome nicht verwende, zweitens nicht auf Extension stehe und vor allem weil Chrome mich nicht daran erinnern kann wenn etwas ansteht. Es soll ja die Standard-App ersetzen und nicht zusätzlich verwendet werden. Sonst ist die App wirklich sehr schön umgesetzt. Das eine oder andere kann man sicher noch implementieren, sonst aber gut so.

Update 25.3.2020
—————————
Scheinbar wird es nie einen Sync zu den bestehenden Apps von Apple geben. Für mich unverständlich und persönlich ein Killerkriterium. Das verwalten in verschiedenen Apps kommt für mich nicht in Frage, das macht alles nur komplizierter und unübersichtlicher. Zudem funktioniert alles so träge und langsam.
Ich gebe die Sterne für‘s Design und UI und weil der Ansatz gut ist.

title: Teuer-Abo
body:
Zuerst stürzt das Portemonnaie ab nach Bezahlung des Abos, dann die App. 
Abo gleich wieder gekündigt. 
Nach Abhaken von Tasks passiert sekundenlang nix, bis der Haken erscheint. Man meint, man hätte das Kästchen nicht richtig getroffen und so deaktiviert man den Haken wieder und so weiter, so‘n Quatsch hab ich noch nie gesehen. 
Wiederholungen von Tasks gibts auch nicht. 
Nonsens für viel Geld. 
••••
Hallo!
Sie haben auf meine Rezension geantwortet. 
Es ist nicht meine Aufgabe an der Verbesserung der App mitzuarbeiten und den Support zu kontaktieren. 
Ich habe das Abo bezahlt und kann erwarten, dass das funktioniert bei Nutzung. 
Ich werde keinesfalls Zeit investieren, die ich nicht habe. 
Deswegen nutze ich ja die App, um Zeit zu sparen. 
Wenn sie also abstürzt, bin ich doppelt geschädigt - finanziell bei Bezahlung und dann bei eingeschränktem Gebrauch und dann soll ich noch mitwirken ...
Ich kauf ja auch kein Auto, um danach der Werkstatt helfen zu müssen, weil es nicht fährt.

All in all, it's just too expensive compared to other apps.

title: Bien au départ mais gros ennuis sur la fin!!
body:
J’ai beaucoup aimé cette application qui est je trouve très complète et utile et très bien faite.
Mais! Mais... depuis environ un gros mois peut-être plus je sais pas, mon application Any.do débloque complètement !! Elle bug, c’est-à-dire qu’après une action (p. Ex: rajouter une tâche ou en modifier une), l’écran (et l’app) se fige complètement. J’essaie d’appuyer sur un autre endroit que là où je voulais toucher au départ mais pas moyen, une fois figée, l’application quitte sans une explication sans un message d’erreur par la suite. Et ce à chaque fois que je l’ouvre maintenant, du coup chaque jour. Alors elle est devenue inutilisable.
J’ai pourtant envoyé par 2 fois un rapport d’erreur dans l’application même comme c’est possible mais je n’ai pas reçu de réponse et le problème reste inchangé.
Dommage... De plus j’ai perdu toutes les informations que j’avais mises dessus au fur et à mesure. Donc je sais pas si c’est un problème de version et de version (je l’ai mis à jour à chaque fois qu’il le fallait, qu c’était possible), ou alors de téléphone (iPhone 8 déjà dépassé?!)...?
Bref. Si jamais quelqu’un a rencontré les mêmes difficultés ou qu’il y’a un moyen de régler ce problème, faites-moi signe!

title: Sehr gelungen! Aber …
body:
Sehr gelungene App mit intuitiven Design. Ermöglich des schnelle eingeben von 2Do's.

Ist im Prinzip wie "Erinnerungen" von Apple, einfach das Interface ist anders aufgebaut und benötigt weniger Aufwand.

Gut ist, das man die Aufgaben sortieren kann. Schlecht finde ich jedoch das neue Aufgaben oberhalb und nicht unterhalb hinzugefügt werden, da man Aufgaben ja meistens in der Rheinfolge eingibt wie man sie abarbeiten möchte.
ausserdem finde ich es schlecht gelöst wenn eine Aufgabe einen zu langen Text hat. Dann wird dieser – wenn die Aufgabe ausgewählt ist – horizontal gescrollt. Ein Zeilenumbruch wäre wünschenswerter, da man dann die Aufgabe nicht zuerst anwählen und dann warten muss bis der Text durchgescrollt ist.

Etwas was mich wirklich stört ist, dass man die Ordner nicht sortieren kann. Eigentlich merkwürdig … Man kann die Aufgaben sortieren, sogar in andere Ordner ziehen, aber die Ordner leider nicht sortieren.

Was ich auch schade finde ist, dass es keine App für den Mac gibt. Im Moment gibt es nur eine Chrome Extension.

title: Schön, aber nicht ausgereift
body: Ich mag das Design sehr, und die Board-Ansicht der Desktopversion erleichtert die Planung der Woche erheblich. Doch die mobile App ist leider nicht viel mehr, als eine normale Liste, und auch auf dem Tablet findet man nichts der komfortablen Desktopversion. Die ist nur eine Kopie der Handy App. Im Gegensatz zu der Handy App nehmen in der horizontalen Ansicht allerdings unnötiger Weise die Listen-Ordner die Hälfte des Displays ein. Aber eine merkwürdige Funktion macht Any.do für mich unbrauchbar: wenn ich  eine Erinnerung an einem bestimmten Tag in die Liste einfügen will, drücke ich auf das plus Zeichen neben dem Wochentag. Aber dort wird sie nicht abgelegt. Sie landet bei Irgendwann. Das macht die Arbeit, besonders mit der mobilen App, unnötig umständlich.

title: Schlecht übersetzt, Usability fragwürdig, unzuverlässiger Support
body:
Diese To-do App bringt einige interessante Ideen mit, weswegen ich sie anhand der Beschreibung präferiert hatte. Nach der Installation hat mich als erstes die Bedienung ziemlich irritiert. Es gibt keine klare Menüführung und die Komponenten der App sind ziemlich verwirrend. Ich weiß nicht, warum der Entwickler auf die Idee gekommen ist, eigene Listenelemente zu entwickeln, anstatt die Standardelemente von Apple zu nutzen. Allein damit wäre es schon deutlich besser. Aber so ist die Gebrauchstauglichkeit wirklich unterirdisch.

Dazu kommt, dass die Übersetzung ins Deutsche vielfach schlecht oder sogar fehlerhaft ist. Auch das ist aktuell mit den Möglichkeiten künstliche Intelligenz wirklich nicht mehr nachvollziehbar. Es zeugt einfach nur von wenig Ernsthaftigkeit und Professionalität der Entwickler.

Zudem habe ich den Support angeschrieben und darum gebeten, mein Konto zu löschen. Aus der App heraus gab es immer nur eine Fehlermeldung, es hat einfach nicht funktioniert. Ich habe bis heute keine ordentliche Unterstützung erfahren. Ich kann jetzt einfach nur die App deinstallieren und damit leben, dass meine personenbezogenen Daten für alle Ewigkeit auf den Systemen liegen. Für eine datenschutzrechtliche Beschwerde ist mir zumindest der Aufwand zu hoch, aber eigentlich müsste man das machen.

title: Nicht alle Versprechen werden gehalten
body:
Leider habe ich mich zu schnell zu einem Abo entschieden, weil dummerweise nicht alle Versprechen gehalten werden. Deswegen vergebe ich auch nur zwei Sterne.

Problem 1, wenn man sich auf einem Apple Gerät registriert, dann kann man auf einem Windows Rechner die App nicht benutzen, weil der Apple Login nicht funktioniert. Es geht nur die Version im Browser. Andere Entwickler bekommen das hin.

Problem 2, es ist kein richtiger Sync der unterschiedlichen Kalender, sondern Any Do liest nur die Kalender aus, auf die das verwendete Gerät Zugriff hat. Den geschäftlichen Exchange Kalender sieht man nur auf dem geschäftlichen Handy in der App, nicht aber auf privaten Geräten. Any Do ist also nicht der Master, es liest nur aus, was auf dem Gerät im Zugriff ist. Damit ist die Sync Funktion völlig sinnlos.

Schade, weil die Bedienung der App ansonsten ziemlich gut wäre

title: Überteuert und schlecht programmiert
body:
Diese App ist - vor allem in Bezug auf die Premiumfunktionen - wirklich schlecht programmiert. Für die Premiumleistung zu zahlen ist nahezu rausgeworfenes Geld. Es gibt eine vergleichbare App, nur ohne dass man Kategorien anlegen könnte, die einmalig 5,37 Euro kostet für Premium und zuverlässiger läuft. 

Hier meine Kritikpunkte:
- Änderungen in der Uhrzeit wiederkehrender Aufgaben werden in 90% der Fälle nicht angenommen, ich muss also die Aufgabe löschen und neu anlegen. 
- heute erledigte Aufgaben sind immer noch auf der heutigen Liste, nur durchgestrichen. Das kann man auch nicht umstellen. 
- wiederkehrende Aufgaben, die beispielsweise Montag und Donnerstag anfallen, werden erst in der Liste für Donnerstag angezeigt, wenn ich sie am Montag erledigt habe. So kann man aber nicht planen!
- ich kann keine Dauer für Aufgaben einstellen. 

Sorry liebe Programmierer, da können andere Apps mehr für deutlich weniger Geld

title: Nicht alles Deutsch.
body:
Nicht alles in Deutsch übersetzt. Bitte alles in Deutsch.

Sehr sehr schlechte Übersicht. 

Es wäre cool wenn man verschiedenen Listen verschiedene Icons geben kann.

Auch cool wäre wenn man die Hintergrund Farbe und die Schriftfarbe selber einstellen kann.

Das man ganze listen ortsbasiert machen kann und nicht nur einzelne Einträge.

Der Ortsbasierten Erinnerungen sind sehr ungenau. Also die Erinnerung kommt schon viel ehr. 

Auch super wäre wenn man die Listen in der Listenansicht noch in Ordner zusammen fassen kann.

Praktisch wäre auch, wenn alles Getrennt werden würde. Alle Listen in einer Übersicht. Alle Zeit Erinnerungen in einer Übersicht und alle Orts Erinnerungen in einer Übersicht. ...

Bei Orts Erinnerungen fehlt dass man ein Radius angeben kann. Das die Erinnerung beim Betreten eines Radiuses erscheint.

Wenn man bei einer Erinnerung Notizen gemacht hat, dass diese in der Übersicht angezeigt wird oder ein Vermerk.

title: Fehlerhafte Terminspeicherung nach Update, sonst aber gut
body:
Beim Speichern von Termin wechselt das Datum immer auf das Jahr 2017. Sobald ich auch an der oberen Leiste ein Datum auswähle z.B. 13.09.20, dann wird beim Speichern immer ein Tag davor angezeigt also 12.09.20. Es ist umständlich, das richtige Datum nochmals einstellen zu müssen, gerade dann wenn es mal schnell gehen muss.

Unabhängig davon kommt es generell zu Fehlern beim Speichern. Manchmal werden Termine auf meinem Handy gespeichert und nicht auf dem Tablet - und das obwohl keine schlechte Internetverbindung besteht. Oder die App vertauscht Namen: in der Übersicht steht X aber wenn ich drauf klicke dann Y. 

Am Laptop kann ich nur den Google Kalender öffnen, aber nicht den, den ich mit dieser App bearbeite... 

Es wäre toll, wenn man auch freie Tage sehen könnte.

title: Sync funktioniert nicht
body:

Gerade die Funktion "Moment" ist wirklich toll, da man sich so gezielt einmal pro Tag durch seine Aufgaben arbeiten kann um sie für den jeweiligen Tag zu terminieren. Das große Problem ❗️ist allerdings, dass die Synchronisation der Aufgaben mit anderen Geräten nicht korrekt funktioniert. Termine die ich auf dem iPhone erstelle, werden mir auf dem Mac als abgelaufen angezeigt, obwohl sie auf dem iPhone bereits als erledigt markiert wurden. Der Abgleich mit der Apple Watch funktioniert überhaupt nicht. Es wir immer nur "Syncing tasks" angezeigt und dann passiert nichts mehr. 👎🏻

Was dem ganzen noch die Krone aufsetzt, ist der schlechte Support. Vor Wochen habe ich die Probleme gemeldet und ich habe immer noch keine Antwort erhalten. 😤

Da ich als  Unternehmer in der AutoBranche schon 30 Jahre zu Hause bin, glaubte ich der EMPFEHLUNG durch APPLE. Seit Jahren nutze ich EVERNOTE-Premium bzw. Timepage-Kalender mit Moleskine -Actions. Hier ist das eingesetzte Geld sinnhaft angewandt. 
Ehe man bei Any. do zum Ergebnis kommt, ist der Tag oder die Woche vorüber. Wie kommt es zu einer solchen Fehleinschätzung der Wertigkeit?
Ebenso vermisse ich eine durchgängige Bedienungsanleitung in DEUTSCH bei dem Preis; welches für Ihre Mitbewerber Standard ist. 
Bis zu ihrer Reaktion habe ich die App in den RUHESTAND versetzt. 
Aber wie heißt es so schön; aller Anfang ist schwer. 
Mit freundlichen Grüßen 
Günther Rüttgers

title: Eigentlich genial .........
body:
........wenn nicht die B Note wäre.

Zum positiven, der Funktionsumfang für eine Free App bzw. die freie Version, absolut genial und fair 👍👍👍

Einträge generieren mit Notizen, Spracheingabe, Video und Dropbox Support aller erste Sahne, da kann man nicht meckern. Die Aufmachung der App, schlicht und modern, ohne Ballast, auf den ersten Blick, schaut man unter die Haube sind doch einige Unzulänglichkeiten zu entdecken, zumindest für meinen Geschmack.

Was stört mich .....ich habe eine Aufgabe generiert sie mit einem Enddatum versehen und keiner sieht es auf den ersten Blick, erst mit wählen der einzelnen Aufgabe wird das Enddatum sichtbar. Ich finde das sehr unproduktiv, bedeutet es doch das ich jeden einzelnen Eintrag anklicken muss um Details zu erfahren und sei es nur das Enddatum der Aufgabe.

Das Ko Kriterium für Any Do ist in meinen Augen aber das Inseldasein. Any do kommuniziert mit keiner anderen Anwendung, Import aus einer beliebigen anderen App - Fehlanzeige. Import von Lesezeichen oder einem Link aus Safari, als Beispiel, in Any Do - Fehlanzeige. Das generieren eines anklickbaren Links in Any Do - Fehlanzeige, alles muss mühselig per Drag and Drop erarbeitet werden. 

So cool wie ich Any Do finde, Produktivität sieht anders. In diesem Zustand ist Any Do Chancenlos gegenüber vergleichbaren Apps.

title: Nicht zufriedenstellend
body:
Je nach dem wofür man sie nutzen möchte möglicherweise ausreichend, leider nicht für mich. Kurze Zusammenfassung: 

- nicht alle Optionen lassen sich gleich für eine Aufgabe einstellen sondern man muss sie mehrmals anfassen um Dinge wie Wiederholen, Erinnerung etc. einzustellen
- Aufgaben die erst in Monaten fällig werden stehen trotzdem unter "in Kürze" und Müllen so den Platz zu
- Aufgaben werden nicht sortiert nach Fälligkeitsdatum
- verschiebt man eine Aufgabe händisch, so verändert sich das Fälligkeitsdatum und die Uhrzeit wahllos was bedeutet das man nicht korrekt erinnert wird 
- man kann die Wiederholung nicht vierteljährlich einstellen

Alles in allem habe ich die App nach einer Woche wieder gelöscht. Wer aber einfach nur eine ungeordnete Liste braucht für den reichts.

title: Update in die Vergangenheit - Finger weg!
body: Any.DO hatte ich früher gerne genutzt, weil es sehr leichtgewichtig konzipiert war: keine unnötigen Features, schnell geladen, Todos angelegt und morgens neu arrangiert. Seit dem letzten Update lädt die App ewig und reagiert nur sehr verzögert, manche Buttons funktionieren gar nicht mehr. Dass Any.DO wesentlich weniger Features hat als andere ToDo-Apps, war  für eine kostenlose App ja ok, vielleicht sogar eine Stärke. Aber Basis-Features, die jede Freeware bietet (und bis zu diesem Update auch Any.DO!), hinter ein horrendes monatliche Abo zu packen (anstelle einer kleinen Einmalzahlung) ist für diese App der endgültige und wohl verdiente Todesstoß. Man tut gut daran, diese unseriösen Entwickler auch in Zukunft weiträumig zu meiden.

title: Beste TODO-App bislang
body:
Ich bin von der App gerade aufgrund ihrer Schlichtheit begeistert!

Trotzdem ist alles, was ich brauche, enthalten:

- Strukturierung in Ordner (Tipp dazu, s.u.)
- Terminfestlegung plus Erinnerungsfunktion
- eine weitere Ebene für auch abhakbare Unteraufgaben
- wichtige Aufgaben markieren
- sehr intuitive Bedienung

Endlich eine App, bei der ich wirklich alle (!) Funktionen nutze und nicht die Hälfte total unnötig ist, weil man sich um Kopf und Kragen verwaltet!! :-)

Gerne nutze ich auch die Funktion, die alle Tasks nacheinander anzeigt, damit man sie für heute, morgen oder später einplanen kann.
Dadurch, dass man immer nur eine Aufgabe sieht, hat man viel mehr Fokus und plant automatisch realistischer. :-)

Mein persönlicher Tipp:

Die Ordner habe ich nicht nach Projekten sortiert, sondern so, dass man sehen kann, was gerade in bestimmte Situationen passt, in denen man gerade Zeit hat:

Z.B.:
Geschäftszeiten, am PC, bei der Arbeit, zu Hause, persönlich, mit Person XY...

Und zwar funktionieren manche Einträge nach dem erstellen nicht mehr, die sind zwar aufgelistet und an die wird meiner Meinung nach auch erinnert aber man kann sie nicht antippen, um sie zu verschieben oder zu ändern. Er wählt einfach die Tätigkeit eine Zeile darüber oder dadrunter aus. Löschen kann man den fehlerhaften Eintrag leider auch nicht.

Groß und Kleinschreibung bei Ordner-Namen zulassen.

Ordner-Namen nehmen zu viel Platz weg. Schriftgröße bei Ordner-Namen verkleinern (Und dann vielleicht fett setzen).

Desktop-App für Mac OSX, dann wäre Any.do perfekt.

title: Großartig...
body:
Ein grafischer Hochgenuss. Sehr intuitiv in der Bedienung. Reduziert auf das wesentliche ohne dabei arm an Funktionen zu sein. Habe bereits Dutzende todo Apps über lange zeit auf ihre Tauglichkeit geprüft und finde, dass diese hier alles bietet, was ich brauche. Seit dem deutsch auch Aufgaben per Mikro diktiert werden können, gibts kaum noch Verbesserungsvorschläge. Wenn man einen Namen diktiert oder schreibt, à la "Otto anrufen" wird automatisch hinter dem Eintrag ein kleines call Icon sichtbar, über das man die Person direkt anrufen, oder eine Mail schreiben kann. Im landscape Modus erscheint links der todo liste ein Kalender mit allen Aufgaben, die sich dann auch auf ein bestimmtes Datum verschieben lassen. Außerdem werden alle kalendertermine, z.b. Geburtstage etc. Eingeblendet, ohne das diese als todo Ereignis vorher händisch eingetragen wurden. 

Hierzu noch ein Wunsch: dass man die Kalender auswählen kann, die angezeigt werden. Beispielsweise nur den privaten Kalender und nicht den geschäftlichen.

title: Super App
body:
Hab ja viele todo Apps ausprobiert, keins war so gut wie dieses hier. Die Bedienung ist anfangs zwar gewöhnungsbedürftig, wenn man sich allerdings ernsthaft damit beschäftigt und jeden Tag nutzt dann kommt man sehr schnell mit klar. 

Die UI ist klassisch minimalistisch. Sehr clean und ohne geschnörkel. Meiner Meinung nach sehr schön. 

Das einzige was ich zu bemängeln habe, ist dass es noch keine deutsche Version davon gibt und somit das Voice-Recording auch nur englisch versteht. Ich finde allerdings das das in der heutigen zeit nicht mehr das allzu größte Problem darstellen sollte. 
Deshalb kein "Punktabzug"!

5 Sterne - gebe ich mich allzu oft ;-)

title: Looks good on the outside...
body:
but there are some inconsistencies on the inside. 

1) Say it's Thursday and you have an appointment on Monday NEXT week, then in any.do the appointment is listed under 'This week'. It may be true that it is gonna be within the next seven days, but at least to me it's somewhat confusing. And it's not that hard to make the application intelligent enough to be able to know what week it is. 

2) The dictating feature should be optional. I never use it and it happens too often that I pull the interface down too long and thereby activate the voice feature. Shouldn't be too hard to make it an option. 

3) An iPad version. I love it how reminders automatically syncs my appointments between my iDevices, but I sorely miss that feature in any.do

Other than the above points, however, the application has a great touch and feel, not forgetting the awesome look.

title: Regret and a Trap – Not Worth the Buy
body:
Why:

1. Task-Sharing Limitations: If you buy a single user or two license, you can't share tasks not even your personal. To do so, you need to pay an extra $5/month for each additional user on each of the users. This wasn't clear at the outset, which feels like a trap.

2.Integration/migration Issues: They claim integration with apps like ToDoist, but it's not true. Migrating from ToDoist doesn't bring over comments or files, and they don't mention this anywhere. It's misleading.

3. Poor Support Experience: I bought two licenses to keep tasks private between users, but was surprised to learn you can't share tasks at all. I suggested many solutions, but the support team was unhelpful and dismissive, rejecting every solution.

4. Regret Dropping ToDoist: I switched from a more affordable, reliable service based on convincing but misleading reviews. I've wasted time and money on a service that doesn't deliver as promised.

title: ¿Por qué la expansión no es un pago único?
body:
Ciertamente es una buena app y la versión free bastante completa, pero no le veo el sentido a ofrecer una suscripción por añadirle características ¿se creen Netflix? Me parece un abuso, yo podría pagar hasta 20€ o 30€ por las otras características (que es mucho para los precios que se acostumbran en la app store) si solo lo pagara una vez.

Otra cosa que me pareció muy tramposa con la suscripción es que cuando instalé la app me salió un mensaje diciendo que me daban un descuento del 50% por la suscripción anual y que tenía 12 horas para decidirme con un contador regresivo. ¿Qué pasó cuando el contador llegó a cero? Que el precio por la suscripción anual se mantuvo IGUAL!!!.

title: Good idea, sloppy implementation
body:
The UI is clear, but it's implementation is not even beta quality; there are loads of placeholder texts everywhere, the app takes multiple seconds to respond, the syncing between the app and the desktop equivalent is inconsistent, and the less said about dictation and other "do what I mean" features, the better. And where is the iPad version?

The latest version also crippled the task-sorting feature by allowing only four "Any.do Moment"s per month. And to get more, you'd need to upgrade to the Premium version.

title: Devenu une appli pour perdre du temps
body:
Mise à jour de ce matin  GALERE DE CHEZ GALERE

Les reports de date sont devenus beaucoup trop compliqués. Bonjour la douche froide un lundi matin (c’est là que j’organise ma semaine). Au bout de 10 minutes, j’ai réussi à reporter quoi ? …. disons 10 tâches.  Il m’en reste un sacré paquet à revoir avec les vacances scolaires qui sont là, et mes priorités qui changent.

En fait, cette appli que j’utilisais depuis de nombreuses années est en train de devenir INUTILISABLE.

Son intérêt était de faire gagner du temps.

Depuis quelques mois déjà, je n’en gagnais plus. Mais il restait la « satisfaction » d’avoir une aide-mémoire avec tout ce que j’avais à faire.

Par contre le coup des reports amène carrément une perte de temps. Il faut tellement de clicks que ce n’est plus possible.

Bref c’est devenu l’APPLI POUR LES GENS PARFAITS. Les "Kens" de Ken et Barbie. Les « blonds » de Gad Elmaleh. Les gens qui n’ont pas besoin de reporter de tâches parcequ’ils sont tellement parfaits qu’ils ont réussi à faire tout ce qu’ils avaient prévu quand ils l'avaient prévu.

Pour moi qui ne suis pas parfaite, et qui pendant quelques années comptais sur cette appli pour m’aider à gérer ça. Et bien … c’est mort ! Je le sentais venir, avec tous ces magnifiques développements (là pour le coup, chapeau à l’équipe de développement, ils sont brillants, et visiblement plus nombreux qu'au début) ça devait finir par ne plus correspondre à mon besoin. D'ailleurs on sent la recherche d'un business modèle rentable. Avec l'ajout du partage en équipe et tout un tas d'autres choses dont je n'ai pas besoin, mais qui j’imagine permettrons de financer les équipes. 

J’avais juste besoin d’une TO DO Liste FACILE A UTILISER et RAPIDE. C’est tout !

Cette mise à jour me le rappelle cruellement :((

Bref, je pars à la recherche d’une autre solution. Si quelqu’un a une idée je suis preneuse !

title: Excellent with yet a few shortcomings
body:
Globally an excellent task manager, featuring :
-a very clear view,
-a great calendar/do-list combo
drag & drop the tasks
- sync with native Reminders & Calendar
-the signature "Moments" feature that allows you to reassign a task which has not been completed
- the "someday" part, which allows you to create a task without a concrete due line. 

Unfortunately for the moment Any.do still falls shorts of offering :
- above all, really convenient and TICKABLE SUBTASKS. That would be a major improvement. 
- a function allowing to hide some categories when showing "all tasks" (for instance the films to watch list or the grocery list), in order to focus on the main tasks & projects.
- a setting allowing a task without a specified date to fall automatically into the "someday" section : which would seem logical?..Instead, it unexpectedly falls on top of your today's do-list (!?)
- special lists for randomly recurring tasks, like groceries, for instance : allowing an item like "bananas" for example, once ticked, to remain "reactivatable" when there is a new lack of bananas! Without showing on the main tasks list, in order not to congest it with a myriad trivial items. This is again about good subtask functionalities.

Overall, a great app, great job.

body:

Jusqu'à la dernière  MAJ V2.0, Any.DO était ma préférence pour la gestion des choses à faire ou à remettre à plus tard. 
Très performante (avant la MAJ), et en même temps très simple.
Hélas la version 2.0 impose quasiment un compte payant cher (24€ à l'année), avec peu de plus par rapport à la version 1.19, performante même en restant en gratuit. 
Je conseille donc vivement de bloquer le "upgrade" vers v2.0 et/ou de revenir sur v1.19 depuis une sauvegarde.

Dernières nouvelles: je viens de la désinstaller et j'utilise Swipe, excellent, et Clear, un peu différent. 
Pas d'abonnement payant avec ces apps. (concept très prétentieux pour une petite App comme Any.Do)

A Vin_Vnz : 
si vous saviez combien j'ai déjà dépensé pour les programmes payants , vous seriez étonné d'apprendre que ça dépasse plusieurs centaines d'€!
Payer, oui, mais pas n'importe comment.

title: Très bien
body:
Pour en avoir testé beaucoup, c'est à mon sens l'une des meilleures pour une gestion du temps simplifiée.
Élégante, agréable à utiliser, avec de jolies idées comme l'outil pour préparer sa journée ou l'intégration géniale à gmail via le module Chrome.  
Quelques aberrations quand même, comme l'impossibilité de supprimer ou renommer le dossier par défaut, pourtant signalée depuis plusieurs mois et sans nouvelle.
Pour une gestion plus détaillée (et pas uniquement basée sur l'urgence), ma préférence ira à 2do qui est plus complète et totalement paramétrable pour s'adapter avec la méthode de chacun. Mais c'est plus cher et plus lourd a utiliser. Donc si votre besoin est simple ou que vous n'avez pas une idée très très précise de ce que vous cherchez, foncez sur celle-là !

title: Indispensable malgré qq lacunes
body:
Dans l'absolu, c'est l'appli indispensable pour gérer ses RV, ses tâches, ses listes à faire au quotidien et avoir une vision globale de ce qu'on a à faire dans le futur proche ou lointain. Le problème c'est l'instabilité des notes dont la date d'action se modifie (toute seule... C'est gênant !)
Le classement est intelligent et pratique 
-aujourd'hui 
-demain
-à venir
-un jour
Mais la date de rappel ne se maintient pas toujours et l'on est obligé de revérifier régulièrement la hiérarchisation de ses notes pour ne pas oublier une tâche à venir.
La synchronisation avec l'appli "cal" fonctionne bien.
Malgré ces défauts qui seraient à corriger par les développeurs (svp, merci) appli indispensable dans mon quotidien

title: La meilleure dans son domaine selon moi
body:
L'application est vraiment complète et gratuit en plus de ça. Il me tarde de tester « Any.Do Cal ».

Dommage que ça bug en mode portrait sur l'iOS 7 (bêta). Et sinon je sais pas si c'est moi qui n'ai pas trouvé ou si c'est une fonction manquante à l'application mais comment on fait pour effacer une tâche qu'on ne se souhaite plus accomplir? Pouvoir renommer les dossiers ne serait pas de trop bon plus. Faudra penser à changer la façon dont on accède au réglage car avec le centre de contrôle de l'iOS 7 c'est pas très pratique.

Voilà je pense avoir tout dit, je prie pour une version iPad et Mac ! Bonne continuation à l'équipe, vous m'avez fait supprimer l'application « Clear » de mon téléphone.

title: Pas encore optimisée
body:
La nouvelle interface est sympa, faut juste s'y habituer. 
Ce qui me gêne dans cette bonne application de to do, c'est un bug que je croise encore sur cette nouvelle version : mes tâches programmées 1 à 2 semaines d'avance ont tendance à changer de date toute seule! Bref, pas pratique pour ceux qui se veulent organisés! De plus, les pastilles sur l'icône ne se mette pas à jour toutes seules, seulement après avoir lancé l'appli. 
Enfin, je croise quelques ralentissements sur mon iPhone 4.

Perso, je retourne sur Droplist : plus simple plus légère, et encore plus pratique pour reporter ses tâches...

title: Un must !
body:
Pour tout les adeptes des todo listes, c est le top !
J ai essayé un grand nombre d'appli plus ou moins complexes, mais celle-ci est simple et efficace !
J adore : le style épuré, la création de tâches à la volée par reconnaissance vocale et surtout any moment ! Cela permet de faire des revues hebdo (avis aux GTDistes).
Et la synchro auto avec l'appli Google.
Les moins : la derniere mise à jour avec une police moins stylée.
Enfin c'est la seule appli que je connaisse qui permet de trier par contexte ou échéances en 1 clic.
Le tout gratuit, que demander de plus!
Un grand merci aux développeurs !

title: Free Trial Trap
body:
I was attracted to this app by a slick instagram advert.

The free trial of premium is required to access any of the really cool features like the WhatsApp integration. 

I couldn’t get WhatsApp to work with it so decided to cancel bu here’s the thing .... you can’t!

Well not from in the app or from their online account.

You need to go into iCloud and do it from the subscriptions.

In a world of clear and easy to navigate flexible app prices, any.do stands out as a bunch of crooks with fancy ads that don’t actually deliver on the promise then lock you down for a full 12months subscription which doesn’t appear to be refundable. 

I told everyone about this app when I downloaded it, for the WhatsApp thing. I thought it was a great idea and I’ve been using an alternate todo app for about 10 years - I’m very loyal to that app, it’s got a month contract cancel any time. 

I was prepared to migrate. But now I’ll tell anyone I can to avoid this app unless you absolutely are sure that you want it.

title: Very Good But Needs Some Tweaks
body:
I primarily subscribed to this app as I wanted an ‘All in one’ Calendar/To-do List app which included Location Based Reminders, and there are very few out there which do. 

This app does have a load of great features and on the whole it is very well thought out, but is has some frustrating little niggles for me, for example there is no search function in the calendar, only in the tasks screen. When you add sub-tasks to a main task, the newest one added appears on top where I think the oldest on top would be more logical as you would normally work down a list clearing your oldest tasks first. Another option here would be to make them movable but at present you can’t do that either. 

The main problem for me though is the design of the Location Based Reminders. It is straightforward to use but it is the only version I’ve seen where you don’t have an adjustable Geofencing option to allow you to trigger the reminder a set number of meters (or more) from your destination. Instead you have to input a postcode or address and this can cause problems if you wanted alerted in a certain area but you may not have the actual address or postcode (for shopping reminders while approaching shops for example). Also GPS positioning is not always 100% accurate, so sometimes the alert does not trigger. It is also not possible to drag or reposition the pin on the map either, so it can be VERY limiting. 

For most users though, it will probably be fine but I subscribed to the pro version specifically for the features which still need perfecting.

title: Close, but no cigar...
body:
I've been using Any.do for as long as I can remember now and enjoy its combination of simplicity and effectiveness. 

Recent releases have brought with them a glitch that duplicates entries temporarily when you drag to reorder them, sometimes even changing the order of items around them which is beyond frustrating and pushing me very close to finding an alternative app. The ability to prioritise and reorder lists is paramount but Any.do isn't delivering the goods recently. Please fix this ASAP as the app is near perfect otherwise. Submitting feedback through your non-responsively design website also seems impossible which is why I've regrettably had to report this glitch here.

I'm hoping to award five stars for the next release, but in the meantime I'll try my best to persevere with this version.

UPDATE: Still abysmally buggy, often crashes, takes far too long to load, takes up a lot of space and often needs restarting when you can't drag items to re-order them. It also sets all items to one week in the future as default rather than the day you're currently on, which is a little inconvenient. Such a shame as this app used to be great and has so much potential!

title: New release entirely broken; giving up
body:
For those who have been using Any.do to keep track of their to-do lists on their own device without setting up an account, relying on constant access to "the cloud", trusting your data to third parties in unknown jurisdictions, etc. - do not install this update!!

Previously it was possible to bypass the sign-in step by selecting an item from the Any.do widget, which would then bring up the app.  A nuisance, but workable.

Now, however, the geniuses behind this thing have noticed this useful workaround, and have disabled it.

As a result, I have just lost access to my lists.  Well done, Any.do.  You win: I will stop trying to help you to improve the app, and will instead delete it permanently.

title: So far, so very, very good.
body: I've tried quite a few "to do" apps and most seem either far too complicated for their own good or far, far too basic - so much so that they're no better than Apple's Notes app. So finding Any.DO has been a revelation ... so far. The simplicity means adding tasks is a breeze, and the options for each task are, it seems, just about spot on. I love the "Moments" add-on - but it is a bit annoying to have to pay for this and some of the fairly basic functions, like customising your "repeat" notifications. My feedback would be to offer a limited-period trial after which a reasonable app fee is charged to continue - like £2.99. I do think £40 a year is a ridiculous amount for a "to do" app - no matter how good it is! I know you offer half-price discounts as an incentive, but still ... too much money for a year's sign-up in my opinion. For that reason I give it four stars - otherwise it would be a nailed-on five.

- It would be great if we could launch the "moment" from Notification Center as well
- Add new task from Notification Center doesn't work .. It just takes me to the app where I have to add a new task

title: Getting Things Done, right
body:
I'm pretty obsessive when it comes to GTD apps and rely on an easy to use powerful system throughout my daily work.
I have purchased and used the most popular apps on apples eco system, some better than others, but I am always on the look-out for the best system for 'me'.
This is my new go-to system all rolled into one neat package. 
Someone has sat down and put a lot of thought into this app from simplicity of the UI they have understood that someone needing to track tasks must have a straightforward intuitive way to do so. From the speak to create a task all the way through to the dragging and tilting functionality, it has all been thought through.
5* for engineering a human friendly software tool that I will use daily. I'd easily pay for this and any other versions the developer can create for Apples other devices. Great work. 
Download now if you continue to imagine that 'things' and 'omnifocus' etc are the best things for your daily work lists

title: Best Tasks App On The Market
body:
I've been putting off writing a review for nearly 4 months. Now with a lot of experience (over half a year) with Any.Do, and probably another 1-2 months trying other task apps,Any.Do is by far the best.

It's simple and minimalist yet beautiful and practical design makes remembering things easier than ever.  I'm not a busy person (13years old) so I don't have many deadlines to make, just things to do.  I'm also very disorganised, and Any.Do has helped me  organise myself too.

I think the reason it's the best is because it does what it says it does, does what it should do and always does what you want it to do, no more, no less. It's simply beautiful.

I hope you choose Any.Do
Make the most of it

Matthew (Aged 13)

title: Excellent and intuitive
body:
Clean, minimalist layout with only the info you need, coupled with a rather excellent predictive / automatic feature that learns (for example, you enter "Email Bob" and the app automatically checks your contacts and then places a link directly on that to-do item that opens Mail with Bob's address filled in).

Tried many other task management / to do list apps, and always return to this.

EDIT FOR UPDATE: As you can see above, I was a huge fan of the layout prior to the update but I'm actually really loving the new design changes. Not an improvement as such, as the previous design was lovely, but certainly on par, just different and perhaps more cohesive throughout the app now.

With regards to the app itself, everything above still stands. An absolute bargain, particularly considering the price of some if the similar apps, and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.

UPDATE: With the recent release, and along with it the addition of the scheduled 'organise your todos' this already fantastic app just got even better!

In response to the complaint that you can't disable the speech feature, you can by simply not choosing that way to input and typing instead. No extra measures needed, just tap the empty text field rather than the microphone specifically.

title: So, so good. Where have you been all my life?
body:
I've tried many, many productivity apps and to do lists in the past. The more minimal ones feel better to me but I'm always frustrated by the lack of features. The big boys (Things, Omnifocus, etc.) give much more flexibility but also feel clumsy and bloated. Like organising my productivity is a huge task in itself. And I always end up ignoring the majority of the features and just using a Today list and scheduled events. 

Any.DO gives me exactly the features I need and nothing else. I can see what I've got to do today and peek at what's coming up tomorrow. Items drop into my list when they need to. They're not nagging me from a distance.  

And it's beautiful. Really clean and well thought out. This isn't style over substance. This is proper UX design. Clever, clever touches at every turn. Smart auto completion of tasks, voice input, quick capture. Swiping tasks to mark as complete is lovely but even better is the little shake gesture to clear your completed items and get back to a focussed list of what's still to do. This is the first app I've seen use the shake gesture in a way that feels satisfying and not stupid. 

I keep noticing features. The companion Chrome Extension is excellent and the Gmail integration is pure genius (automatic task recognition and suggestion from your emails). 

The only thing I don't like about this app is the price. Take my money. I'd rather pay £40 for this app and the devs make a living from it than have it for free and wonder how long it'll be before the staff are acqui-hired and the app is 'sunsetted'. TAKE MY MONEY!

title: You don't know good till you've tried this
body:
I was happy with wunderlist that is till wunderlist 2 and the multiple problems signing in, syncing or even viewing my data offline. As a result I looked for an alternative and any.do was worth a shot

It's actually vastly superior to any other to so app. It has location reminders. Short drag downwards adds task. Longer drag adds a voice recognition task. Swipe left to cancel. Tasks autocomplete to most common choices. Plus categorises tasks based on priority so you are never overwhelmed with tasks far into the future until its time to address then

Plus the recent addition of any.moments is an unintrusive way to reprioritise your tasks dynamically day to day like mailbox app does with email. This app has no close competitor as a result and is accessible on pc via a chrome extension. Hopefully we'll see a web version soonish. 

Absolutely no sync or load issues so far I can thoroughly give this the highest approval. Any.do is the best because it isn't willing to rest on its strengths. I hope it continues its rise

author: QasimRehman

title: Absolutely stunning
body:
With what I can only describe as a 'stunning' UI, Any.DO has become one of, if not probably the most, used apps on my phone. This app has helped organise my life, and it feels like I haven't done a thing.

The interface is gorgeous, working well with the Apple ethos of simplicity. All my tasks are separated between Today, Tomorrow, Upcoming and Someday, and are added with the tap of a button. If I'm walking and remember something I can easily tap the microphone button and use dictation to add my task. The tasks can be further filtered through work and personal tasks or highlighted in red to show important tasks in the list.

The use of a downward swipe to add a new task is so intuitive I find myself doing it absolutely automatically. It just works. Another gesture, the side swipe, is used to cross off a task. This couples well with a shake to get rid of all the completed tasks, which are put into a very accessible folder. It does arouse a sense of pride when a banner appears along the bottom of the screen to show you've completed 20 tasks. This is also shareable with FaceBook, to show off your efficiency. 

The app integrates with contacts too, and simply by adding a name after a command, e.g., "Text Sarah" an icon will appear beside the reminder that lets you jump straight to your messages, with Sarah already selected. Again: it just works.

The app helpfully displays the number of today's tasks in a red notification bubble. Any.DO is nestled neatly on my iPhone dock so I can always see how many thing I wanted to get done today.

All in all this app is a MUST BUY. It's too good not to get, and I urge you to download it as soon as possible.

title: Brilliant
body:
I have tried a few apps that claim they make your life easier but they some how fall short. This one delivers on it's promises and whole lot more. Browser addition is perfect, it's where most of my reminders are set from. The folders are a clever way to organise your todos, but the true beauty is the ease you can switch from folder priority to date priority (and vice versa).

The google tasks tie up is cool, and the contacts connection is pure class. But, Location based todos are icing on the cake. 

 Apps like this should be judged on how easy it is to input data; they don't get much easier than this one (and I haven't even mentioned voice input that it has) 

 The program is slick, intuitive and very fast. Its where I need it to be, when I need it to be and telling me what I need to know.

title: Almost complete task ecosystem
body:
This app gets a lot of plaudits based on its looks, but equally important are the additional touches and functionality that others lack. 

For Gmail/Chrome users, installing the extension gets you access to your tasks and adds an excellent option to received emails so you can add a task immediately if something needs followed up at a later date.

Only reason this isn't 5 star is lack of repeating tasks, and no way to set a default alarm time (new tasks are set to the time they are being added rather than, say, tomorrow at 9am as a starting point).

author: ursul_polar

body:
Best interface I've ever seen for a to do app. I've had an iPhone for 2 years and despite having installed the 'best' to do apps, I've never found myself coming back to use one until now.

Any.DO has a wealth of features considering it's free!

- Clear user interface
- Responsive actions
- Recognises things: type 'Go to' and a list of common sentences appear such as 'to bank', 'to town' etc. Also the names of contacts: 'Text Ni..' and below comes up with 'Text Nicola Cousin'. When the app reminds you to do it, you can call / email / text from a command within the app which takes you to the relevant screen.
- Voice recognition. Not as amazing as Siri but once you know what it does understand, it's easy.
- Can add subcategories to your tasks via a 'notes' function
- View by Date order or Folder (category) order.

These are just some of the things that I love about this app and which has stood out to me, making me want to actually have things to organise!

Would like the ability to drag to reposition to the order of my folders though. That's the only discrepancy I can think of so far. Good app!!!

title: I don't usually write reviews... But...
body:
Simply put, this is an excellent programme. Nice looking interface. Easy to use and way better than the native reminders on the iPhone. The only criticism would be that it's difficult to read the Notes section (which scrolls)... Why not leave this as a text block as that's far easier and quicker to read? 

  Also, perhaps a couple of levels of priority would be nice. I.e. instead of just making the text red to indicate priority tasks (which works fine) another colour could indicate, say, Priority 2 tasks. Even better would be Numbered tasks....so that when tasks are moved about they have a "1." to "x." to the left as an ordered list.

  These are NOT criticisms though... The developers have done a really nice job.

title: A Lifesaver for the Organised Mind
body:
As someone who thrives on organization and efficiency, I've found Any.do to be an indispensable tool in my daily life. The app's intuitive design and user-friendly interface make task management not just manageable, but actually enjoyable.

Synchronisation Across Devices: One of the standout features of Any.do is its seamless synchronization across all devices. Whether I'm on my phone, tablet, or computer, I can access my tasks and schedules in real-time, ensuring I never miss a beat.

Task Management:The app's task management system is top-notch, with the ability to categorize tasks, set reminders, and even delegate to others. It's like having a personal assistant in your pocket.

Calendar Integration: The integration with the calendar is a game-changer. Being able to view my tasks and appointments in one place helps me plan my day with precision and prevents any scheduling conflicts.

Voice Entry and Widgets:The voice entry feature and the widgets for quick access to my to-do list are incredibly convenient, especially when I'm on the go and need to capture a task quickly.

In conclusion, Any.do has significantly improved my productivity and has helped me stay on top of my busy schedule. It's more than just an app; it's a productivity companion that I highly recommend to anyone looking to streamline their life.

---

I hope this review captures the essence of what makes Any.do a valuable app for many users. If you need any further assistance or another type of content, feel free to ask!

title: Using it for 4 years on and off
body:
I’ve been using Any.do literally from the day it was launched. Honestly, used it on and off. I would always come back to it because of its way of presenting tasks and the innovative and authoritative tasks UI in the GTD approach. 

I always stop using it after a while, ironically, because it has the calendar feature and it does a damn poor job of it. Initially juggling calendar and tasks was hard when any.do lacked this feature. But when it added, I quickly realised how disparate and unimaginative the integration / UI is. Please make the calendar UI “cleaner”.

Lastly, one personal request: kindly use more of the screen real estate by using swiping gestures and hiding the crap tonne of buttons and menus you have always in every screen. I know that it’s one click. But, there are many ways to do one click access to text input and actions without feeling like components have been “slapped” on. 

Someone desperately needs to look at and regain the core strength of any.do - unifying great design with deep understanding of workflow UX.

title: Nice, but could be better
body:
Ok, so the “Plan my day” option is perhaps the best feature of this app that I haven’t seen in any other productivity app. Not even on Evernote. I generally get drained looking at all the tasks I couldn’t complete vs all those I did, and this feature makes that guilt go away with a very simple reschedule that requires minimal effort. This feature is simply too cool. It’s the only reason I subscribed. It even allows syncing with apple reminders which is rather useful.

Now for the cons. The calendar view is annoying as a slight scroll takes me many days ahead or behind. I wish it segregated events and tasks so I could view all my events for the day in one shot rather than scrolling. Also, all my apple reminders gets clubbed in one category here which I honestly find a bit annoying since the colour codes of my lists get lost. I prefer apple reminders as I can add photos to tasks, but this app does not have that feature. (Although it does allow adding notes, subtasks and color coded labels.) For so many missing features, not sure if a subscription fee that is more expensive than an Apple Music subscription is worth it. 

If the developers can look into enhancing the app’s features, I certainly don’t mind spending.

Update for developers as on 2 Mar 2020: Thanks for your quick response! I have updated my rating accordingly. My request was actually for segregating the calendar and tasks in the daily view so I can see all events at one go and then all tasks, without having to scroll. The widget offers me this so it’s a workaround, but would be nice if the app did. And happy to know I can add photos. But I meant adding it to a task directly via the photo itself. Or even add a weblink via the browser. That feature would be so awesome.

title: I love anydo
body:
Love the app. Specially for all the pats and wows that I get after completing my tasks. Love the motivation. Love the usability details. 

I'd love to suggest a feature-create categories for tasks. For example, work tasks, grocery shopping tasks, billing and banking tasks, cleaning tasks, etc. Each tasks done can have unique voices & badges- for example if I finish my work tasks, a boss-like voice can be added & maybe I get a badge of superhero@work. If there's too much of work tasks & I'm finishing only that, maybe I get a reminder of work-life balance & asks me to stop turning into a workaholic. maybe any.do sends me a reminder of granmums birthday if I've listed it :) I can go on! But for now, love Any.do!

2) Suggestion: Swipe from right to left could bring out options to postone the task to tomorrow - next week - upcoming - someday
3) the chrome extension should also have a view similar to the one we get on landscape mode of the phone 

Thank you for implementing repeat option for the tasks.

title: Non all’altezza delle aspettative.
body:
Sono settimane che cerco una to-do-list app per organizzarmi le attività, che possa sincronizzarsi con Alexa e condividere la lista della spesa in famiglia.
Trovo sul web il sito di Any.do e mi innamoro subito. Ha tutto quello che serve e sembra perfetta per le mie esigenze.
Quando scarico l’app avvio immediatamente l’abbonamento annuale perché sono sicuro che la mia ricerca sia finita.
Invece iniziano una serie di aspetti che lentamente mi porteranno a cancellare l’abbonamento e abbandonare l’app.

1. La grafica: ha un ottimo potenziale, ma ha dei dettagli che stonano e non hanno coerenza con l’app. Scritte e titoli più grossi o in stampatello, menu a tendina tagliati perché la scritta non riesce a starci o comparsa di ombreggiature indesiderate quando si trascina verso il basso la pagina (come per ricaricare). 
Segnalo anche dei piccoli lag durante lo scroll di alcune pagine, tipo quella del calendario, che non incentiva il suo utilizzo (possiedo un iPhoneX iOS13).

2. La lingua: ovviamente nel mio caso Italiana, ma non traduce correttamente tutti i sottomenu o alcune parti (come la spesa intelligente).

3. Alexa: uno dei motivi base per cui avevo scaricato l’app era proprio poter sincronizzare la lista della spesa e condividerla in famiglia. Quando vado per installare la skill su Alexa compare un errore che mi avverte che la skill non esiste più.

L’esperienza di utilizzo non mi ha convinto nemmeno fosse stata gratuita, figuriamoci per quasi 7€ al mese.

Mi dispiace perché magari su altri dispositivi le cose funzionano meglio, però su iPhone, dove lavoro la maggior parte del mio tempo, non è stato così.
