title: Ideale per non incasinarsi la vita
body:
Programma molto valido SENZA PUBBLICITÀ (che è sempre molestissima) per organizzarsi le giornate.
Già che non abbia odiosi banner pubblicitari la mette in testa rispetto alle altre, ma entrando nel merito, l’ho preferita alle altre “to do list” perché si interfaccia con Calendario di iOS, si possono inserire gli impegni con comando vocale (altra cosa comodissima, così se viene in mente una cosa basta dirla), la schermata delle attività è suddivisa in “oggi - domani - a breve - in futuro”, che ricorda vagamente il Pomodoro (metodo che mi ha spinto a cercare app come questa) e c’è una funzione comodissima nella sua semplicità (Any.do Moment) che si può far partire sempre a una certa ora, e che in pratica ti sottopone tutti gli impegni che hai (compresi quelli lasciati lì) e ti domanda quando vuoi eseguirli, con icone semplici tipo “oggi”, “domani” e UN solo sottomenu che ti domanda a che ora, potendo scegliere tra poche possibilità “tattiche”, ma permettendo anche di specificare un certo orario personalizzato, come una sorta di segretaria. 
EDIT: questa funzione è a pagamento, purtroppo. 

EDIT #2: come risposto qui sotto dallo sviluppatore, la funzione “Moment”, cioè la segretaria virtuale, può essere usata fino a 5 volte al mese nella versione gratuita ( ammetto che mi piacerebbe averla illimitata nella versione free 😄😅)

Si possono creare categorie di impegni (tipo “lavoro”, “hobby” ecc) e si possono vedere le attività nella stessa schermata del calendario (dove si vedono anche i “progetti”, cioè la roba di iOS Calendario).
Chiaramente la app manda notifiche per ricordare la roba da fare. 
Per me è veramente un bel programma, è il primo che trovo in grado di essermi utile. 
Se integrassero pure un orologio Pomodoro con il solito sistema del 25+5 che si interfacci con la lista di cose da fare, e magari un’interazione con “promemoria” di iOS sarebbe proprio top.
EDIT: andando nelle impostazioni, si può attivare l’integrazione tra Siri+Promemoria e la lista delle attività, dunque una delle mie due richieste è già stata esaudita.

Ad ogni modo merita 5 stelle già così

title: Bella esteticamente, ma da migliorare
body:
L'app ha uno stile minimalista molto bello, sicuramente più stilosa di tante altre applicazioni della stessa categoria. 

Però può sicuramente migliorare ancora tanto nelle funzionalità. Due esempi che mi hanno lasciato alquanto perplesso:

1) si possono aggiungere sub-attività, ma non si può selezionarle come eseguite. Rimangono quindi perennemente nella lista, che, se lunga, diventa poco leggibile. 

2) se si vuole modificare le attività o le su attività si va incontro a numerosi bug, alcuni dei quali rendono invisibile capire cosa si sta modificano. 

Quindi: app con grande potenziale, ma finché non vengono risolte queste fastidiose banalità non consiglierei di pagare per l'abbonamento

title: No Chat GPT Plugin 😡
body:
Guys, I know you have a GPT but it’s 2026 already, even Todoist has one. 

After Chat GPT Work came out the game has changed.

Are you even in the productivity space? Get with the program. 

I am sorry I am venting here but it’s because your product is so good that I am frustrated you are missing the AI train. 

I love that Any.do connects to Hermes via OAuth , but I need a Chat GPT plugin.

I love that Any.Do connects to my old apple watch, my old Samsung tab, my Windows 10 computer, my old MacBook Air, ny iPads.

I love the daily reviews. 

But my strategy is done with Chat GPT chat due to context continuity.

In a nutshell, get the Chat GPT plugin and I will give you 5 stars.

Leverage Chat GPT.

title: Excelente Aplicación
body:
Tomando en cuenta de que ya muchos han hablado acerca de lo buena, sencilla, practica y elegante de esta aplicación, me centrare en otros aspectos.

No requieres crear una cuenta, sin embargo si la creas puedes delegar actividades a otras personas, muy útil cuando trabajas en equipo. Además, tiene dos extensiones geniales, una para Chrome y otra para Gmail, con la primera puedes trabajar en tu PC y con la segunda puedes convertir un correo en una tarea, y todo esto se sincroniza.

Me gustaría que pudiera agrupar y categorizar las tareas, además de robustecer el aspecto de la delegación para que uno pueda tener seguimiento y retroalimentación una vez que dichas tareas han sido realizadas o modificadas.

title: Huge potential, extremely poor execution
body: I downloaded this app specifically for the integration of my Apple reminders & calendar. It looked promising but it does not work at all. If I add subtasks to my reminders (in Apple reminders), all these subtasks end up underneath the “someday” tab and the original reminder does not have subtasks at all??? Also when I create a reminder, and edit it (e.g. time, again in the Apple reminders app), the edit does not show in any.do and also if I switch back to Apple my edits are gone ??? It also shows everything as “Apple reminder”, instead of the different lists/categories I use in that app. I wanted to use this app to bring my calendar and reminders together, not having to use any.do for all input. Too bad that they used “integration” as a marketing ploy and fail in actually integration.

body:

Het werkt mooi dat je in combinatie met de agenda ook je taken daar in ziet staan en andersom, dat je je agendapunten bij je taken ziet staan. Enige nadeel was dat de volgorde van installeren uitmaakte. Ik moest eerst de to do installeren en daarna kon ik de cal installeren, andersom kon ik de apps niet met elkaar synchroniseren. title: Best To Do list app I've used
body:
It's safe to say that I am not the most organized person in the world. 

Next to that simple fact, I'm a freelancer, I'm forgetful and I don't have the time or patience to learn a system to keep me in check.

I've tried TeuxDeux; not enough features to actively remind me of things. I've tried Wunderlist; too complicated at first glance to dive right in. 

Sceptical as I was, this app actually fulfills my needs. It can be as simple as a list, you can add the functionality of reminders and dates and if you want even more, you can start organizing your tasks. Low learning curve, but good functionality when you want it!

Also; smooth user interface and superclean design. For all the ADD'ers, freelancers and creatives: get it. You won't be disappointed

title: All is well … until all is lost
body:
Any.do is certainly a great concept, easy to use, flexible, and decent to look at, and it works great most of the time. I struggle, however, with its reliablity in the long run.

I've had this app now for maybe a year and a half. Today is the third time it has simply deleted all my todos without any form of warning. When I open the app it gives me the welcome splash screen as if it's the first time, and although I sign in with the same account as before, all the missing items are still gone. This tends to happen at the worst possible moments, on average about every six months. Last time was my 2015 Christmas preparation plans, this time I'm planning a vacation and a wedding party. All gone.

The FAQ says "Sometimes the syncing process cannot complete and your tasks do not fully load. Please log out and back into the app on all platforms - this will retrieve the most current information that is on our server."

Following this advice, I managed to recall a single entry from over a year ago, which I had long deleted from the list after completion, but none of the recent ones were there.

I strongly feel that I can't trust Any.do, and that I've given it more that a fair dose of patience and second chances, so I'm kicking it out. Adieu.

title: Really the best
body:
Ok - so I have tried literally about 10 to do list apps over the past year n this is by far the best n the reason why I like it is bec...
1) automatically rolls over days tasks to next day
2) function allowing u to review days lust. And inside this you can put tasks off to a chosen other day
3) automatically slots them in order by time on the list when you creat them 
4) instant touch change between date format n task format ( so for example if I'm sitting down c time to do emails, I can look at the list of emails I need to write, but then switch back instantly to my various mixed tasks for the day)
6) easy of categorizing task types call, email, to-do, when downtown...what ever I create.
7) reminders have a pleasant tone n can be set either according to location ( n either when coming or when going) or exact time.
8) can easily "pick up" a task n move it around to diff time slots
Ok - so kinda long review! I was using Next Thing before this, only better feature with that was u can click on an exact day in the future on the main tabs list n see set tasks, with this one, everything beyond tomorrow is all stacked out in one list pretty much. But otherwise it's the best by a mile. This n Mail Box for organizing emails, have actually changed my life just a little bit. More relaxed. I live a SUPER busy professional life working around the world n with family. With this app I can set a task n relax, knowing it will come back to me when I need.

title: Nice little app
body:
Nice app. Sleek design. Couple of things could do to improve it further:
- have a mac version as well that syncs and you can use on your desktop
- appointments for "today" and "tomorrow" need to automatically move back one day after you've entered them. Ie if I enter a to do for "tomorrow", 24hrs later it should appear on my "today" list. It doesn't. You have to move manually which is annoying. "Next week" should also move automatically, "later" could stay static. 
- the "mail" option doesn't always automatically appear when the task has the word "email" in it. You should have the same function for when the task says "call". Eg "call" should show a phone and link directly to calls. "Email" should show an email. "Book" could show both phone and email. "Pick up" should show a link to maps. 
- vocal input could be improved, but I like the concept. 

Look forward to the next series of updates/iterations - great base to start from!

title: Thumbs up for Any.do moment, which is absolutely ingenious
body:
I procrastinate A LOT, so the Any.do Moment really helps pressure me to finish my tasks. I'm a big fan of the minimalist aesthetic as well, because it helps me focus without causing the anxiety that comes with bold colors and busy text.

My only complaint is that it takes a long time to start up. Also, there should be an option/button/whatever to easily delete repeating tasks when they are no longer needed. Right now, I have to tap the task, tap the reminders button, remove the reminders, and swipe right to delete the reminder.
author: KN0W1T4LL

title: Ease and Simplicity
body:
I've tried other big name productivity apps (to-do lists) on the AppStore and it's Any.Do which really cuts it for me. Mainly in part due to its simplicity in classifying tasks according to 'Today', 'Tomorrow', Upcoming', and 'Someday', it helps keep you focused on successfully accomplishing the few most important things of the day - although at the expense of making big lists. 

My only concern is that the animation for drag-dropping (arranging) the tasks to other lists is kinda clunky as compared to a standard drag and drop with Apple's Reminders app (when using the Edit function).

Very clean, minimalist, and a delight to use! Points of improvement though:

- An option could be created to make tasks whole-day instead of having to be assigned to a specific time all the time. Not all to-do's can be pinned to a certain time of day. 
- Although if tasks in a day are time-specific, maybe make them arranged chronologically in that day from top (earliest) to bottom (latest), unless they have been marked as a priority task. 
- A more interactive tutorial, or maybe a link to a video, could help make the learning curve less steep for first-time users!

I hope you consider these suggestions! Thank you for the wonderful app. :)

Issue 2: there is no way to schedule tasks, so for daily tasks such as "exercise", i have to enter each task daily.

The two issues above are inconvenient enough to make me want to stop using the app, regardless of how wonderful everything else is. Please fix!

title: Beware of auto renewal
body: I did not realize my premium account was active or would be auto renewed when I stopped using the app, which I found not useful. My account was auto renewed annually for 3 years without any notification to me via email or otherwise, and I only realized it when my credit card expired and an email was then sent about the failed renewal. Any.do refused to make any exceptions to give me a refund, citing their policies, without takingy circumstances into account. Beware of their rigid auto renewal policies that rely on your vigilance to ensure you are not charged unnecessarily.

title: Adds to the clutter
body: Nice idea but just added to the clutter of my day or didnt make me more efficient organising or at getting stuff done. So I road tested the app for a few weeks and then deleted it and totally forgot about it until, what do you know, the annual auto renew kicked in with no warning email or reminder message (so much for their claims to increase efficiency) that the app was about to renew. As soon as I saw the charge I asked for a refund and was told the company has no obligation to tell consumers about the renewal and that I should have read the terms and conditions! I wouldn’t deal with any.do again in this basis. “The best way to organise your life” .... really? My experience, to me, proves this app is anything but. And it will cost u money to learn that.

title: Would appreciate to have daily task saved
body: Hi! I enjoyed using this app as a housewife to organise my daily tasks and had subscribe for a year. However, I have one simple request if you could update it and have the option to get the daily done task be saved instead of deleted each day so I could refer on other days if that task had been completed days before. It would be great if I could just flip back the calendar to check if I have done and completed it to prevent me wondering if that task had already been done in advance for the week. Also, it would be great to have the option when I complete the task, it shows the time I completed it instead of the time that is due to be done only.

The app take at least 3 seconds to orientate when I change orientation... Reorganizing lists of things is slow... Even checking a thing of the list is slow...

A to-do app is meant to record the user's to-do list quickly and efficiently. What's the use of a to-do app that has lots of extra features but doesn't do its basic functionality...? 

I love this app. And I hope the developers will clean it up a little in the next update and fix all its bugs.

title: Simple n Gd but need improvements
body:

Overall good work and hope to see new things soon :)

title: Allows adding and checking off via Chrome browser
body:
I have been using Any.do for a couple of months now and I find Any.do fits my needs perfectly. 

Before trying Any.do I was using Clear and Steps (both paid apps) for a time. Both Clear and Steps were highly anticipated and praised apps but I found that Clear was a little too simple for me. Whereas, Steps was better (it snyc with Google Tasks) but somehow the UI didn't really appeal to me. 

And that's where Any.do comes in. It looks great. UI is simple and clean. As the same time it allows me to enter as much text as I want to for each item. It allows me to add notes, set an alarm and it allows me to set my own folders. But best of all, I can install the Any.do on my Chrome browser and add or check off completed tasks straight from my browser. How cool is that?

Try Any.do, it's free. What do you have to lose?

title: Decent
body:
It’s a decent app. But the visual craft and layout of everything just feels ancient, like it hasn’t been looked at by a designer in 10 years. 

The developer response is telling: defensive and clueless. If they cared about minimalism, they wouldn’t have ugly gradients from 2006, poor item spacing across the entire app, poorly chosen and inconsistent icons, and ugly backgrounds with no option of customizing them. If they knew anything about real design, they wouldn’t say “design is subjective”. It looks like it was designed by a second semester design intern. 

I don’t have the energy to do a full design crit of the app in an app store review. But this silly developer response was enough for me to stop using the app. They clearly are just coasting at this point and have no desire to make the app better anymore.

title: ALMOST Perfect
body: On the website, you’re able to change the background, but on the app you cannot. Wish you could change the background on the app too! Otherwise, this is a great app for students and office workers who just need an app that they can jot down notes and to-do’s! I personally enjoy using the desktop website more than the iOS app (at least on iPad), as it is more streamlined and easier to see, plus it’s more aesthetically pleasing on the website due to the aforementioned background problem. Finally, I wish there was an optional “widget” within the app that functioned like a sticky note on the wall. I.e jot down a reminder that you want to keep on the screen at all times; I do want to reiterate that this feature should be removable and optional to have, as not everyone would want it. However, the app is good as is, and I will be using this for my senior year!

AND…. That the Kanban functionality, even if I DO upgrade, is only available via the Webb… And not the Mac, iPhone or iPad apps.😢

This app has some amazing functionality and beautiful design… but without universal access to Kennan boards…It’s a fail for me. I’m sure other people love it, but I can’t believe that this isn’t standard across all tiers -  just like almost every other productivity app out there, including Trello, which is just as affordable.

title: Ugh! I thought my search was over…
body: Just downloaded the app ~30min ago. It’s already heading to the bin. A star given for the overall first impression of the interface. In many ways it borrows or models itself after Apple’s own native apps, which IMHO is terrific. However, 3 stars off bc Anydo ultimately failed to meet a couple minimal expectations: 1) INCONSISTENT FONT SIZE. I have good vision but the font type and size in the app are inconsistent. Some places have mouse-font that can barely be seen. (I expect this for certain calendar views but not anywhere else.) Can’t find app specific controls to adjust this. 2) CAN’T FIND CONTROLS TO DELETE INDIVIDUAL LIST ITEMS. I know they’re in there somewhere but even using Anydo FAQ, can’t find it. For example, building a grocery list adding items works much like Apple’s Reminder app which, again, terrific. However deleting individual items from that list is challenging. I can only find controls to delete the entire grocery list. Swiping, press/hold nor any menu I could find has worked. I now realize the same is true on other lists. Perhaps my growing frustration blinded me from seeing the obvious but that is EXACTLY why I’m considering deleting the app. I don’t want an app that drains my time and energy figuring out how to do easy things. I want to get in/out of the app quickly. I don’t want list making to become another time draining task that gets in the way of actually doing. If deleting a grocery list item turned into a 30min speed bump, what happens if I try to use Anydo for something important? Shame. The initial impression showed such promise…That all said, Anydo has stood the test of time and has many devoted followers. That’s a HUGE accomplishment. For that, I give a second star out of respect.

title: Close, but not quite
body:
Such good potential wasted by essentially being converted into a clunky sales pitch. 

Visually, the app appealing, easy to navigate, and makes sense contextually. There are all the “must-have” features like calendar integrations, lists and labels, reminders and deadlines and such, but the efficacy is lost with notifications, banners, badges, and an entire section of the main page dedicated to showing you all the value of the paid subscription aspects still available to you if you’d only pay the monthly price of yada yada…

Another significant hindrance is the difficulty in trying to join in to another user’s board, unless that’s simply another feature available for purchase. I could see this working for someone who was going to be the sole user of the lists, but unless you’re willing to pay, it’s not quite a team application. 

On a personal level, I found that seeing so many “call to action” pitches throughout the app was not only distracting, but quickly got annoying. One or two. That’s all we need. I know where the buttons are, I clicked on them before, I’ll remember if I do decide to upgrade where I need to go. In a time of software as a service and subscription models galore, this felt a little too heavy-handed and stood out for the sales pitch it is. 

Three out of five, works fine enough I guess, but download it and try it out, I’m not your boss, I can’t tell you what to do with your life, be a free spirit, fly on the breezes of the App Store as far as your little wings will take you.

title: Good Website, Buggy App
body:
I’ve been using Any.do for a while now, and I rarely have problems. I usually access the website instead of the app. Therefore, I haven’t noticed the issues.

This is one of my favorite organization apps to use, but there are some errors. Starting at surface level, the “My Day” label in the bottom left is slightly skewed. Not a functional issue, but it bothers me. 

As far as function, I’ve had a few issues. I recently moved my tasks from one large folder into multiple smaller ones, so as to make my life easier since I cannot afford to test the subscription. I can simply add whichever tasks I need into “My Day”, which is my favorite feature of this app that really sets it apart. However, after moving these tasks, all of the sub tasks disappeared. I now have to go back into my assignments and re-write all of my sub tasks. This is very frustrating, as I already have to juggle seven classes before having to organize. This app is meant to make my life easier, rather than adding “Fix my to-do list” onto my to-do list.

Overall, this app is amazing. I just hope they fix these bugs.

title: Simple and Effective; The way an App should work
body:

author: Obyrnesean

title: Keeps crashing
body:
UPDATE 3: Yesterday when I opened the app, the plus sign, which is how you add a task, is missing. I can add an event but not a task. Events show up differently and you can’t snooze them that I’m aware. With all of its issues, this was still the app that did the closest to what I need, but I’d I can’t add tasks, that will no longer be true. I just wish they would fix the issues instead of creating new ones. It’s so close to perfect. 

 UPDATE 2: responding to the developers’ response to me: I didn’t know that Apple forced some things on developers however, condescension in response to something that most users would not know is not appreciated and the smiley emoji doesn’t help. The issue with this app continuing to scroll through upcoming alerts without telling you the date it is due (it only lists the time) has caused me to miss repeating tasks because I mark them done when the alert isn’t due until a later date. Another issue is that in order to save your date and time, you have to click DONE in the lower right corner but if you are clicking to indicate that the task is completed, you do so with DONE in the lower right corner. They either need to change it to DONE and COMPLETE, or SAVE and DONE. I’ve often inadvertently marked a task as complete when I only intended to save a change. Users should know that this app is much easier to use on Android than on iOS and that there are features that can cause them to miss appointments. 
 
UPDATE: I was finally able to get the app to load on my new iPhone X. I have used it on an Android for years. There are a couple of features I didn’t care for on Android (it stops you from doing anything when the alerts pop up and sometimes made me lose what I was writing) but I prefer that to the iPhone version. There is no easy way to snooze the alert like there is on Android so you have to click to go into the app to do it. But when you do, it scrolls through all of the alerts you have set without telling you when they are. So I end up marking repeating tasks or something I have previously snoozed as done because I can’t see that that alert is for a later time. When trying to set an alert, I generally write something like, “Dr appt at 3:00” and set my alert for 2 so I’m not late. Sometimes, I set an alert for the night before so I am prepared for the change in my schedule. But if you do that, The app WILL NOT LET YOU CHANGE THE DAY OR TIME! It auto fills the date as today and the time as 3 and you can’t change it. In order to get around this, you have to enter the time and date in the app first, then what it’s for. However, it will sometimes still default to the time it wants you to set rather than the one you set. If my appointment is at 3, I don’t want an alert at 3. I’m already there! 🙄 And I would like to just write the date and time in rather than having to scroll through the flip menu. Additionally, if you don’t remember to set am/pm FIRST, the app won’t let you set the time correctly. So if it’s 2:00 am and I want to set my alert for 1:00 pm, The app absolutely will not let me and keeps changing the time until I fix the am/pm issue. It can be helpful to have it do that if I was trying to save the alert for a time in the past, but not being able to fill it in in order (day/time/am or pm) is frustrating. If you have to fill in am/pm first, then put that before the time. In my initial review, I said I would give it a 4.5 if I could get it to load but on second thought, I would give it a 4 in the Android version due to the issues I mentioned and a 3 in the iPhone version. The help desk did help me figure out how to get it to load, though it took a day after they said they solved the problem (too many completed but not deleted tasks) before it actually loaded and didn’t crash, and I appreciate that! I feel like this app is so close but it continues to be frustrating to use. I can’t find anything better so I’ll probably stick with it, though.

 INITIAL REVIEW: I’ve used any.do for years on my Android phone and really like it. I got an iPhone X, downloaded it, and it either won’t load at all or it crashes when it loads. I tried deleting and then downloading it again with the same result. I can’t access it at all. My schedule is in it and I can’t access it. I would love to know if there’s a way to solve this. I would give it 4.5 stars if it would let me use it.

title: Any.do is Too Buggy to Ask Users To Pay
body:
Been using Any.do on my phone and PC for years.

- Open the app, and half the time the screen shows in dark mode and the other white, so you can’t read half the tasks on your list until you force-close the app and reopen.

- Add a task to the calendar, and there’s a substantial chance it freezes while editing it. Reopen and the task you had added will be gone. Not where it was originally created, and not where you tried to update it.

- Sometimes tasks are solved but still show up on the task list as unsolved.

- Recurring tasks will sometimes have dupes and their times change to some random times if not completed.

For how long this app has been around and charging for a subscription for the more useful features, it’s not worth the cash and time for how buggy it continues to be. I don’t get how these issues are still present.

Now I gotta spend time looking for other recommendations on a clean, reliable, robust, stable task manager that integrates well with other apps and works across multiple platforms.

title: I want to love it
body:
I’ve used Any.do for 2 years now, through college and wedding planning. I need this app to be efficient and streamlined. I have had the premium subscription for both of these years. 
As an Apple phone user but a windows laptop user, I love that the desktop app is versatile—if it would work. It doesn’t load, it doesn’t update, and it doesn’t display the calendar as efficiently as I need it to. 
With so much going on in my life, I need to color coordinate, and that simply isn’t possible with Any.do. I can sync my Google calendar to the app, but it’s all in one color. 
I deleted my windows app a while ago after it simply stopped opening. 

I relied on the iPhone app, but it glitches far too often for it to be truly efficient. I need to immediately see what I need to do, not be presented with a glitchy screen every few hours. I need the tasks to get a strike through as soon as they have been completed, not hang out for a while and leave on their own time. 
I have the same calendar issue on my iPhone app as I did with the windows app. Everything is the same color, and it often uploads twice. I would be getting double reminders for the same event. 

I want to love Any.do but for a task efficiency app, it is simply not efficient, and not worth the premium subscription.

title: Doesn’t really flow.
body: I downloaded this app for one reason only. It works with Alexa. Ok, I said, ill give it a try, so I got it and signed up for a month of premium ($5.99) The rest of my morning was spent trying to figure the app out. After the first three crashes, it smoothed out. The UI is simple, white back ground- no Dark Mode. You have the ability to change the font color. The screen that allows you to show all of your calendar and to dos is a scrolling clunky mess. You can get this view from any app on the market. On the To Do side, adding them is simple- not by keyboard shortcuts, unfortunately (like CMD-N) Adding repeating events is very clumsy (this feature is only available with premium) The repeat automatically defaults to the present time with no way to edit this and you cannot go into a task and edit it to repeat- this has to be done during the initial task set up. On the to do page, it gets worse. In one view (on iPad) on the left is a list of My Lists- which cannot be edited- cannot remove a list..I turned off Apple Reminders, yet there is still a box there,unused, that I can’t get rid of. There is another tab for Tags, which are color coded. Nice, but when you add a tag to a To-Do, you only get the color- not the label for the tag in the To Do view. So, this is about as far as I got with this app. I’m not happy with all of the little “quirks” and weirdness of it. Deleted it.

How much revenue is gained by this obfuscation? (ALL approved in TOS and your STINKING lawyers, I'm sure!)

FIX THIS!!!

Holding onto MY money like Gollum onto "My Precious".

title: Cancelled subscription due to sharing issues and annoying features
body:
When I started paying for this app, it was fairly simple and worked well to share shopping and todo lists with my wife.  Over the years, the features have multiplied, bugs have multiplied, and I feel like I’m being strong-armed into using features that aren’t helpful and are actively annoying.  Sharing and syncing issues were the straw that broke me.

First, the unwanted features. Any.do created lists I did not want, and I was unable to delete them after hours of trying and googling.  Any.do started using artificial stupidity to automatically add due dates to items:  “2-3 avocados” turned into an “avocados” item due on February 3rd.  Any.do decided it needed to organize my grocery list, but of course it doesn’t know where anything is in my grocery store, and it makes all kinds of bad guesses about what things are.

That’s only a taste of the “advanced” features that were forced on me in a barely working state. Have you ever had somebody insist on helping you, and they’re so incompetent that you prefer to be left alone, but they won’t take a hint?  That’s Any.do.  For each new feature, there was a learning curve to figure out how to avoid accidentally activating it.  That was no accident; Any.do was desperate for me to start using these features that didn’t serve any purpose for me.

But I might have continued to tolerate it if we hadn’t had chronic issues with sharing.  I don’t think I have ever been able to delete a list that I shared with my wife.  She couldn’t leave the list, I couldn’t remove her from it, and neither of us could delete it.  The final straw was my wife being unable to sync our grocery list and me not being able to fix it after twenty minutes of trying, including uninstalling and reinstalling the app.  That’s the end for me, and I feel relieved.

Two stars instead of one because we got a few years of utility out of it despite the issues.
author: PartialFunction

title: iPad app buggy
body:
I use Any.do on my Android phone and an iPad mini 5th gen. The iPad version is very buggy. 

(Jun 6, 2021) Repeat options do not appear when editing a task unless they have been first set up on Android. Then if Repeat day or time is edited, changes are not saved. They must be edited on Android before they will be saved.

Floating keyboard will not close. Even going to Settings or elsewhere in the app, the keyboard will not go away.

Also with floating keyboard, problems entering a new task in the quick entry field at the bottom. It’s necessary to tap the up arrow and enter the task in the main new task window.

In Calendar view, all Google calendar events display in one color only, the default events color.

(Jun 7, 2021)  After tasks are marked “Done” they continue to appear in reminders. If those reminders are marked Done, there will be a 2nd crossed-out line with the same task. I have seen as many as four duplicates of the same crossed out task.

If these multiple completed tasks are recurring tasks, then the next upcoming occurrence is pushed ahead. So a weekly task ends up appearing in Upcoming 2, 3, or 4 weeks away. The only way to fix this is to go to Android and reset the date of the next occurrence. 

I will add more to this review as I come across other problems.

title: Any.Do is The Best Way to Prioritize My Work
body:
I have been using any.do now for over six years. I have tried many other applications to help me organize my to do list and set priorities. Any.do allows me to quickly move items from category to category and up and down within categories so that I can organize my daily tasks around high priorities. This allows me to stay focused on my most important priorities and related tasks so that I do not get distracted into activities that are less effective.
We all have a temptation to check items off our list for the satisfaction that brings. Checking the right tasks off the list, even if fewer tasks get done, is much more important than the volume of tasks. Any doubt do allows me to sortAnd shuffle multiple times a day to keep me focused.
I fact that any.do syncs with my email account, my slack account, and my calendar, and can be used on my phone and laptop, makes it a tool I can take and use anywhere. I highly recommend any doubt do to anyone who wants to get things done.

title: Misleading calendar support
body:
This app does not directly support Gmail or Outlook calendars. Instead it relies on the iOS calendar integration.

This is significant because to connect iOS to a work Exchange or Outlook 365 account, you must accept their security and remote device management policies.  Allowing these often means certain settings on your phone are disabled (like disabling the lock timer on your phone, which I use when cooking).  It also grants your company’s agents the ability to remotely wipe your personal phone which puts your data, like personal photos, at risk.

In my opinion, Any.do should directly support common calendar API’s using a custom sync engine and remove all reliance on the iOS calendar system.

Also, when editing a task, the font size is ridiculously huge.  I can’t believe I have to scroll left, and arduously long task in iOS, to edit a single sentence todo.  Shrink the font size so I can drag and drop the cursor at the place I wish to insert an edit.

Edit:  The developer responded and I appreciate that.  I do still think the landing page at any.do/calendar is a bit misrepresentative.

It displays prominent images for Google Calendar, iCloud, and Exchange and includes this language, “Always know what’s coming next on your agenda.  Any.do works perfectly with other calendars such as Google Calendar, iCloud, Outlook, and more. It’s the best calendar app to help you regain control over your busy life.”

There’s no asterisks or disclaimers stating that a phone is required to use this functionality.

I think that potential customers should be aware of this before they make a purchase.

title: NEED: Better ALARM & functional NOTIFICATION BADGES
body:
I set many reminders, but frequently miss them! The reminder alarm is even less attention grabbing than a simple Facebook notification. Plus, if your phone is on “silent mode” for IPhone, the reminder doesn’t even vibrate. This means, if I’m not staring directly at my phone at the time the reminder alarm is shown... I miss doing the task. 

I also have 10-20 notification badge icons attached to the Any.Do app at any givens time. The badges represent ALL tasks for the ENTIRE DAY. This isn’t functional. Badges should only appear once it’s time for me to do a task or after the reminder has passed (so I’ll know I’ve missed something). The fact that the badges show ALL your tasks, for the ENTIRE day, ALL day long until you check them off makes the alert system even less attention grabbing than it already is. 

Could the app developers please make a more attention grabbing reminder alarm? Something that emulates a regular alarm system perhaps. For example: A message that stays on my screen until I click “OK” or something. Could you also recode the badge icons to only appear as the task are scheduled throughout the day?

I really love the functionality of this app and all the different options for organization and sharing. I truly think this app has the potential to be the BEST daily planner app out there. However, these two problems could become deal breakers if they aren’t fixed :(

Thank you in advance

There’s a tag feature, but you only get one tag without paying $36 a year, and I can’t figure out how to filter with it anyway. Help is no help. There’s a focus mode but that’s premium too, so I don’t know anything about that. There’s icons all around the periphery of the screen, and some of them do things. You can look at your todo’s sorted by date or by project. There’s a panel on the left-hand side which lists projects (and grocery lists!) in big rectangles. It’s probably no fun if you have more than 6-10 projects. Oh, Projects may be lists. Or maybe some lists are projects. It’s all so hard. And pricey.

title: So many bugs this app is basically useless
body:
I’ve had this app for maybe a couple years now. I’ve so desperately wanted to love it and have been so patient with it, but it’s basically broken—literally almost every essential feature just doesn’t work. 

Let’s start with the calendar. The calendar has a bug where the name of the month at the top glitches when you flip to other months. It’s almost ALWAYS showing the wrong month name making it impossible to know what month is actually displaying. I contacted support months ago about this problem, even sent them a screen recording to show the issue. They said they figured out the bug and would fix it in another update. Never happened. So the calendar is useless.

Alerts. Flat out don’t work. When I set an alert for events, it doesn’t matter what time frame I select... 15 mins before, 30 mins before, 1 day before... the alert never triggers until exactly 1 min before the event every single time. Event alerts will NEVER come through at the time you selected. Period. 

Lists. Half the time, my list won’t sync with Alexa. No amount of refreshes and restarts will sync it. I add a lot of things to my list via Alexa, only to find them nowhere to be seen in the app. So I try to add items to my grocery list manually... nope! I type items with my actual fingers and add them to the list, and they disappear. Never show up on the list. Also, as an added annoyance, every time I open my grocery list the “smart list” feature tells me it’s found things in my other lists that might be groceries and asks me if I want to move them to my grocery list. Except the items it identifies are not even close to grocery items—such as “vacuum apartment” from my to-do list. PLEASE allow the user to turn this feature off. 

All of these most basic and essential features are so broken, I sadly am about ready to move to another app. Like I said, I so badly want this app to work... but it just doesn’t.

author: 𝕖 𝕝 𝕝 𝕪 ®

title: Buggy and Inconsistent
body:
I want to love this app. But I don’t. The more I’ve used it over the course of well over a year, the more I’ve grown to hate it. Now I’m just waiting to try and find time to find a new replacement app/service, but my whole life is in this thing. Migrating will be tedious, especially since I can’t reliably know I’m getting all my data out.

Where to begin with why I feel this way. For one thing, the app is very inconsistent across platforms. I have an iPad, an Android phone, and I use the browser version from Chrome while at my desk. I also have it integrated with Amazon Alexa lists. The experience between versions is absolutely horrendous. Take something simple: search. The Android app, just doesn’t have a search feature at all. You read that right: YOU CAN’T SEARCH in Android. PERIOD. I mean... WHAT?! You can search in the browser version and that is simple enough. On iOS... you can do it, but good luck finding it. I’m on an iPad... to search, I have to first go to the grid view. Search isn’t just an option on the main GUI. Nope. You have to go to a specific place. But, it gets better: you can only see the search option in PORTRAIT mode. I’m in landscape mode most of the time with a Smart Cover keyboard. So this is a royal pain. If you’re in landscape orientation, the search icon just isn’t available. Nice, guys.

But that’s not all. Simple things like Tag view. You can’t do tag view from the browser version. At all. So, go ahead, tag all your tasks and get really organized and creative with it. Then become absolutely crippled when you’re at a web browser because there is literally no way to even SEE tags. They don’t exist there. 

Those alone would be deal-breakers. But there’s so much more like this. If you use an iPad, the dialog for setting a due date/time/reminder doesn’t render right. It never has. In any orientation. The options don’t all fit and you can’t see them and/or scroll to select them. So, simply setting a recurring event is a huge pain on any iPad (and I have 2, a pro and an Air 2). And there are lots of things that just don’t render right, or are moved, or flat out don’t work or don’t even exist in one version or another. So, if you are a multi-platform user of a heterogenous set of devices LOOK ELSEWHERE or else be warned you are in for a frustrating experience as you move between app variants. I should mention that I always keep my apps and devices up to date... just in case you were hoping these were one-off bugs fixed long ago. 

Even without the variance of features and consistent experience, I would at least expect as a bare minimum for an app like this to offer rock-solid functionality and reliability. If you’re going to rely on this thing to manage and organize your professional and/or personal life, then it needs to work. Well... this doesn’t. It crashes often in both Android and iOS (and has been that way on multiple OS and App versions for the year+ I’ve been using it). Synchronization across devices is spotty. I use Amazon Alexa and rely on speaking my thoughts out into the air so that important tasks are recorded and later, hopefully, followed up upon. Well, there are often big discretions between my devices. With 2 iPads, both with a totally good internet connection, side by side, I just now scrolled through and noted a handful of discrepancies. Despite manually doing syncs on both, forcefully quitting and re-opening the apps on both, and trying again. The order of tasks is different, the revision of notes of the same tasks are sometimes different, and sometimes entire tasks don’t exist on one but do on the other. This is the same app version on the same device type and OS version, side by side. It’s worse when going between my Android phone and iPads and/or browser. Let alone Amazon Alexa. 

As if all that weren’t enough, the core concepts of the app and its interface are flawed. Tasks lack any way to “postpone” them. So, as you scroll through your “Today” items, it’s not easy to just put things off to focus on what you believe you can get done. You have to either drag items to “Tomorrow” (hard if you have a big list”, or manually set a new due date. The reminder notifications give you an option to get back to something, but it’s unclear and not customizable how long you’re putting it off for. It just puts it into Upcoming. There’s no indication from there when that task is now going to fire again. If you experiment, you’ll find it’s a week. 

There’s also no distinction between a due date and a fire on date. So, you can’t have reminders notify you of things in advance. You also can’t have a task that you intend on working on that will take longer than a day. You’ll just have to keep moving it from day to day. Sub-tasks lack their own due dates. This is not good for projects... even very, very small ones. The simple act of returning something you bought online is hard with this. I need to call customer service tomorrow when they are open. But then I need to wait until I get a return label, at which point I’ll then need to drop off my package. But then I need to wait to confirm they got it. Then I need to wait to confirm I get my refund. I end up having to either make a task that lives on being manually re-scheduled 4 times to get this done, or else I have to make 4 completely separate tasks. And there’s no concept of waiting on something for a task.

But conceptually, the worst thing is recurring tasks. The interface often doesn’t show you when an upcoming task or recurring task is next due. Sometimes it will, but not always. Worse, if a task fires and you postpone it, it seems really odd when it chooses to fire again once you finally complete it. If you let it sit in “Today” until you mark it done, it will use the original fire date. If you reschedule it, it might ask you if you want to reschedule the occurrence or the series. It usually doesn’t ask you this! Most of the time I’m just left unsure at all and end up mystified.

title: Great UX, DON’T BUY Daily Planner”
body:
PSA: This is a thoughtful review, both potential users and the app’s team should note it. 

Before anything bad, I’d like to say their organization and interface is awesome, it’s clean and logical, at least to how I think about task doing. 
BUT they try to fool you into subscribing to their “Daily Planner”... please do NOT do this. Once you use it once on the free version, you’ll notice that it doesn’t do ANY planning for you, it has you pick the time for the task manually (although it has some preset options)... so.. you’ve entered in the task, you’ve manually set it’s time.. why are you paying $5 a month ?? 

@ Developers, what should have been done here was use the same preset options: Morning, Noon, etc. then take those preferences and use them to organize the tasks into time slots. May not fit into user’s preferences perfectly but it could be really good. You were literally so close to making something awesome and worth real money but what you made was literally pointless and actually a burden to anyone who clicks a preset option for more than 1 calendar event because they need to go in and change that.

BTW, is that not false advertising? I mean it is NOT a daily planner, you provide all of the planning information. 

In summary, great app if you’re not paying. App devs, hop on an AI tool to do the planning.

title: Great Hierarchy of Thought/Strategy
body:
I like the subtask feature best. It matches the way I think. Sometimes a simple list doesn’t provide enough detail, but it’s nice to have a list for quick reference, especially on long term goals. This program/application allows me to add details behind the list when the going gets rough and I find out there is more involved in a project or task than I originally thought. It gives me a sense of accomplishment, because I don’t have to erase and re-think the original goal. I’m still working toward it, but breaking it up, clarifying, and re-thinking my strategy. Hierarchical organization can never be under rated.
 
With regards to the grocery list feature: great/excellent.
I never thought of putting my groceries in a category so that my grocery time will be cut down because I’m not zigzagging all over the store to different places. I appreciated the automatic categorization feature so I don’t have to think about it. It’s a great feature and works better than I thought it would. Also, the ability to name the lists is great. For example, my wholesale store items and my local market can be in two different lists. (I like to buy some things at Costco, for example, and others at Walmart or Macy’s or Target, etc. Making a separate list for each store is a breeze with this application, or moving items from one to the other when I don’t find them at a particular store.)—Note: I use “voice identification” a lot during this process. It’s great this program links with it. It helps me not forget to buy things I need. 

Quickness of response to thought is a key component. I think this program has done this.

title: a couple tweaks needed to an otherwise perfect app
body:
This is so close to being the ideal calendar/to-do app. No other app that I’ve tried (and I’ve tried a lot) has done as well at integrating to do lists and a calendar.

 There are a couple things that would make this absolutely perfect, though. I really like having the monthly view with the dots showing which days have events, but I *really* wish the agenda view below it would scroll. It’s more difficult than it should be to move between dates in that view, especially when I’m trying to find time for an appointment far in the future.

And this seems like a hard thing to do, so I’m not docking any stars for it, is being able to say or type, “meet Mom for dinner at 7 PM at restaurant,” and then having the app put all that information where it needs to be. Instead, the user has to type all of that in the individual date, time, location, and description fields. I’ve tried other apps that have this feature, and it is so convenient. But I’m guessing the tech behind it is pretty complex.

title: I like the app, but...
body:
I have recently downloaded this application and I like the interface and the overall usefulness of the app itself. 
However what I find to be frustrating is I like a reminder app which gives me location based reminders. Most apps you can simply type in a name of a location such as Kroger's for example. You do not have to put in the address and it will simply remind you whenever you get near or at a location with that same name without having to put in a specific address. In this case you have to put in the exact address in order to get a location based reminder, most places you don't have an address unless it's a place you go regularly. The app doesn't give the option to show a map and look up a location however when you find what you're looking for it does not give you the option to select the location on the map and have the address automatically imported . Hopefully this is something they will correct in the future because this action would make the app easier to use in the end.
Also the app automatically connects to Amazon Alexa. Which would be fine except for example it copies over my grocery list. Then shows for my tasks over 50 items due today because my groceries have been added to it. Even though my groceries have not been given a due date just items needed. So every day when it asks you to create your day. It will ask about every single grocery item and when I plan to buy them. Got old real fast. I have looked and do not see an option to stop this from occurring. Plus the option in setting to sync with Alexa...doesn’t allow you to edit it to choose what you would or would not sync. I for one have my grocery list synced to another app and wouldn’t even include it with this one. 
Also every single time a reminder/task comes up on your screen and you go and mark it complete. It automatically opens the full application for you to go in and mark complete. Very annoying. What is the point of having the app show up on your watch or pop up on your screen if you have to go in and manually mark complete anyways. 

I don't know if I'll be keeping the app do to these issues. I am not willing to pay $9 a month with these types of issues in place. Maybe I will check it out again if they make changes.

title: Great App But Mossing 1 Key Feature
body:
I love Any.do. My favorite part about it is the “Plan my day feature.” I don’t know about other people, but my todo list priority order frequently changes. The plan my day feature is a great way to re-prioritize as well as view all your tasks so nothing slides through the cracks. It’s seriously a great feature you have to try to see the benefit. Other aspects of Any.do are also pretty good. Nice interface, pretty stable, looks nice. 

Now the missing feature: Natural Language Input. Half the time I’m entering a task, I’m trying to do it in a hurry and I almost always need to set a reminder. With other apps, Todoist and Tick Tick for example, you can add a todo by typing “turn on the sprinklers at 8am” and they parse the input to create a reminder for you. Any.do doesn’t do this (as far as I can tell).

There seems the best a pretty popular feature request on their website, but it’s quite old (+1 year). This one missing feature is having me considering switching back to todoist or trying tick tick. 

Please added this feature! (Or show me how to use it if it already exists :)

author: nielsenpablito

title: Only worthwhile premium function doesn’t work.
body:
I love the standard Any.do functions, they’ve really made a great product that is intuitive and works well. I decided to try out the premium features because the location reminder service standard in the iPhone Reminders app is lacking. This was the sole reason I decided to pay for the premium features. Unfortunately, the location reminder feature has never functioned correctly. I spent time working with customer support and trying all of the “troubleshooting” they offered. Nothing worked and the problem persisted. I finally grew tired of waiting several days in between responses and asked for a refund. I was told that Any.do as a company has no control over refunding customers and I’d have to go through Apple.  I submitted a request to Apple and was told that they could not issue me a refund for this purchase. It seemed like an automated response. Honestly at this point I just gave up, it wasn’t worth the wait trying to get my money back. 

After about two months of only using the app for simple lists I received a response from customer service saying they’d updated the app and fixed the location reminder issue! Fabulous! Well, I just updated the app and went through the process of setting up a location reminder and the feature STILL does not work. I’m at a loss for how this is possible. It seems like Any.do isn’t testing their product in real world situations before making claims about what it can do. If their reviews were based on the premium features offered and not the simple free version of the app I’m sure their rating would be much lower. I’ll rate the app again if they can ever fix this basic issue, but until then this app can’t be used as advertised.

Update 4/10/19
The developer contacted me and informed me that the most recent update fixed the issue. Unfortunately this wasn’t true for me. As I stated before, I was in contact with their tech support and continued to use the basic features of the app until this update was available. It was only after downloading the updated version and seeing that the location reminders still did not work that I left my review for the product. I will gladly update my review again if the problem is ever fixed. And to top it all off, it looks like they released ANOTHER update just a couple of days after I unsubscribed from the premium features of the app. Did this update finally fix the issue? How could anyone know without paying to find out? I’d recommend that anyone who wants to purchase premium features solely for the location functionality check other users’ reviews before doing so. I eventually was refunded by escalating the issue directly to Apple, but in my opinion Any.do dropped the ball by not ensuring a feature functioned on all devices before deciding to charge for it.

author: Pierce0210

title: New look makes it more complicated
body:
Why would they make a simple UI complicated and make this a less productive experience for the user?

The new design is less straightforward and more cluttered. 

Once you add a task, you only either set a reminder for a certain date. You can no longer set a reminder for a date in the future AND set that same task to reoccur weekly or monthly. Instead, as soon as you choose the task to repeat, it will repeat it on the same day and time the task was created.

Also, once you set a reminder to a task, you can’t choose a date for it to reoccur or make any other reminder based edits. You have to delete the task and create a new one, but are still bound to the issues outlined above. 

Any.do team, please understand that the simplicity of your app is what made it work. There’s no need to keep adding fancy things and changing the UI. Just make sure it’s simple and works and syncs well, and it will remain a favorite.

After being told that the web version is the “source of truth” for the current tasks, I started using the web version while at work (instead of the chrome extension which is not being updated).

However, whenever I open the app again, it has never synced to the web version. Even after selecting sync on both the web version and in the app, both versions continue to display their respective tasks, and the phone app never updates to the web version.

This, of course, makes users less productive instead of more, as we end up having to do dual task removal and addition.

title: Great app. Started crashing recently. Needs bug fix

Things I’ve did in the app before it started crashing:

1. Added my calendar
2. I also started an Any.do moment, looked at the premium upgrade, clicked not now, and exited out of the Moment. I was considering upgrading, but the crashes do not now.
3. Moved some tasks around (app didn’t crash immediately after doing this, so probs not). Renamed a task. Deleted a task
4. Added a subtask to an existing task and removed completed sub tasks. 

The app crashed after #4. The app continues to crash whenever I open the app. It takes a few seconds to crash. During those few seconds, I’m still able to scroll and mark tasks as completed or change them back to complete. The changes I made were still saved after the app crashed and I reopened it.

Usually a great app with a nice UI, but crashing. I’ll fix the rating when the app works again. Hope you guys fix it soon! Let me know if I can help.

title: Used to mostly work, now unusable
body:
I’ve used the app for a few years now.  I learned early on not to rely on its reminder notifications, because most of the time they don’t work (especially on repeating tasks).  However, other than that, it was pretty useful.

In the last couple weeks, though, it has become so buggy, it’s completely unusable.  When I mark a task as done, it crosses out like it should, but then it just stays in place instead of moving to bottom of the list.  When I press the X to remove it, nothing happens.  I have to either switch to a different screen (say, the settings) or force-close the app and reopen it before it will update the list.

When I added some new tasks recently, it took a couple tries before it actually saved them.

And now I just realized that some of my tasks have disappeared entirely.  I have about a half-dozen tasks that repeat every Monday.  They were all there last week, but, as of today, all but one is completely gone.  I hate to think what I might have put in there a while ago that might be gone now and I won’t even realize it until it’s too late.

I don’t need an app that forgets the things it’s supposed to remind me to do.  I can forget to do things all on my own.

title: Not with this app.
body:
The calendar app is good. Not so much for the todo and reminders. 

Unfortunately for me (and apparently many others) one HUGE missing feature is the inability for reminders not able to reschedule repeating reminders based on completion date. For example if you need to repeat a task every 3 days. And some times you do it in 2 or 4 days. Well with a repeating reminder based on completion it will reset to every 3rd day based on last completion day. 

Not with this app. 

For me it’s a showstopper. It’s a basic feature feature for a digital reminder platform. The UX without this basic way for managing time based (repeating) reminders is simply subpar. Hope the UX deficiency will be corrected ASAP. Unfortunately it looks likes it’s been stalled for many years so will not hold my breath.

title: ⚠️ Sync with Reminders at your own risk ⚠️
body:
Great app except don’t sync with Reminders because it will insert due dates, re-order lists, delete reminders, and all of this odd behavior will continue to be triggered by interacting with said Reminders, even after deleting the Any.do app, until one recreates their Reminders lists from scratch. 

Otherwise, seems like a good app that would be useful if not for this Reminders quirk.

——Edit——

I appreciated receiving the developer response, even if it was about year ago that I left this review. Since then, I’ve noticed the “due date” desynchronization issue occur sometimes when Reminders are altered on my Apple Watch, implicating Apple’s own API’s as the likely culprit, and I have read about various other apps that interface with Reminders API exhibiting the same behavior. I still think that developers for apps that interface with Reminders have to be aware of the issue and should thus issue a warning (but that would probably keep their update from being approved on the App Store, so that again falls on Apple). I’m changing my rating to 3 stars based on my limited usage of the app and willingness of the developers to troubleshoot the problem with me, but I’ve chosen to leave this review up as a warning to others, even if this problem is not Any.do’s fault.

I’d just like to add that I wish Siri was more compatible with the app. For example, “check X task as complete” or “add X to any.do.” I’m not sure if there’s already a way to do this but with the ways I’ve tried, Siri has responded that it is incompatible with any.do. title: I miss some old features, but I really like the new color-coded tagging system

This feature used to really help me realistically plan how much I could get done in one day. They canceled the feature and now the “moment” feature works differently. I really miss how it used to be. I hope they can add it back someday. 

However, one new feature that I really like is the tagging system feature so you can add your own color-coded tags onto your tasks and define what each tag means to you. 
For example: you can have a tag (red tag) that means to you “this takes 3 hours or longer to complete.” So you know not to plan a lot of stuff that’s tagged red. 
I personally also added: 
(yellow tag) = “this task takes 30 minutes - 2 hours to complete”
(Green tag) = “this task takes 15 minutes or less to complete.”
You can also tag stuff like (blue) = “social”
Or (grey) = math projects for college.

author: Texas Snow

title: Too many bugs, terrible tech support
body:
Unfortunately I no longer use this app and will not be recommending it to my friends. I experienced the same bug multiple times. If I created a task and went into that task to add additional details, all features were not available and if I tried to use them, I was prompted to upgrade to the paid version of the app. This is an ad that swings up from the bottom of the screen when you touch a feature that isn’t available in the free version.  However, even the features that were supposed to be available in the free version were not available and I was plagued with this ad to purchase your full version while not having access to the features in your free version at all. Not cool. 

Your help desk kept having me uninstall and reinstall the app. I corresponded with them over a several week period. I described the bug in great detail. Uninstalling and reinstalling was their only solution offered. I did that on three separate occasions and the app would work fine for a few days until the same bug would return. One even suggested it was my phone and not your app. I was asked to create a video of the bug but unfortunately I didn’t yet have that feature as I have an older iPhone. 

Oddly enough my husband was also using Any.do and experienced the exact same bug, though. Maybe it’s his phone too? Doubt it.  I don’t believe it was my phone but I guess your customer service team doesn’t want to fix bugs, just blame the user. That’s called lazy customer service. 

The last time I uninstalled it and reinstalled your app, I lost all of my task lists when I logged back in. I had over fifty some odd items typed into Any.do. I reached out to customer service hoping there was maybe a way to access a back up, I again got no assistance. Since I had to recreate my whole task list I just switched to a different task list, Wunderlist, and have had no bugs or problems since. I know it’s being remade but it’s still there for now and it works much better. 

I can’t recommend your app because it’s purpose is to save me time while instead I was left dealing with the frustration of this apps bugs and trying to get help from customer service took up MORE time. Losing my task list completely was a huge waste of my time. I am so relieved I did not pay money for your full version!! Useless customer service and an app with too many bugs. 

There are plenty of other task list apps out there that work much better.

Update: I received an email and review response from the tech support person at any.do, Tali. I found the response to be unhelpful and unproductive as it was mostly just explaining that they feel they did their job and I did not provide adequate description and the information they requested for them to resolve my issue. I feel the need to further explain since I don’t believe that is fair or accurate. 

Asking a customer for a video of the bug when it is happening after the customer has provided a detailed description of the bug several times isn’t helpful to the customer. At the time of the email I did not have the capability to take a screencast on my iPhone because I had not updated my IOS yet. It is not that I wouldn’t provide a screencast, I couldn’t. But that said, Customer Service never bothered to gather any other information about the situation such as what iphone I had, what iOS version, which app version I was running, etc. That is critical information that can help solve bug issues. Why did they never ask?

Since I could not provide a screencast of the bug I was refused help at that point even though I had provided a detailed description of the bug. I was also told that no other customer had described a bug like that so that was how the representative drew the conclusion that it was likely my device causing the bug. At that point there was no additional help offered to me. In my opinion this is not effective tech support response in investigating a potential bug. They didn't even collect any info on my phone, iOS version, etc as most tech support people investigating a bug do. 

If I could move this rating to NO STARS, I would. I feel like instead of just saying sorry, and accepting constructive criticism to improve their customer service effort, Any.do support is now blaming me for their lack of technical assistance in resolving a bug! Ridiculous and unprofessional. They keep responding with long excuses and assigning blame to others instead of owning the issue and using this scenario as a learning experience for their customer service group. 

Don’t buy this app. If you can get the free version to work, kudos to you. But if you use the free version just know that you are not likely to receive good customer service if you have a problem.

Update 2: The app developers keep updating their response saying I can still reach out to them but still have not taken any responsibility for the numerous times I tried working with them. I happily will use Wunderlist until it is cancelled, as it is a far superior task app and has all the features AND IT WORKS even though it’s not even supported.

title: Best of many similar apps I tested methodically
body: Before I purchased Any.do, I evaluated over a dozen competitive programs (wunderlist, minimalist, things to do3, Trello, etc.), reading all the reviews and even buying most of them and test driving them for a few weeks with test lists.  I had been a big fan of the old program ToDoMatrix, which was really WAY ahead of its time so much so that before they adapted it to iPhone I kept my blackberry a couple of years past its prime because of the importance of a really functional ToDo program.  Was really disappointed when TODoMatrix finally stopped working so I launched an all out evaluation of the best replacement.  The only thing that Any.do does not do that I wish it did is permit one to reorder tasks within sub task lists.  Otherwise, it has easy entry, reordering, grouping, sharing with others, reminders, locational notifications etc.  in short all of the stuff that we have come to rely on.  I think Wunderlist is a pretty close second and in fact I use it supplementally for straight list management like shared grocery lists, travel checklists etc.  Any.do's best feature is arguably "Plan my day" where it encourages you to pick which of the many things that have built up you are actually going to tackle today, and quickly assign times to everything else later in the day, tomorrow, in 2 days, next week, a specific date, or "someday".

title: Try Deleting a Task
body:
In order to delete a task, you are required to complete it, then hunt for it deep in the settings. That’s like requiring a driver to turn off the engine before opening the door.

I’m a todo list veteran, and it took me 6 minutes to figure out how to delete a task... that’s shameful. Apparently, here’s the process that makes sense to the Any.do team:

1. Complete the task by swiping it right or tapping the checkbox/circle.
2. Go to the general settings tab.
3. Under the third main category called “Tasks”, tap the [Completed Tasks] menu item.
4. Find your completed (but not actually completed) task.
5. Tap the [x] located to the right of the task.

Unreal...

title: In Memorium
body:
Any.do is like your first car. Despite its flaws, you love it, because it’s simple, it gets the job done, and at that point in your life, you’re not in need of anything else. That is, until you wake up one morning and realize they took the steering wheel from you. And charge you to get it back. 

I had been a user for years, and even though I came across a glitch almost every day, it was only a minor annoyance, because I liked its interface so much. Never-mind that at times some of my tasks would just completely disappear on their own (which somewhat defeats the point of having a task manager in the first place to remind you of what needs to be done), I stuck with it, and even incorporated the version for my MacBook.  

But recently, as I was promoting Any.do to my fiancée so we could plan our wedding with the app’s collaboration features, my dark theme went away. When I went to deactivate it, the app demanded that I subscribe to its monthly service. Something that I once had for free, for years, was now gone. This may not seem like a large issue, except for my medical condition, which comes with a frustrating eye sensitivity. I contacted Any.do about the issue, but unfortunately never heard back.

There always comes a time that we must trade up, and thankfully, there are plenty of options out there. If a car maker wants to remove features, and start treating their maintenance-heavy product like it’s a BMW, then maybe it’s time for the junkyard. Thanks, Any.do; you got me through a lot of years. I’ll miss you, but I’m very happy with my new set of wheels.

title: Love/Hate Relationship
body: The Any.Do team is ahead of the game by adding features people are actually requesting and need. The Alexa/iOS reminders integration is a hugggge update and is very smoothly implemented (THANK YOU FOR THIS FEATURE!). It boggles my mind that this feature is not the standard for To-do apps, but I digress. The Plan My Day feature is phenomenal. I am a huge procrastinator and this makes it easy for me to plan my day without hassle and frustration. These two things are the biggest selling points for this app, and I LOVE them. However, there are some things that could be greatly improved. Firstly, the calendar portion of the app needs to be overhauled badly. I took one look at it and noped out of there back to Calendars 5. If I could just merge Calendars 5's calendar views into this app, Any.do would be THE best app for its intended purpose. Granted, I love those view options because I am a highly visual person (you may not be), and the whole month view with dots everywhere just looks cluttered and overwhelming to me. However, until there is an update to the calendar section, I will continue to ignore it and focus on the app's awesome to-do list section. The interface looks great for the most part, but I wish there were more ways to customize my viewing experience a little bit (different colors for different lists, "List" Lists view instead of the default "Tile" look, etc). One major issue for me is the way subtasks are handled in this app. It is incredibly frustrating that you cannot rearrange subtasks. Also, subtasks are much too hidden and require one too many steps to get to. Besides subtasks, I greatly wish there was a way to exclude certain lists from your "All Tasks" list and "Plan My Day" feature. I have a daily checklist with a ton of small recurring items (such as "Don't forget teeth whitening strip") that I would like to be able to consolidate into a simple "Complete Daily Checklist" under the "All Tasks" list. I would normally get around this by making a Daily Checklist task and have those small specific things subtasked, but as I stated before, the subtask feature needs to be heavily updated. These frustrations, as few as there are, are detrimental to my usage of the app and keeping me from going all in on premium for the app. However, considering the recent updates and features added, it is quite clear that the Any.Do team is in the business of listening to its customers and innovating. I have a feeling I will be back here to change my review and rating to 5 stars in the months to come. All in all, a great start to an amazing app.

title: Just what I needed!
body: I have been using this app for two days and I love it. The "Plan My Day" feature is so helpful. It requires me to re prioritize each task and resets the reminders. This is a huge time saver and perfect for when I don't get to a particular task as scheduled but need to remember it later in the day,  next day or later in the week. I signed up for the subscription so I can share and edit tasks with my teenager. I can see when he has completed items. It saves our face to face time for conversations and enjoying time together and keeps tasks all business. I'm getting less arguing so far! He can also send me a list of things he needs for school or home and it syncs in with my other tasks. No more searching texts to remember that he needs more highlighters! While I could stay organized the old fashioned way, I am so grateful for the way this program does so much of the organization for me. There is also a calendar view that syncs with your iCal. You can see both scheduled activities and task for each day. It can be added as a widget on the control panel screen on an iPhone. Try the free version first and you will fall in love. It does bug you to upgrade but I was happy to do so.

title: Nice app but could be better
body:
Overall, this is a good app for keeping track of your to dos; however, I would like to see two changes.  First, I would like to see the "today", "tomorrow" and "upcoming" categories automatically sort by reminder time.  You can manually drag them into the desired order, but it would be better if it were done automatically.  Second, you swipe right to delete a task, but then it sorts to the bottom and you have to scroll down to complete the delete process.  I would rather it stayed where it was so you could tap on the "x" to finalize the deletion process instead of having to scroll down one or more pages.  Also, I have noticed that sometimes a task appears twice on my list and if I try to delete one, they both disappear.  I'm not sure if this is happening with tasks that I had my Amazon Echo add to my to do list or something else.

As for the developers response, I do not want my calendar combined with my to do list. This is why I did not choose the calendar view, so this does not solve my issues.

title: I love any.do for iPad!
body:
Any.do does what the others don't! I love it! 
5 stars for: syncing between all devices, sublists, helpful reminders, and countless other organize features. 

A couple things i'd like to see:
An option to make a bunch of sublists, lists. So if I have an item that I make 15 sublists entries for, I would like to have the option to put them in a list. Right now they are stuck as sublists entries. I actually got out a good old fashioned pen and paper to write down the sublists entries I wanted to move to other lists to add as actual list entries. Because some of my sublists entries need notes or sublists of their own. I get that it could get messy with never ending sublists. So that's why I think there should be a feature a little 3 dot button perhapys with an option to move to another spot within my any.do
I love EVERYTHING else about the app. I use it on my Windows desktop, my Chromebook, my iPad, and my android smartphone. 
I downloaded over 75 note taking apps on my android smartphone a couple of months ago in hopes of finding the best one for getting more organized. 
Any.do is the best to do list app
Any.do is the best note taking app
Any.do is the best organizing app
Any.do is better than Evernote
Any.do is better than Google Keep
Any.do is better than default to do lists

I have turned countless people on to Any.do
Group discount on premium would be awesome. Similar to Spotify premium for families or Google Play Music family plan. Separate private accounts that pay one low rate.
