title: Simple to use and more capable of handling everything.
body: After buying so many other to do list's on the market, this truly shines above the rest.  With an Apple watch, phone and Ipad I could not set an appointment fast enough before the lady at my doctors office kindly made a card for me to take home with the date of my next appointment written on it.  I left the office and immediately changed to the Any do app.  It collects everything no matter where I am.  I can tell it a random thought.  It's saved.  The Moment system brings it all together to quickly organize it.  Like magic, nothing gets forgotten, I don't stress, and it's simple, super simple and really really fast.  In a few seconds I can get a thought into the ap saved for later.  I'm not creating shapes and colors and symbols in a crazy scheme like other apps.  This just makes sense.   Its the first app that can actually handle the many different responsibilities of my life.  Pay for the premium.  Its completely worth it.

title: Horrible and clumsy interface
body:
Others who rate this great, they're probably not
doing that much. Certainly nothing hideously complex.

I work in financial IT as a project manager - so I know how good to-do lists work. I've even hand built GUIs on occasion, so I have a good understanding of how to best use applications to enter data and access various functions.

Take it from this PM - If you're using this to track tasks, either look for something more intuitive.

And if you truly need something to track your "insanely busy life", you'll have to look at a calendar on a daily (if not hourly) basis anyway, so just use that. 

Avoid this like the plague.

title: Go-to app - needs Siri commands
body:
Any-do is the only app I use for keeping my task list.  The separation between today, tomorrow, upcoming, and someday - and the ease with which I can drag items from list to list - simplifies things amazingly.  Any.do reduces the amount of icons I need to tap to do things to my list. Entering new items is easy, and when I've finished an item, crossing the item off the list is also an easy, single swiping motion (rather than having to select the item and then press delete like you have to do in most apps (or in iOS itself)). That might sound like a small thing but it totally makes a difference, you'll see. 

The only thing that's sorely lacking is Siri interactivity, so that I can use a verbal formula to add items to any.do the same way I can with the native iOS Reminders app.

title: Suggestions
body: 1.The items in your today list should appear in order of the time it's due. 2. I'd like to be able to rearrange the order of subtasks. 3. I don't like that at midnight my today list changes automatically. Even though it is technically a new day, I work until 11 pm and usually have a list of things to do before I go to bed and I don't want them to be mixed in with the things I have to do when I wake up. There should be a setting to change the time that your today list switches to the next day's tasks. 4. I don't like that I have to give a set hourly time to all of my tasks. Sometimes I will plan to do something on a specific day but it doesn't need to be done at a set time. Then I'd like to be able to just quickly rearrange the items by dragging them and then see them in that order when I pull down the Today tab in notification center.  5. If I give a task a specific time, I'd like to see it between my events on cal. 6. Cal needs to be updated because it crashes often and the app does not navigate easily. And my any.do tasks often appear twice on Cal. 7. On the any.do app, Id like to see my upcoming tasks grouped together by the day of the week I've planned to do them and to appear in chronological order. 8. I really enjoy any.do moment and thats the main reason I still use this app. You should consider creating a similar feature for the next 7 day's tasks that also includes someday events so it's easy to create a plan for the whole week. & the settings should allow you to choose which of your lists you include in this feature so that way you don't end up scheduling every item on your grocery list

title: Great "To Do" App!!
body:
I like this app a lot and use it as my primary "To Do List" app. I would have given it a 5 star rating, but it has a couple of annoying glitches. The one glitch that drives me crazy, which other reviewers have also mentioned, is the "create new task" page issue. If you accidentally click on this page (which I often do), there is no way to simply "go back" to the page you were on before. The only two options you have are to: 1) Exit the app completely 2) Make up task. 
If I were not a paying premium member, I may be willing to overlook such an inconvenient problem. However, there is no excuse for such an annoying and easy to fix glitch, especially for those who are paying. 
My second issue is more of a suggestion as opposed to a glitch. I would like an option to be able to see "subtasks" listed (or at least part of them) under the primary task on the "list" page. As of now, one has to click on a icon to view a separate subtask page. 
As far as everything else goes, the app is great! It's easy to read, easy to use, convent and I can attach just about any file to my tasks. The only other thing I would love to see, is the ability to customize the app's interface a bit more. At least in regard to more colors and different fonts. However, this isn't a necessity...

title: Annoying- needs a lot of work
body:
Full Analysis here:
I was referred to this ap by Street Leverage so I had high hopes. Unfortunately this ap doesn't meet any expectations it can list and share, it is more frustrating than helpful. 

Like many in the other people's comments, I think it is simply ridiculous to accidentally start a new task and then either exit the ap or make-up something to then check off in order to leave that screen. <-- #1 annoyance. 

My husband also reports that the ap nags him everyday in the morning to, "plan your day!" which one can only do if they pay premium (which we won't be doing because we're poor). So the "plan your day" is ludicrous. He says it's very invasive and bothersome.

Another complaint he has is that the ap also leaves an alert on his phone's desktop pull down menu that he can't "slide away" AKA dismiss it. 

Also, I dislike having the little red number of the sum total of *all* the things on *all* my lists that then appear on my ap icon. Many of the things on the list are only for my husband (on a shared list) and many of the items on the list are long term or low priority (getting to projects or something like organizing my sock drawer, which, who knows when I'll get around to that... - hence the list), so seeing the little red "47" over the icon on my home page is disconcerting at first, and then just annoying. 

Another thing that would be helpful is being able to prioritize. I put things on my husband's list for him to do, however, because his phone doesn't sync the same order I put that list in, the top of the list might be "iron clothes," so he does that instead of "Get copy of gas bill," which would be more time sensitive. This works vice versa for my To do list as well. Ain't no one got time to scan through 20+ items and figure out which one your spouse, or even yourself, wants you to do first and second and so on. 
Priorities people.

While there is an option to star specific items, not only does the list not sort by stars, but the problem remains the same in that when there are many starred items, one has to scan through them all, or, if only staring 1 or 2 items, having to fish through the list of regular items after those 2 starred ones are complete. Another problem with stars- something might be very important to then star, like "renew driver's license," but some of that must be done in parts, like getting 2 forms of ID, and some of those important starred items may be out of your hands for a while, such waiting for a bank statement. Therefore the star system, while mildly helpful, is still flawed. 

I also think you should be able to un-cross-off tasks that are complete. I buy milk almost every other week and so I have to enter and re-enter "milk," when it would be so much easier to just slide the other way when we need it again and then have it not be crossed off. 

This ap's doesn't seem to be very user-friendly for iPhones. My husband has a Galaxy and the design looks better on his screen and is easier to manage/understand. 

Still, we're a little disappointed and annoyed with the turn-out of this ap. If it doesn't update or change its current design, we'll find another free ap that isn't as frustrating to work with.

I can't create new categories. By categories I mean Tomorrow, today, upcoming, etc. I really wish there could be one for groceries so it doesn't go under the others. Or for crying out loud let me crest my own and get rid of the ones I want. If your going to update your "newly improved" app soon, include an editing tool for the categories that. The to do's and events go under. It's annoying when my event/to do can't fit under any categories. If this doesn't get updated anytime soon, I'm going to just use the app that I'm WAY more happy with for organizing things; Notes. At least on Notes I have control of how I want to organize things.

title: A great app for keeping managing tasks
body: Any.do is a great app for helping me manage my tasks. I have various things to track and complete, but there's not always a definitive timeframe for getting them done. I really like any.do and it's the perfect organizer for me.

title: Love it minus only one issue
body:
I downloaded this app because I needed something would organize my tasks productively. By productive I mean efficient and effective. 

Every other task app I've used either took too long to set up or didn't do what I needed it to.

This app does all I need and more. I used it for two hours and decided to upgrade to the $27/year premium version.

I LOVE the "someday" section. There are so many things that I would like to do, but they don't need to clutter up the tasks that I need to do.

My only issue: The synchronization feature is garbage. I was pumped to get this app because I switch between iPhone, PC, and iMac all day long. I was disappointed to see that the syncing doesn't quite work across my devices. Most of the time all of the new tasks I create show up fine. However, I'll complete a task, click sync, open my other device, click sync, and it doesn't complete the task on my other devices. 

All in all, I think it's a gem and the best task software available. I've finally found my solution to getting stuff done and keeping track of it. Once any.do gets their act together with the syncing, I'll be 100% sold and give 5 stars all day.

title: Wanted to like it, but...
body:
I really wanted to like Any.do, but I wound up switching to another to do list app, and so I thought I'd lay out exactly why I ended up switching.
First, and my most major issue with it, is that it forces you to assign a due date to every task. I prefer having some tasks with a specified due date but having other tasks with no due date -- things I have to get done eventually. This wound up being the main reason why I don't want to use the app anymore. Along with this, when you add a task, it defaults to "today" as the due date. Then, if you have notifications enabled (which I want to do so it notifies me of important to-dos), it ends up notifying you that you have, say, 78 tasks due that day (which included everything on my "Groceries" list, all of the random tasks I wanted to leave undated, etc.). Eventually, almost all of my tasks wound up unsorted in the "Today" part of the list, which rendered the whole app pretty useless for my purposes.
Other miscellaneous annoyances: you can't delete tasks, the interface is pretty boring and the font is small, completed tasks pile up at the bottom of the to-do list until you go down and "x" them out so they move to the "completed" list... Oh, and since I had notifications enabled and so many tasks listed in "today," the app would send me "helpful" notifications like, "productive people have fewer than 5 tasks on their to-do list per day!" Um, STOP.
So yeah, not worth it for me. Already found another app that has none of these issues! This is not to say that Any.do is a worthless app -- clearly it works for a lot of people, so it's certainly worth trying it out. That said, I wanted to lay out the features that DIDN'T work for me, just to give a fuller perspective of its pitfalls.

title: Use this app everyday!
body:
I use this app to keep track of all my shopping lists.  I used to be in a store like Walmart or Lowe's to pick something up and I just knew there was something else that I had thought of getting there a few days earlier but I couldn't for the life of me remember what it was!  And of course I'd remember as soon as I returned home!  But now I don't have that problem. Whenever I think of something I need to buy somewhere I just add it to that store's list that I've created on this app. I've even made a list for "things to by somewhere".  It's a list I can use when I want to buy something but I'm not sure where to buy it. That way whenever I'm anywhere shopping I can look at that list and look to see if that store has what I'm looking for. 

This app has helped me be much less forgetful when I'm shopping and has saved me a lot of time and money. With less trips to town and less time walking around store aisles racking my memory.

This app checks both of those. It does nearly all that I need out of a to-do app (which is possibly the most important app on my phone).

However, I have one complaint. I like to use Any.Do in the pull down "Today" menu. However, when I check off a task from the pull down "Today" menu, it does not seem to sync with the app itself. Ultimately, I'm left with all kinds of tasks that I've finished in the "Today" menu, but none finished in the app itself, which causes problems. I'd love to see that fixed.

Otherwise, excellent work, and keep helping people become more productive.

title: Pros and a few Cons
body:
The Any.Do app system is the best to-do tracker I've used so far. I've tried a bunch of free productivity tools over the past year (Trello, Google Calendar, etc.) and found that they don't stand up to Any.Do.

Pros: simple UI, great reminder/moment system, great recurring and location reminders

Cons: few themes/color-schemes, non-intuitive settings and screen flow in the app, could use more features such as better photo integration (more than just attachments)

Returned to review this ap because I love it so, and I would just be recapitulating the previous review. Unlike other reviewers of this version I welcome the paid ap changes, and my partner and I are talking about how to integrate it into our project tracking. Here's the old review:

title: Today and Tomorrow's date is still missing
body:
Let me start out by saying that I'm only rating this app 1 star so the team reads my review. (I already emailed you guys about this before!) I am addicted to this app. I have gotten my entire family to use it now. 

But Today and Tomorrow's date is missing. I think this is a serious flaw in user interface. It should be shown somewhere on the app when you're viewing your to do list. In example: Today is Sept 20. Tomorrow is Sept 21. 

I understand that you wouldn't need a date for the upcoming section or the someday section, but I am used to dating all of my to do lists. 

Other than that, you guys are doing a fabulous ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ job. I'm really enjoying the reminders section. I think the sub tasks could use a little more work. The user interface for sub tasks isn't that intuitive.

As other reviews have stated, it would be nice to color code urgent tasks so you don't ever miss them when your list gets super long. 

Anyway, keep it up team and I'll keep recommending this app to everyone I know. Eventually, I would love my entire company to use Any Do as well to improve productivity. 👍

title: Not bad buuut
body:
I like it (Apple's default reminders app deleted my stuff twice and that makes me really upset, so I tried to find another app), but I think it's kind of slow. As in, why is there so much lag after I save a new reminder, or set a new time? I'm used to making reminders immediately. 

Continuing on the "lagging" point, it is also irritating to have to change lists (I have mine named "personal" and "work," and have not figured out a way to change the list I put a reminder in unless I go to that specific list. And I cannot do that quickly because of the aesthetic time it takes to switch (it floats slowly after I click on it ... Not sure how to explain without remembering the term). So if that could be quickened that would be more convenient.

Also, is there no "finished items" list? I would like that, instead of having to delete them all (in case I ever need to check if I've finished something but have forgotten). 

In addition, I agree that there could be darker lines or something separating the "today" from "tomorrow" lists and such. 

I think there should be more options put for "snooze" as well, like "snooze for 10 minutes" and those kinds of presets. It's kind of a pain and takes more time to edit and reset the time entirely. 

I do like the chime of the reminder. It's not irritating at all, which I appreciate. 

Not a bad app but there could be many improvements, I think.

body:
I just recently downloaded the app - so far, it's FANTASTIC. Two elements I wish were involved in it, though:
1. A reminder that will also email you when something is due (similar to that of Gmail). I sit on my office computer a lot of days and I've missed a few reminders that have popped up on my phone and, since I'm not on my phone a lot, I've just become accustomed to keeping the web version up on my computer and check it occasionally. It'd be awesome if a reminder setting could be turned on/off that either had a desktop reminder pop up OR send an email to you. 2. When something comes due, Id love a setting that allows me to then add it to a "follow up" list. Many of my to-do's involve sending people emails but (as people are apt to do) they don't always reply. This way, I'll get a follow-up reminder to email them again. 

Just my two cents :-) BUT I am loving it thus far!

title: "Moments" feature puts Any.Do ahead of the competition
body:
Any.Do provides a simple yet effective user experience for laying out my tasks for work and for home, but what puts Any.Do ahead of the competition is their "Moments" feature, which makes it easy to review, prioritize, and check off any outstanding tasks in a matter of moments.

I receive daily reminders on Watch before I even finish my first cup of coffee. My daily to do list is available on my desktop/iPad/iPhone at start-up. This app has absolutely saved me time, increased productivity and costs much less compared to annual subscriptions for Omni or Evernote. No more stopping your workflow to make a damned list! title: Minor frustrations in a great and straightforward product
body:
Any.do seems to be the app that I was looking for to make my to-do list something that is more likely to be completed. I am now a premium subscriber because the Moment feature is very good for organizing my thoughts and reminding me of what hasn't been done yet. 
There are some things that bug me about how the app works that should be simple enough to work out. On one list I have a series of tasks that repeat everyday so that I do them each day and start over the next. In my mind, I have a certain way of doing them, so I like to keep them in a particular order. I have hand-sorted the order numerous times and then when they are complete they move to the next day, but in a different order than when I sorted them and completed them. 
Another annoyance about daily recurring tasks is that when I set them to remind me at a certain time, but I complete it before that time it remains in the "Today" section. 
An unrelated thing that I would like changed would be to have the ability to delete a task easily. Sometimes I make a new entry on my list, but then find out that it's not my job anymore or it's not something I'm going to do ever. Naturally, I want to delete it rather than scratch it off my list (that would invalidate my total completed counter!).
author: Shlobert

title: Great idea, but a little "spammy"
body:
Any.do is probably the first todo that actually helps me get more done. The 'handle now or reschedule for a definite time' structure (familiar to users of Mailbox for email) really helps your todo list from turning into a graveyard of aspirational goals. One innovative feature Any.do has that I haven't seen anywhere else is the "plan your day" screen, which forces you to schedule each and every task due that day, in a row. It really stops you from ignoring your todo list, without forcing you to do all of it all at once. 

My one complaint is that the app really tries to upsell you. It requires you make a (free) account to use the service, but has bunch of reminders to upgrade to their paid (currently ~$2.50/month) service. They also bug you with ads for some "rewards" service (though you can turn that off in the preferences.)

My only other wish for the app would be to have user-defined times for how long to snooze a task. Mailbox and its ilk allow you to choose one of 9 snooze times, which you can define yourself. Any.do only lets you use today, tomorrow, upcoming and someday. 

Still, even with those complaints, I'd recommend this app, especially if other todo systems never worked well for you. I'd also check out Swipes, which is similar in approach, but with a slightly different design.

title: Finally Found a Good To-Do App
body:
This is a great app. I used to like it more. They've added a ton of features and obviously now tailor to enterprise level. There's list sharing and all that. I wish they'd kept this simple and added all the features to a premium version.

None the less, here's what I do still like:

The interface is still relatively clean and well designed.

Finished tasks: 
It keeps track of how many tasks you've completed, just cause see that number go up is rewarding. 

The best calendar view:
It syncs with your calendar. When you turn your phone sideways, any.do turns into a beautiful calendar

In short, I used to hate my clunky to-do apps and ended up reverting to using the notes app or post-it's.

title: A few small complaints but still a quality app...
body:
All of my problems with Any.do are minor. 

1. To start off, having to pay $2.99/month to access some features other apps offer for free is frustrating; HOWEVER, I highly recommend you subscribe to the paid version. Any.do in its premium form is easily the best to-do app around. Yes, even better than Wunderlist and Todoist.

2. The folders are not collapsible. Everything is still perfectly organized. You just might have to scroll a bit to see future tasks.

3. Subtasks cannot be moved around and reorganized. A simple drag-and-drop feature would allow for this.

Those are my only complaints with this app. They are small, so they don't detract from the app much. Any.do is the to-do app I'd recommend to everyone.

title: I like what I see, but...
body:
I tried Any.do a couple of years ago but I couldn't stick with it because it was too simple back then: no repeat features and no plan your day feature as well! But I've come to really like this version so far!
The plan your day feature is my favorite! I often use it, then reuse it 3 times a day! I also love how it tells you that you have too many tasks planned for the day!

I also really love how clean and simple it feels!

But I do have the following complaints so far that I really hope will be addressed: 

1. There needs to be a better way to change the due dates with out having to set an alarm to change it. 

2. It should give you an option in the settings to see multiple lines of the task's description on the list view when it takes up more than one line without having to click on the task to see the rest of it. 

3. On the plan your day view and alarm view, the task description is often cut off here as well, so when you read it, you have to try to remember what the rest of the task description said because you only get to see the first few words. Please make the whole description viewable.

4. When you set up the task as a project, the order that you type the sub-tasks in is where they have to stay! There is no way to rearrange the order, they're just locked in place! That's not good at all and pretty much makes the whole project feature useless!

I hope that these items can be addressed in the very near future! I just hope that any upcoming updates will not cause me to lose my lists and tasks like I've read in some reviews from other longtime users.

title: Any.Do - not what I consider a MAJOR update
body:
I've been using this app for three solid years, and have come to depend on it 

I've loved is simplicity and it had given me a lot of support in my life.

But, this is NOT what a major update looks like.

Improvements I like:
1) you've replaced the dark red highlighting off high-priority items with a much easier to see, star.
2) toy have a simple view available to see JUST these items. Also nice. 

BUT,

Problems:
1) Application crashes continue. This is the only app I think that crashes in my iPhone 5s.  It just quits and I'm back at the home screen. Annoying!
2) can't collapse lists now. I have way too many items to NOT be able to do this. Please put this back ASAP.
3) getting completely stuck in the"Buy Priority Support" screen. Wow, does that annoy a customer.

Don't get me wrong. I do like this app. But, I'm never going to pay MONTHLY support for an app.  I would gladly pay up to a $10 one-time fee, but never monthly. Sorry.

So, I'm not sure what's happened to the original developers, but you just need to listen to your customers better.  Easy to say, i realize.

A good app, and I'm going to hang on for just a little longer in hopes that you're listening and will make some changes.

title: Pretty Solid
body:
Still no iPad version. 

The first thing that caught my eye about this app was the interface. I really like the simple and clean white interface, or dark gray if you switch it, as it complements iOS in general. It's simple to use and great for making lists. I don't use it so much for reminders as some people do more or less, I use it for shopping lists and the like. There are some nice sounds which is always a fun and added plus.

While some people have suggested that paying for the app isn't worth it, and I somewhat agree, the free version for me has been fine. As you're making lists, one of the nice features, is being able to start typing something and it pulls information from what other people have typed. For example, if you're typing a grocery list and add "lemon" it will help you complete that without having to type the whole word.

A few things that I would like to see in the future is, one, and iPad version. Two, and iPhone six optimized version.three, a quick way of adding things to the list much like Clear does. For example, when you tap on the screen it immediately adds a new reminder or item to the list. With this app you have to tap the plus. Not a big deal but something that I appreciate in other apps.

title: Best task app I have ever used
body:
I'm a neurotic list maker - and have a corporate job in a day and age where huge companies don't have much support staff anymore so there is not enough time in a day.  

This app has helped me not only in daily tasks, but in capturing ideas and concepts as I think of them throughout the day when I'm not at my desk to jot a note.   

I am paying the monthly subscription service - and I'm very very frugal.  I really believe in this product.   It can be a little glitchy on my iPad view - but I love that it synchs my iPad and iPhone automatically.  

I use the daily moment to plan my day (often more than once).  I have added friends, coworkers, and family to tasks. Even if they don't have the app, it sends them an email with a task. I've also set up recurring tasks to make a monthly call to a customer on a certain day, or refill a monthly prescription.  

The money I'm saving on scratch paper and post it notes alone makes it worth the money!  Highly recommend.

title: Exceptional for to-do's and lists!
body: I use this application to keep track of "to do's", as well as for various lists. The interface is intuitive and easy to learn and/or use, and the relative simplicity of this app makes it possible to add and modify entries quickly, which makes it much more useful than other applications designed for similar purpose. My only criticism is that in a recent update, the designers have tried to incorporate features for shared lists and calendars. Rather than have to control these features by settings, I would like to see different versions of the app available in the future based on whether or not these features are desired. I would like to be able use this app without having to worry about accidentally sending something to the wrong person or group of people. On another note, something also worth mentioning is that this app works great when linked up with the calendar app from the same designers. I definitely recommend both.

title: Nearly perfect
body:
UPDATE: This app is not opening after the last update. FIX IT!!!

Original review: I needed a simple "To Do" app that would let me control the order of the tasks in an easy way and allow me to repeat daily tasks. This app is great. It does everything I need/want. I only gave it four stars because I have two issues/suggestions:

Not everyone uses Google Chrome. I use Firefox and Safari. It's forcing me to use Google Chrome to download what I need to do to sync. There needs to be another sync option where you can sync directly to google docs, Evernote, etc. even being able to email the list to my email address would be a backup option.

I would also like it if there were optional icons for the types of task folders you use. I trialed an app that I didn't like as much in terms of functionality. But it was nicer visually. The app had about five pages of icons you could select for your folders. For example, if you selected a car for Errands, when you placed a task under the Errands folder, that task would have a car all the way to the left on your ToDo list. This is nice when you're looking at your day and getting a snapshot of the types of tasks you have to complete. And it's fun! 

So nearly perfect. Almost there. Any.do is probably the best To Do app I've found. But I'd love to see those improvements.

title: This has worked great for me
body:
Using this as an organizer and task manager has been great so far. The UI has been simple and easy to keep up with. I Love that I can sync my tasks with the calendar Cal, so I know what needs to be done on what day. And that little surprise you get when you shake your phone to clear a task was so cool. 
I haven't tried to get "moments " yet, so I'm not sure how that works, and I don't try to sync across all devices because my work calendar is public, and some of the stuff I put on my personal calendar/task list is pretty personal. So I haven't run into the bugs other reviewers have mentioned. And since I didn't use it before they changed some features to a subscription-based service, I haven't felt disappointed that I now have to pay for things that were previously free. I knew from the beginning what the costs were going to be and was able to decide if I felt it was worth it or not. 
So for me, this has been a great app that has helped to keep me productive and organized.

title: From best to worst
body:
Any.do was one of those no-question easy recommendations to any friend. Although I didn't enjoy their calendar app as much, I thought this was the best to do list of the five or so I tried. I loved the swiping, the sub-tasks (great for grocery lists), different work/personal lists, chrome extension, and now list sharing. But this last version killed it for me. 

I unlike some reviewers don't mind paying for an app like this--IF you prove its worth it. And I probably would have paid for any.do right away. Except their update came with not only a hard sell to upgrade but SO many frustrating bugs.

Twice a day it logs me out while I'm on the phone in the middle of something. 75% of the time when I log in it doesn't recognize my credentials. If it DOES recognize them, it looks as though all my tasks have been erased. I have to wait about two minutes and they eventually come back. 

At the end of the day, I just can't put up with all this. The reviews and bug reports have to be coming to them for weeks now and I've seen no update. Sorry to say I have to move on. If only the folks at Dropbox would make a task app...

title: Rate Zero Stars If I Could
body:
This app used to be pretty good and needed only a few tweaks to make it great.   The annoying part about this app would be items in Upcoming would move up on their own, no setting to disable that. Constantly having to move items back forced me to use the app differently than I wanted to. I wrote to the developers almost a year ago and they never gave us the option to not have items in Upcoming to stop moving up. 

The developers gave an update that blurred the image when the app opened for a few seconds and then sharpened. I guess so we can visually "focus" on our to do lists. This was inconvenient and slow. 

With the next update, the app crashed any time you moved a task from today to another day. The Someday tasks still moved up to Today on their own, but now moving them back crashed the app. 

I just updated in hopes of a fix and all the items I have entered have been deleted. Over seventy of them. 

The app developers have no intention of making an app that is actually useful to the user. They forced cosmetic visuals on the user like the blur when opening the app and never allowed users the option to manually move items out of Someday.   And upgrading, in hopes of a fix, wiped everything out. 

Zero stars.

title: Way too little, way too late.
body:
Any.do had so much promise when it was first released. In particular, the Any.do Moment is an excellent solution to most people's failure to review their outstanding tasks on a regular basis.

Unfortunately, these developers have failed to keep up with their competition, and don't even update regularly enough to reasonably satisfy new iOS and iPhone releases.  By the time they finally released some much-needed, but very delayed, features (recurring, collaboration, attachments, sub tasks, etc), the app was too old and slow to justify keeping around.

It is almost painful using Any.do on an iPhone 6 Plus. Not being optimized for the new screen sizes is one thing, but there is serious lag following most touch commands, and actions like reordering lists look jumpy. I am happy to pay for an app that 1) meets my needs and 2) is being regularly updated, because I believe in paying for good products. Unfortunately for both myself, and the developers of Any.do, this app does neither.

body: I've been using this app for well over a year. I use it daily to keep track of all the things I need to do. Now, however, they have started charging for several things that were once free. I loved the feature of having the app remind me of a task when I left or arrived at certain location. Now I have to pay for that feature. title: Recent update ruined this app
body:

Now the app is useless to me unless I pay a price that’s too expensive for what I’m getting. 

Don’t get me wrong, I’m not against any.do charging for a premium version of their app. The premium version has some useful features for people working in teams—the ability to attach files and share to-do items with teammates. But I’m not going to use any of those items: I just wanted a seamless and elegant to-do list app to organize my own life. Ironically, in the future I might have paid for the premium version of this app. Now, though, I’ll probably never have the chance. I’ll be switching to a different to do list app.

title: MAJOR PRIVACY VIOLATION-DO NOT DOWNLOAD!!!!
body:
If I could give this app zero stars, I would. 

In search of a new way to manage my to-dos, I extensively researched the most popular productivity apps and decided that the premium features of this app were best suited to my needs. The "moment" feature is what truly sold me- it is brilliant.

So, after paying for a year's subscription of the premium account, I gleefully began entering all of my to dos (in English-this may seem odd to mention now, but you will see why). As I was doing this, strangely, a to do that I know I did not enter appeared under my "Today" section. How did I know that I did not enter it? Because it was in Portuguese, which I do not speak. I pulled the translation to see if perhaps I had entered something that due to some language setting I did not realize I had flipped was being entered in Portuguese. This was not the case. Confused, I deleted the item and continued to enter all the important details of my life. This happened again, however, within the next five minutes. I replied to the "welcome" email hoping to get support on my issue. (The welcome email encourages you to reply directly with questions or comments). This was the text of my email. 

"

Thank you for this very interesting app. I am entering all of my to-dos at the moment, however, and I am running into a bit of an issue. I am using the web to enter them, and I am noticing some to-dos appearing (in Spanish or maybe even Portugese) that I did not enter! I am a little unnerved by this as I feel like there is someone else editing my account...is this possible?????

Please respond ASAP. I paid for the premium and I am hoping that I will not have an issue with an app in which I made a financial investment."

It is worth noting that the purchase of the premium app promises the help of technical support, so I felt the issue would be handled appropriately in good time. Unfortunately, this was the response:

"could you please try to go to Settings->Preferences->Languages:
*If English is not selected - Select english, the kill app and restart.
*If English is selected - Select another language, Select English english, the kill app and restart.

Let us know if that worked."

At this moment I realized that the excellent support that I paid for was nothing more than a third party company who rather than being familiar with the workings of the app was copy-pasting answers from a support manual. They did not address the important issue- the fact that someone else has access at least in some small way to my PASSWORD PROTECTED PAID-FOR APP. They simply read the word "Spanish or Portuguese," flipped to the part of the binder that says "language settings" and typed away. I have never been more disappointed with an app.

body:

title: Gone Downhill, No Customer Service
body:
I remember many months ago, perhaps a year, after version 1.8.1 was released that the Any.Do team removed the beautiful typography that made this app so singular, a ton of people complained and tried to say something about it by voicing their thoughts and concerns via the in-app feedback system, email and social media – without success. I myself tried tweeting and emailing Any.Do *numerous times* but never got a single response back. So disappointing. 

I've got a feeling that with this premium features change is going to be more of the same. It seems the customer service is nonexistent at Any.Do and their focus is clearly elsewhere. I find it so disheartening that a company like them with arguably one of the most popular productivity apps on the App Store does not seem to care about their userbase and instead is pushing for a way to maximize their profits. 

What's worse is that most of these so-called "premium features" are ones that users have ALREADY been using since forever, and now they just simply cannot use them anymore or are capped. 

This is all such a shame regardless of how one looks at it, especially when one considers the previous changes that have gone down in a similar fashion. If anything, I'd be happy with paying a one-time fee for a premium version of the app, but not this. Hell, there *isn't* even an iOS 8 widget in this new premium model!! Or the ability to choose between different fonts! 

All in all, this is nearing the not-worth-it moment at this point. And I urge other Any.Do users to express their concerns here and to the Any.Do team (even if you'll probably never get a response back).

title: Demoted
body:
I have been an avid Any.do user for months and have recommended this app to everyone I know. As someone with boarder line OCD when it comes to organization and "to-do" lists, this app is the best list-making app I've come across; it goes above and beyond. Rather, I should say it went above and beyond. 

I was thrilled this morning to learn that an update existed and thought to myself, "how could they make this any better?" The answer, quite simply, is that they cannot. Now all the perks that made this app special that were included for free (the only version there was until now) now come with a price. 

An example, and one of my favorite features, is the setting that allows you to utilize your gps to notify you of a task when you are arriving to or departing from a specific location. 

While I understand the creators' want to make money, I disagree with their model of removing features that users are already accustomed to and expect. Instead, add new ideas to entice us to upgrade. 

Looks like the time has come to yet again search for a new to-do app...

title: Useful...Needs a More Changes
body:
The app appears to need an update after the change to iOS 8; when expanding a task, the date and buttons often don't appear.  There are a few legacy enhancements I still suggest:

Have a "next week" category, or allow users to create categories ourselves, rather than just using "today", "tomorrow", "upcoming" and "someday".

When you edit a task, it seems to move to the top of that category.  Rearranging them to the order they occur can cause the dates to change when using the "upcoming" category.  The dates must not change for any reason, unless I specifically update them myself.  I rely on the dates to be accurate.

When editing a long task, the text should wrap so it's easier to access the text at the end.

If these changes to in, the app will be really useful!

title: The Hotel California for your data
body:
If you create an account, don’t ever expect to be able to delete it. There is no way to do so in the app or on the web site. Sending a help request results in an auto-responder, telling you to send an email to their privacy alias requesting deletion. 

I followed these steps, and I have no received any reply. After ten days, I started replying to my original request, asking simply “any status on this”. It has now been nearly a month since the original request, and I have no received a response from the privacy address or anyone else at the company. Not even a notice that they are looking into it and will get back to me. It could very well be that no one is monitoring either address. 

I ask you: is this the kind of company with which you want to store your data? If so, good luck. I hope you don’t have any issues, because as far as I can tell once you sign up they couldn’t care less about you as a customer. 

You’ve checked in, and you can never leave.

But it's missing one key feature that makes it hard for me to commit 100%, namely some mechanism for exporting a history of tasks. It could be as simple as a CSV export or a RSS feed with info about when a task was created and completed. (My preference would be a feed, since that could be used in combination with IFTTT to store data elsewhere.) 

Other than that, a big thumbs up.

title: Fantastically simple app!
body:
I was hesitant to move away from the iOS reminders app, since a todo list sounds too simple to need a 3rd part app. I tried a few others, and was never impressed. I tried any.do on a whim, and it totally nailed the sweet spot between being simple and useful.

The groupings of Today/Tomorrow/Someday are really helpful for getting things done, and planning them out in advance. I'm less likely to be presented with a task I don't intend to complete anytime soon.

The simplicity of presentation and functionality is perfect. Other apps may be good at capturing details, deadlines, or collaborating with others. Any.do is all about simple one-line tasks that are just for you.

I will continue to use other task apps for different purposes, but any.do is awesome for simple, productive task management.

It's so easy to reorder tasks in order of priority, and with the press of a button, you can have Any.Do lead you through your tasks so that you can assign them to later times or even set reminders for later that day. My favorite part is how I can swipe through a task when it's done and see visibly that it has been completed with a line marked through it. title: My favorite app
body:
I've tried so many of these organizer/list apps, and Any.do is by far the best one for me. It's quick and easy, and therefore I actually use it everyday, unlike others I've tried and ended up not using. It allows for setting priority levels, it handles repeating tasks, reminder alerts, and has voice recognition as well. 

I love the "let's take a moment to plan your day" helper, which gives me a quick look at what I've got on my plate for the day. If I don't get to something, it's no problem, I can just run the "plan your day" again and easily change it to "tomorrow", "later", or "someday." 

Any.do  really helps me to focus on my tasks, and if I do happen to get sidetracked, I can just open the app again and either look at my to-do list, or run through the plan again and adjust it as needed. 

I haven't tried the Cal app yet, and I haven't yet installed Any.do on my other devices, so I can't speak to the syncing aspect of it
t, but I will update if I do. As it is though, even without those things, it's great for me. In my opinion, it's the best out there, and I highly recommend it.

title: Love it, but has major annoyances
body:
I've been using Any.do for over a year, now.  I find it an incredibly ingenious app that has no serious competition.

However, it has some bugs that I find seriously annoying, and they waste a lot of my time:

1.  Although the App synchs nicely between my laptop computer and my iPhone, the order of tasks assigned do NOT synchronize.  When I called tech support, they said "that's the way it's supposed to be."  I would like to sequence the tasks in either app, and find that sequence automatically duplicated on the synched device.  Instead, I have to manually synch each device, a huge waste of time, since both should have the same sequence.

2.  I find my laptop frequently signs itself out of Any.do.  Not a problem in itself.  But when I sign back in, any.do has reordered the sequence of all my tasks, requiring me to scroll to the bottom to see what is most important in every category, and then manually restore my original priority one task at a time,  a monumental waste of time.

title: Developers do not listen to their users
body:
I downloaded this app a while ago, drawn in by its sleek design. It simply looked fresh and I used it often. Trusting the developers, I went ahead and updated the app, a huge mistake on my part. The only thing I could notice was the hideous font before me. I really couldn't bring myself to use it any longer. Every update henceforth has been spent wishing for the old font.

Then the any.do team put up the Feedback Forum. Of course, the most wanted feature wasn't even a feature. It was simply a font. We wanted a simple font change. They let that request sit for months on end before officially "declining" it.

I know you may think it's something petty and trivial, but when aesthetics are part of the reason you chose an app over other similar apps, it's pretty important that the design remains appealing. More importantly is how the team completely disregards their users. People loved the old design; some tolerate it now. I cannot tolerate the design nor the team behind this app, so thanks for the productive month I had before I stopped using it.

title: Exactly what I needed in a to-do list
body:
I wanted something that was easy to use, allowed me to write a list of items, and then check them off as completed.  This app fills the bill.  I only have a couple of minor complaints- one, I'd like to be able to enter the whole list at once, not one item at a time.  And two, I'd like to be able to edit an entered item.  But those are minor.  What it DOES do is great.

Put an item on the list today, such as 
Grocery shopping.  Don't get it done?  It will automatically move to tomorrow, or you can move it to any day on the calendar.  Have an item on your calendar?  It appears on your list for that day.  You can catalog the items into areas (I don't, haven't figured out how and frankly don't think it would be helpful, but it is there.)  You can check off a finished item and leave it in the list (which helps make you feel productive) or you can delete it after you check it off.

It's an easier way to do what I used to do with notes.  And I love it.

body:

1. For best results REINSTALL this app after iOS 7 upgrade.
2. Make sure that your connection w/ device's contacts and calendars is TURNED ON. (Apple) device, go to <Settings>privacy>contacts> where you should see Any.DO listed; toggle ON. Then, same for "calendars" also under privacy setting. Will also need to REINSTALL Cal app for best coordination between these two companion apps. Chrome extension (slick!) allows desktop to communicate with the mobile apps. Must be on desktop machine (not mobile device) and WITHIN chrome browser to download successfully.
Am now finally happy with how this works, after much frustration and investigation. C'mon developers, give us some better help/ info about this beautifully crafted app!

title: Elegant, functional, customizable
body:
I love this app. Unlike other to-do lists, this allows me to customize my folder titles-- mine are To Do, Buy, Grocery, and Appointments-- and choose reminders for each individual task. I love that I'm able to choose whether the app badge displays a "number" based on my listed items; I hate seeing the number of emails displayed on my folder, and it's amazing that I can choose to have no number (or any number) displayed alongside this icon. Tasks like "Call Martin" automatically sync with my contact list, so I can simply click on the task and make the call without switching apps.  

The layout is simple, elegant, and totally intuitive. This app has largely replaced my use of Notes and Calendar apps. I love the way it looks, the way it works, and the music accompanying the "AnyDo moment" is weirdly awesome. 

Haven't updated yet, but I trust it will not do serious damage to current functionality. Download this app!

title: Say it ain't so!
body:
I had been using AnyDo for months, after testing every single to do app I could muster. This one was miles above the rest, with all the features I personally required.  

However, after the recent iOS7 upgrade, the app has become unusable for me. Every time I complete a task, or add a few tasks, I'm guaranteed an automatic crash. I don't lose any data or tasks, however it has forced me to look elsewhere for a similar to-do app until they work out the iOS7 bugs. 

It wasn't until this issue that I realized just how dependent I had become on this fantastic app. Fingers crossed this isn't goodbye forever, AnyDO!

**Update: even with a few back and forth emails with their support team, and doing their suggestion of "delete the app and re-install it" multiple times... Crashing issues and disappearing recurring tasks STILL run rampant. 

I know I'm not alone, because 1 in every 5 reviews makes same comments...Is their support team even listening to anyone?! 

Would love a suggestion for a replacement.

I love that i can make a list for anything and everything and that i can add, change, or remove lists just as easily as i created them. The one thing I do wish the app had though was a way to automatically put things in order by date, for example if I make a category for birthdays, if I don't enter them in order by date then they are all jumbled in my list and it makes it more challenging to view and plan ahead for upcoming events before they reach the tomorrow or today section. It would also be cool if there was a way to add a year to a birthday so when you look at the birthday reminder you set it reminds you that "so and so" is turning 12. title: Would love to love it
body:
I have used Any.do for some time now, and for the basic features it is great. It is the best way to manage my tasks and create on-the-fly to-do lists. However, there are a few problems that have gotten worse, rather than better:

*There is an option on the app called Sync. You'd think this would sync your Any.do app to other iterations (Chrome extension, etc.) but it just gives you the option to download the Chrome extension. This is ridiculously unintuitive. 

*That is even more frustrating because there is no way to actually sync your app and get it up-to-date other than deactivating it. This is also frustrating.

*Sometimes, reminders don't go off.

*Not specific to the app, but Any.do's FAQ tries to spin its bugs (these and more) as features, which is just insulting. It is not raining on my leg here, people. 

Sadly, these features keep getting slower, and really took a nosedive when iOS7 happened. I really want to love this app, but the developers need to listen to feedback and provide some of these simple features. A force sync feature can't be that difficult, can it?

Update: Two versions later and the sync problems remain large and in charge. The app crashes all the time. Please fix this :(

title: Simple, clear, rewarding to use
body:
This app simply works. It is better than Reminders as it has a simple interface that does not lose tasks and does not create duplicates. 

The update seems to be much more stable than the first iOS 7 release. I haven't seen a single crash. Even when they happened, crashes have been non-destructive (I never lost any data). 

The option to turn off sounds is very welcome. 

I also appreciate the app's efficient, intuitive routine for organizing tasks, i.e. to prioritize, postpone, or set one-click reminders for tasks. By default the app prompts you to do this once a day, but sometimes it helps to do it more than once.  

Feature request: The only feature I miss from Reminders is the optional one-line description under a task. Very useful sometimes. 

Any.do does try to recognize tasks involving phone calls or emails and to contact the subject automatically with a tap, so use the subject's full name if you want to make this work.

title: Life Saver APP
body: Like everyone else, I'm super busy and it still always fall back to my notebook (not computer) and write everything down. I always have one notebook with all notes, tasks, to-dos, meetings, conversations, reminders, etc...   At the end of the day, I would go thru my notes, cross off what I completed that day and write out my next day to-do list with new additions from that day. Hey, it's worked for me for years - don't judge. Haha. Anyway, this app has allowed me to do the same thing with my tasks/to-dos except I can now capture everything "in the moment" and then go back and simply complete it or move it to another day.  AND I can make a task a priority for the day.  Since using this app, I only have to keep track of notes from meetings, conversations, and phone calls which always have tasks needed completed. Now, they go in this app. My time saved per day has been unmeasurable, but even more, I'm much more productive and effective throughout my day.  Thank you for this app!!!

title: Organized, clean and simple - LOVE IT!
body:
I wish I had found this sooner. Any.do helps me  get my lists organized in minutes instead of hours. 

Some of the features I love are:
Updating an item has everything you need in a drop down. 

Items can be dragged and dropped. 

It is easy to switch from lists to day view.

Rotate your phone to consolidate your days list with your calendar! 

When planning your day, you can reschedule everything in a few quick clicks, instead of opening and closing each item. 

Navigation is wonderful!! Just swipe the item when it is complete and it grays and has a strike through, and moves itself to the bottom. 

Shake to delete completed items

Pull down for new items. 

Now I can spend my time DOING things on my list, instead of WORKING ON my lists!! 

THANK YOU!!
author: Shirl Pearl

title: Spot On
body:
I've had an iPhone from the first one. With the advent of the App Store, I've searched for a to do list app that fit my lifestyle, the forgetfulness of my brain, and the demanding task management of an over-achieving college student. Nothing satisfied all of my requirements... until I tried Any.DO. This is how I would design a task management app if I had the know-how. 

It's so easy to use, and (as corny as it sounds) it actually makes planning my day fun! Well, maybe not fun, but it is at least something that doesn't seem horrible, and I actually DO plan my day, now. I actually want to use this app. The app badges aren't meaningless, annoying bubbles to me, because I remind myself every morning what they mean. 

In all, the very fact that I am writing a review as a millennial (I'm supposed to be lazy and self-centered, right?) should speak volumes for the utility, aesthetics, and over all awesomeness of this app.

body:

Then when I moved in with my boyfriend, we had to start sharing lists like groceries, errands, etc. He is an iOS Developer and I'm a Designer so we also needed to collaborate on projects together. With much hesitation I had to delete this app and switch to Wunderlist 😫. With Any.do there is only a feature to add a contact to a task. With Wunderlist I get a notification as soon as he checks off milk. 

This app would be extremely useful if it added more collaborative features and that is the bottom line.

Also, when you go to plan your day - it doesn't make sense to me that the app doesn't reorganize your tasks in the order in which you plan to do them... It would be nice if it showed the times you've planned to do them... Furthermore - I hate that if you create a folder - it lumps them all together in your personal folder when in date view...There should be some subheadings and separation between tasks - I don't want the various items on my shopping list lumped in with my other tasks... I hope to see the developer work on these issues - it could be one of the best task lists ever with a little work...

title: Mixed bag - great on iPhone, terrible on laptop.
body: This is an elegant looking interface on the iPhone. Simple & pleasing. However, if you get overambitious, then get behind, & end up with about 58 things for today, it is a hard thing to move them. You have to turn your phone sideways & drag them, one by one, to this tiny, tiny calendar. I installed the extension on chrome, thinking that would be easier, but it's MUCH worse. Slow as anything to load. And worst - you can't sort to a calendar! I thought surely they'd have a larger version of the same calendar, either that or a pull down calendar under each item. I really don't even know why they have the desktop extension. I can LOOK at the list on the phone. What I really need is a way to sort a large list when it backs up on me. Why in the world doesn't the extension pop out to a full screen calendar, then I can just quick drag them, possibly selecting multiple items at once? So - fine on the phone, but where is the laptop parntering?

title: Okay, but not great.
body: This was one of the apps recommended for Astrid users after Yahoo shut the app down, but so far, I'm having a tough time trying to figure it out. It's not as easy as Astrid to create tasks, categorize them, or designate a task as something to do on a specific date without getting constant reminders. For example, I have my dogs' heartworm pill dates on my task list for a specific date, 30 days away, but every 2-3 days, I get a reminder to "Give dogs heartworm pills." It's just an annoying little thing. I'm also not a fan of any.do not having a webpage to create and manage tasks like Astrid. I can't use my phone at work or school, so it's a little obnoxious that I have to use other means to remember a task while I'm in one of those settings. Having a webpage to manage tasks would be a much better feature for users of any.do!

title: Great app; "Done" tasks need improvement
body:
I highly recommend this app.
That said, here are some improvements I'd like to see:
One. The font needs to be changed back to something a little bit more stylish.
Two. "Done" tasks need some tweaking. It's nice to have a feeling of accomplishment, And see completed tasks crossed out, However, that should be limited to only the most recent two or three completed tasks, and then they should automatically be sent to an archive folder. This business about having to press the X in order to remove them from the task list is onerous.
Three. There should be a way to separate and treated differently repetitive, daily tasks, from non-reoccurring tasks. For example, daily reoccurring tasks should not appear in the archived done folder, as they will clutter it up.

title: Simply Elegant
body: Efficient and easy to use, this app is well designed and executed.  I especially like the any.do moment feature; I use it every morning for parsing tasks to relative importance.  This has become an essential tool for managing my life, replacing the litter of multifarious to do notes.  Staying in disciplined routine is hard for me, but I am able to do that because I look forward to using this app. Adding a task by speaking it is so much easier than typing it, and in most situations, easier than scribbling it down.  Any.do allows one to follow the principles of GTD, without being a slave to it.  The only feature that I long for, after three months of use, is a dimension/element for projects.  I like having the any.do moment button on every screen.

title: Want to love it
body:
But I just can't. There is too many things wrong with it, and it has been out too long for them not to have been fixed.  

Before you buy:

1- no way to reorder folders
2- all items automatically going in either "today" folder or "personal folder" 
3- no difference between due date and alarm!  So if you have an event on Sunday but want a reminder before, like every other To Do / Calender app... Nope!
4- also no recurring alerts
5- events/tasks added to sister app "Cal" do not sync with any.Do. (Any.Do tasks sync with cal but purely for viewing - you can't do ANYTHING with them in Cal)

I've written the devs and confirmed all these problems.  They simply say sorry, no assurance that things will be fixed.  

However that's ok bc a quick scroll through this review will show you that those who wait on these devs are always disappointed.

I want to love any.Do, I really do...  I just can't.  It's one update from greatness but I don't think that one update is coming.  Seems like the devs are happy with leaving the app 90% complete.

title: App designer says OK!
body:
I am a graphic designer, mainly app interface, some web, and print. I love this app because it does a few things excellently. 

I constantly download and test apps as design research. I make it a point to find my favorite app in each category and test every feature.

I have tested several other apps and found them to be too heavy and have excessive or clunky interfaces. Wunderlist is too heavy and you have to pay. The native to do app is good functionality wise but has an outdated interface. And doesn't integrate with the calendar. 

I don't remember the old font but I love the minimal interface. This font looks fine and I know that oftentimes legibility is pressed over aesthetics so that may be a reason but nonetheless still the best looking to do app. Any do understands were apps are going and is predictive of future trends occurring in iOS 7. Say what you want about the minimalism or the flatness but I think it's for the better. 

The functionality of merging with contacts is great as well. I only eish it could integrate with siri possibly by linking with the native to do app. I hear people complain about lack of certain features but the features they complain about really belong in a calendar app, which any do has just designed! 

It's my personal favorite calendar app and I find the interface a bit more intuitive than tempo and definitely more aesthetically pleasing. They are still working out a few bugs however. 

TLDR: Best minimal to do app. Does the few things a to do list should do really well. Looks beautiful. 

Also download cal. The new calendar app by any do.

title: Decent replacement for Astrid
body:
What I like:
- Quick input options using pull down or single tap of + next to folder/date 
- voice-to-text input option more accurate than Siri for me)
- Tasks due tomorrow become today's automatically as do yesterday's undone ones
- reminders based on location awareness or time
- any.do moment to review & schedule your tasks for the day
- collaboration function to share tasks with address book contact(s) 
- automatic (mostly) contacts integration on created tasks (how it recognized when I inputed "ask Name..." on a task and gives a "talk" icon next to task that gives option to call, text, or email that contact which is very cool but doesn't seem to work for names in the business field in address book, only individuals)
- calendar/folder landscape view (with some caveats like lack of full editing capability & how some of my iCal calendar events don't show)
- clean, uncluttered and pretty easy to understand interface
- synchronization across devices works fine (I use iPhone native app on both iPhone and iPad)
- shake motion to slide completed tasks off current list and into archives

What I'd like to see:
- a tasks due "This Week" view
- make date display uniform throughout app (in reminder time/date setting area it displays as dd.mm.yyyy but not in actual scrolling chooser or on reminder-set task itself when it's mm/dd/yyyy)
- option to delete useless personal folder or at least a quick way to pick different folder/date on a pull down task creation
- create new task in any.do moment
- any.do weekly moment
- share tasks by folder (loved this is Astrid so husband and I could keep a running honey-do list going)
- fix contact task line bug so it will "sense" and connect to contacts with names using 'business' address book field
- fix bugs mentioned in landscape mode
- iPad/universal app would be nice!
- option to delete unwanted task (not archive like actual completed tasks!)

Best of all 8am every morning Any.do brings everything I have added to it and literally forces me to commit to scheduling, deferring, or doing the task at hand. I think it took me two days to find my flow with the app. I'm looking forward to their upcoming mail and notes app. Their calendar app Cal has already replaced my iPhone calendar app. Why not 5 stars? Agreed with most other reviewers. Would love the old font back, as well as the option to reorder folders, and possibly even prioritize them. Also, would LOVE to be able to share an entire folder with another user, and not just individual tasks. Being able to sync something like a grocery list with my wife, and still have separate user accounts would be so helpful. 
All in all, have tried multiple list apps, and have still landed back with any.do. Most consistent and fastest syncing across desktop and mobile so far. Thanks!

Wish list to get it to 4 stars

- iPad version. But I can live with 2x on iPhone version. 
- ability to add photo to a task. Particularly useful when price comparing at retail store. 
- ability to make a call from the app if there's a phone # in the task. (Surprising so many apps still miss this)
- archive completed task vs delete only

title: Perfect for my workflow
body:
I've used Omni Focus for almost 2 years now and I've always been annoyed that I have to add a due date to a task for it to show up in the forecast. And I don't want "vacuum the car" to show up as overdo just because I didn't get to it on the exact day I originally assigned to it.

Any.DO solves this for me. I still use OmniFocus for ongoing projects and some recurring tasks. (I use the classic "list on the fridge" for daily/weekly routines.) But I now use Any.DO for one-off tasks without hard deadlines.

Any.DO is *perfect* for that use. I love that "today" tasks just roll over instead of identifying as overdue. But of course any old list (app or paper) does that. Any.DO also let's me add tasks to Tomorrow, Upcoming, and Someday and have them move up with the passage of time. And it also has a beautiful interface.

UPDATE:

Maybe this isn't new but the call/email/text feature is so cool! I just added a task "text Pat about the dog" and there was a little icon which, when touched, pulled up a message composition screen with the recipient field already filled.

title: Great, but not perfect
body:
Great interface and lots of great features. Voice recognition is solid, auto-complete suggestions are good, and the contextual actions--a "Call" task with a contact name gives you a button to initiate the call from the app--are gold. Love the ability to remind myself to email and then start typing the email with one tap. It would be great if these buttons appeared in the task view that appears when you open a notification--not just "Done," "Snooze," and "Delete."

*UPDATE* Now even better. Sub-task functionality exists with the "Notes" feature. And the additional features in Landscape mode (plus Calendar integration!) really take this great app another step forward.

New Snooze straight from the lock screen notification is a welcome addition, and the layout of the notes improved as well. Also, the Gmail/Chrome extension is amazing.

**UPDATE** The Any.DO Moment is a fantastic addition--a great way to quickly plan your day and shift tasks around. Repeated tasks are also finally here and well-implemented.

The app does seem a bit sluggish lately (iPhone 4), but stability is improved. I would love to see increased URL scheme support (like a new task URL and x-callback-url) in the future.

title: Used to be awesome
body:
Update- from 5 to 2 stars.  You broke it with the attempt to adequately interface any.do with cal, a separate app, instead of integrate them into one.  The release was premature and the operation is glitchy at best, and eventually is likely to freeze one or more of the apps and lock you out. It became such a nuisance to deal with the problems, I deemed any.do and cal both a total loss and got rid of them.  It did help me realize I need more than just a basic list keeper, however.  My replacement works very nicely and has everything I need in a single app, including an outstanding calendar nicely integrated into other intuitive yet multifaceted and totally customizable features. If all you need is a basic list keeper, any.do is okay, but for the vast majority of us who need more in our life management aids, it falls way short and is vastly overrated.  Don't be fooled by a deceivingly slick appearing user interface.
.…..................
If I had to give up every app except one, this is what I'd keep. It is the best of its kind available in any format.  Indispensable and who really cares about little font modifications.  Make it highly functional and stable (sometimes crashes but never lose anything) and that is what counts.  Would suggest some fine tuning of the any moment making reassigned finish targets show up right away more consistently for us procrastinators.  Also more features for the calendar for future dates that work similar to the main module would be great for some day. Still, without changing a thing, I find it to be outstanding.  Thank you for creating it!

title: Beautiful, but missing features for serious workflow
body:
Seriously. Beautiful and a joy to use.  And paired with their app, Cal, it's even more awesome. If you use a to-do app to help you remember to do stuff, Any.do is brilliant. 

If you rely on your to-do app to help manage your life, Any.do falls short. 

First, selecting a due date is a pain. For dates more than a few days in advance, you have to use the scrolling date picker. It's a pain. Things has an awesome due date selection. (However it does not offer reminders like Any.do.)

Second, speaking my to-dos is nice, but I have to open the app. I do this all the time, so that's kind of a pain. Omnifocus and Things let me add tasks via Siri on the iPhone. 

No iPad app, but I can run the iPhone app in my iPad, so that works fine, and the Chrome browser extension turns Any.do into a web app accessible from anywhere. This is huge. Things and Omnifocus don't do this. 

And finally, the plan your day experience, Moment, is amazingly awesome. 

If you use a task manager, Any.do is highly recommended for anyone, along with Cal. If your life relies on a task manager, adding a task is just inefficient enough to overcome the excellent parts of the experience. 

However, if Any.do we're to improve due date selection or make it easy to add tasks verbally (or if Cal added the ability to enter conference call codes with a click, like Tempo) THEN THIS WOULD E THE GREATEST APP THE WORLD HAS EVER SEEN.
author: Austin Govella

title: Cute but not ready
body: The app is cute and works if you don't have a lot of to do's, but it falls apart quickly when you try to use it for real. Once a date is associated with a task, there is no way to remove that date (to move it to someday category). Dragging to someday is beyond painful once the list size grows. In date view, the tasks have no concept of folders. In folder view, the tasks have no concept of dates. Editing is awkward to exit from. Priority is a non-existing concept. There's not enough features to make this app workable, coupled with awkward UI, you end up with an app that perhaps makes a good starting point, but needs a lot of work before it's ready for prime time. It is NOT a suitable replacement for Astrid. You'd have to take a major downgrade.

title: Why the ugly font?

On to more functional aspects: I'm still disappointed by the categories.  I loved having today, tomorrow, this week, and later.  Now, this week and later are all in one category together -upcoming.  I was hoping this would be brought back to the app by now.  I wanted this app to help me keep track of home work and other school deadlines, and the way this date view is set up does not work for me for that cause.  I use Wunderlist for all my school stuff, the viewing isn't as clean cut, but all the functions are there.  I now use this for personal tasks only.

Then tap "grocery list" and the Notes icon and start adding things to your grocery list. How much easier can it be? 

It's so easy to use I've just finished moving everything from Clear to Any.DO. From now on Any.DO is my go-to to-do list app.

title: Ready to abandon other ToDo apps
body:
I love ToDo list apps in general but so far none of them really stuck with me enough to become my permanent daily assistant in order to achieve my goals. 

Usually, their cumbersome UI, steps  and some learning curve turn me off and I stop using the apps, and then I go back to the analog world of pen and post-it, which for me is probably the most efficient way to get things done.

Then recently I came across Any.DO.
Any.Do is so well thought-out. The developer must have worked really hard to get this simple. I really appreciate the simplicity of inputting to-do's. I also like the landscape view, where the app lays out what's ahead for you with calendar. 

Overall, I'm very happy that I found this app, and I'm ready to stick with it. The only thing was the Any.DO moment animation...really didn't understand the concept and crashes the app when run.

title: Finally a task-mgmt app I keep using
body:
I have very short attention, so it's key that my task-management app be:

1. Easy to enter tasks (ie very few fields to fill out)

2. Easy to maintain. 

Any.do really sets itself apart from all others on both points. Love that I don't have to pick real dates -- only today, tomorrow, or someday. Super simple. Brilliant. 

And I REALLY love that you begin your day with a quick, prompted review of what I completed or missed. This is a killer feature because it saves me tons of keystrokes and time which would have led me to abandon the app. No more editing each task to change the dates and no cutting and pasting a list from day to day. Super simple. Brilliant. 

And the app is so beautiful too -- makes it easy to want to use it.  I'm gonna try their cal app now too.

title: Lack of Find Feature Drags Down A Beautiful App
body:
Before you buy this App know this.  There is no ability to find tasks.

I've tried them all in search of the perfect task manager.  I thought I had found Nirvana with Any.DO, only to discover that it lacks the simple and essentially ability to find tasks.  You have a task manager because you have a lot of tasks, and want to save time managing them.  Lack of a find feature wastes your time looking for tasks.  This becomes more of an issue the more tasks you add.  For example, sometimes you can't remember if you have already added a task.  Without find, your options are to waste time scrolling through your entire list, or hope it is already on the list.  Not an ideal situation.

When I informed the developer they needed this, the reply was "they would consider it".  This is akin to considering whether you need to eat every day.

Its a shame that the lack of a find function turns what is otherwise a 5 Star App into an also ran.  The interface, concept, implementation and the Chrome Web Extension are awesome, but useless for anyone with lots of tasks due to lack of a find function.  In fairness to the developer, if you have a small number of tasks, this is easily the best to do manager, and a 5 star app.
