title: Great in theory, but some flaws in execution
body:
I've long used "Do It (Tomorrow)" as a very quick, simple, intuitive to-do list. It doesn't have a lot of bells and whistles (no alarms, no calendar), but I've found it to be very effective- eventually, I get so sick of pushing tasks to tomorrow that I just do them so I don't have to anymore. When I saw that Any.do had all of my must-haves from Tomorrow.do (good sync, a nice web app, and the any.do moment feature provides the same effect as Tomorrow's push-to-tomorrow feature), along with a few extra goodies (alarms, reminders, recurring tasks), I decided to give it a try. 

The extra features are certainly nice, and if any.do worked perfectly, it'd be the clear winner. Unfortunately, it doesn't. First, my beloved recurring tasks feature causes the app to crash at least once a day. The recovery is always quick, and no data is ever lost, so this is the least of my 3 complaints. It's no more than a minor annoyance, but contrasts poorly with Tomorrow, which did exactly what it was supposed to without issue or exception 100% of the time. I've also had quick crashes on the Chrome web app. Again, no harm done, but it does make the app feel less stable and polished. My second issue is that when I mark off a recurring task, it always transfers to the next day fine, but it sometimes loses its recurring status. This is also an annoyance (as I have to re-enable recurring status), but it's also something that could lead to me not doing something I need to do because I forgot to make it recurring again. For a to-do list, losing tasks or creating a risk that something doesn't get done is the cardinal sin. My third problem is with the any.do moment feature. While it's a fantastic feature, as far as I can tell, it's limited to just 16 tasks at a time. That's all well and good, but my task list usually runs 40 items long. This, for me, is a non-starter. The mechanism of every morning looking at my list and deciding what to do and what to push off is by far the most important thing for me. That's what motivates me to stop procrastinating and clear some of those items out. 

There are a couple of other complaints, but they're mostly aesthetic. I can't imagine why sorting by date doesn't also sort by time (putting items with earlier alarms at the top and items with later alarms at the bottom). As I said, I sometimes have a long task list, and it seems crazy to me that I have to constantly scroll through it hunting to find whatever I have scheduled to do next. I wish you could sort by folder and date simultaneously (so, for instance, if I go to my "appointments" folder, the one coming up soonest appears at the top). I think both of these are such common sense features that I can't understand why they weren't in place way back in Beta. I think the random voice that sometimes shouts things at me is bizarre, and I'd love to be able to turn it off. I think it's supposed to be some positive reinforcement for completing tasks, but checking something off (especially something that's been on the list a long time) is all the positive reinforcement I need. What I need is for my phone to stop startling me by shouting random things when I'm only half paying attention. Finally, I never saw the old font, but also agree that the current one is rather uninspiring, and again suffers in comparison to Do It (Tomorrow). 

Any.do is still a very good to-do app. With enough continued polish and improvements, it could easily be the best. In it's current form, though, there are too many minor annoyances and little inconveniences. I was so excited when I first tried it, thinking for sure I had found the long-term solution to my task management needs. I went out of my way to try to make it work, even going so far as to store half of my to-do list in a different app and combining several recurring tasks into a single mega task so I could get under the 16-item limit on the any.do moment. Finally, I gave up and acknowledged it's not what I'm looking for. For now, I'm going back to Do It (Tomorrow), which is limited, but extremely effective and powerful, and which is by far the most polished task manager I have yet seen. I'll keep an eye on any.do, and may even continue using it to track appointments (Tomorrow's biggest weakness, since there are no alarms and you can't schedule more than 1 day in advance). Hopefully future updates will resolve some of these issues, in which case I'll gladly give them a second chance.

title: No thanks
body:
I'd been looking for a To-do app that synchs with my google calendar. Something that I can list all of my tasks, whenever they pop in my head, and puts them on my calendar. That doesn't seem to be asking too much, is it? Guess again.

First of all, when you install it and request to synch with your Google calendar, it tells you that it will access your browsing info. Why in the world is this necessary? How far does it go? Is it going to be pulling my payment info, products purchased, browsing history? This alone almost made me give up with this app.

Then, when I was adding tasks, and tried to enter the location of a meeting, I was told that to access this "premium" function, I had to invite friends. Premium? Really? If I can't even enter a location of a task, what good is a To-Do app? Are you trying to not add users by not making the app accessible? So far, so good.

Finally, when I did try to synch with my Google calendar, nothing appeared in my calendar. Maybe I didn't do something right. But it shouldn't be this hard. 

App looks nice, but doesn't make people want to go to all the trouble of using it. If the objective is to get users on to another app, mission accomplished.

title: Go to app for reminders and tasks
body: Recurring reminders (daily, weekly, monthly). Syncs with Google tasks; and, across platforms, so changes made on my Droid can be seen on my corporate iPad and vice versa. Alerts aren't missed regardless of which device I happen to be holding. Chrome extension adds to the versatility. "Any.do moment" serves as a daily morning reminder for what is on your to-do list for the day. Notes can be synced by folder or due date. If you grant access to your contacts it can auto-complete names in reminders as you create them. Swipe to complete is easy and intuitive for modern UI's. Calendar view helps at-a-glance viewing for upcoming tasks over time. Location based reminders help for times when you need to do something at a specific place, but you're unsure of when you'll be there.

title: Updated Review :(
body:
Update: Crashes every time I first open it, when I add a new task, set a reminder. Always have to reopen to finish anything. The reminders have a mind if their own and are practically useless. And petty, but the new UI isn't as pretty as the old one (and I'm not a person who minds change... it's just not as pretty). Going back to the native Reminders until they fix the reminders and crashing issues. and yes... I'm fully updated on app version and iOS. too bad... used to be a great simple app, now they're trying to get too sexy with it. 

Beautiful design and easy to use. It's very "common sense" in it's control (hold and drag to rearrange, tap titles to open options, etc.). Only wish I have for it: location reminders like the native iPhone app. I love having a reminder go off when I get home or to wherever, and this lacks that... If they can add it, definite 5 star app!

title: Where the heck did the awsome font go?
body:
I haven't tooled around with the update too much but whatever positive changes were made have been overshadowed by the new heavy font for me. It's kind of like leaving my Mac at home and having to come in to work on windows all over again, except I can't go back to my Mac OS interface.

This app used to do 2 things. Kept my lists organized the way I want ... and was nice to look at while I was doing this somewhat unwanted task. It's now just functional and not much fun. I'll probably see if there is another app that looks nicer now.

Can we have an option for the old font??

Old review:
Work well and has a nice UI. Pretty intuitive. The only reason I'm not giving a 5 is because I haven't seen a way to remove the the 'personal' folder. This gets in the way since I don't use it and don't seem to see a way to rename it.

Overall this is a great app for me though. I keep folders for stuff I want to get done around the house on weeknights after work and on weekends. U can add alarms etc I I want too. Before, I would always have some time come up and i would not remember all of the odd jobs and tasks i wanted to get done when I had a minute. Now I write stuff down when I think of it and look at the list when I have a chance to do something on it. I keep a custom older of quick stuff to do on weeknights after work and bigger stuff to get done sometime over the weekend.

Would recommend for custom lists and someone who wants a easy fun user interface.

title: CHANGE THE FONT BACK!!
body:
Overall I love this app; it is clean, simple in its functionality, intuitive, and practical. 

With that said, I think the latest updates made a visual error on the font change. The previous choice was modern, elegant, and became distinctly "Any.Do." As a result, it carried Any.Do's visual identity. The change not only takes away that highly idiosyncratic element of the UI, and Any.Dos visual independence to the user, but chose a font that is thick and harder to read in all caps. It is as if there was a desire to follow the crowd and get some thing that was "more Helvetica." CHANGE THE FONT BACK PLEASE!!

I am also crossing my fingers for Greek language options. 

All in all, keep up the good work, and please don't overcomplicate this beautifully simple app with the perceived need for "more features." Instead, focus you energies on making more simple, focused, and beautiful products to stand by Any.Do's side.

The newest version of this app introduced the Any.DO Moment which walks you through your to dos for the day one by one, allowing you to set reminders, snooze until another day, or mark as done. I shouldn't need help reviewing the day ahead and planning a course of action, but I guess I do. It's a wonderful help. Another great feature if this app is its integration into my desktop Chrome and Gmail. LOVE. I get an email and at the bottom of it am able to write a to do that goes right onto my Any.DO list. So slick and efficient! This app just gets better and better!

UPDATE: The recent font change was a disappointment, maybe they'll let us pick between? Either way the functionality is great and the design simple. Still my favorite!

title: Still crashes
body: I've emailed and tweeted the developers multiple times, but never got a response. Unfortunately, the crashes persist after 4 months waiting for this new version. I set a recurring daily task, and when I mark that task done for the day, the app crashes. When I relaunch it, the task appears for the next day, but the recurrence is gone. A new issue is that if I set a reminder to take out the trash for "when I arrive" home, and set the time for 6:30 pm, it will remind me EVERY TIME I come home, regardless of the time I set. So you have to either set a time OR location, not both (even though it lets you do both). Finally, this is a persistent one - when I add a new task, it sets a time. I don't want a time, so I hit the X to remove it, but the X doesn't work the first time. Sometimes it takes 4-5 times. I was holding out to see if these issues would be resolved, but since there is no way to get through to the developers, I'm looking elsewhere. I'm on an iPhone 5 with the latest iOS btw.

title: This Task Manager is Worth Trying
body:
Update: Any.do continues to be my go to task manager. Try it, learn it and you will love it. This iPhone/ iPod app works well on the iPad and sync's flawlessly.

Any.Do should fit the needs of most people.
The simplicity is deceiving. Explore to get the most out of the app - use Landscape mode for calendar, use bottom pull-up for more options, microphone icon for voice entry.
I am using it with my iPad and iPod without problems for a month.
Same format on both devices, did not bother me
Really like "voice entry" - NOTE: network access required for this feature.  Very accurate - what a time saver.
Any.Do is more than a reminder list, but if you need a full featured task manager, try Things.
When you discover the features, Any.Do will wow you.
From the support page, look for more features are in the future.

title: Excellent Productivity App!
body:
This app is wonderful! I use Any.DO both on my iPad and as a Chrome extension on my Macs. It is one of my favorite productivity tools and and I use it in conjunction with some other software and services to make my life worth living and I am now the envy of all my neighbors!

I would give this a 4.5 instead of the 4 you see above except that the AppStore doesn't seem to like halfsies. I've reluctantly rounded down because I think there is a feature that really needs improvement.

The fact that I can enter recurring tasks is fantabulous and I use it often, but the recurrence feature needs to be more robust. As it stands there are only four preset choices, to wit: once a day, once a week, once a month, once a year. (There are five choices if you count "None" as a choice.)

My work around is to set a weekly task to remind me to check the date to see if this is when my "every other week" task should be performed. It's an unfortunate missing avian in the wonderful row of ducks that is Any.DO and I hope it will be corrected quickly in a future update.

Even with the single issue I have mentioned I must say that I truly do recommend people use Any.DO.

A very simple section, with the most recent date at the top. Enabling you to keep track of accomplishments each day. It would be great if it went back To the beginning of the app being used.

UPDATE: Wow I continue to use this wonderful app, I have found some other wonderful ones. MyQuests, Getodo, Ita and Productev all work well for certain applications. (I am not a Clear user.) 

I also found a solution with two apps in order to keep track of achievements. Do It Tomorrow and it's sister app Today work together to achieve this, Though you have to pay for cloud syncing to get this feature
DOOO also does this really well, and the layout is exactly the one I had in mind.

title: The search for a sync friendly app stops here
body:
I never write reviews for apps, but I'm making an exception because this one is so good.

I'm a list guy, and the idea of moving from paper & pen to electronic record keeping was nice, but never effective in practice. I have two phones, personal and work, and AnyDo syncs flawlessly so it doesn't matter which one I have with me. The desktop application is also great to easily type in a list of things at once for me to work with later.

The interface is remarkably clean, intuitive and simple enough that it doesn't bog you down. The calendar works well enough and it's easy enough to organize by activity or time.

One thing that has worked great so far is turning some of my tasks into "projects" by listing the more detailed steps or actions within the notes.

The only things I would say to change/add is including Firefox support (or a desktop client app) and to extend task descriptions rather than having ellipses... or maybe make that an option! It does this for the take notes automatically, so it shouldn't be too hard :)

Great app guys, I'm a tough critic, but for now, Any.Do is the top to-do list for me!

author: AlexHearn

title: Made the cut
body:
This is the most well thought out perfect sleek amazing app of all times. From the effective chrome extension to the sci fi font I adore this app. I have (like most of you) an extensive music collection forcing me down to 3 or 4 apps. This made the cut. It's subtlety encouraging, but not pretentious. I love striking through things on my to do list physically. And the categories keep me from feeling overwhelmed by the future (other apps have a calendar up in your face) whilst allowing appointments and the like to be remembered with reminders. And if you want to change it up? Change the colors. Go from Annakin to dark vader (minus the lava)

What to do today?
Praise The Lord for this app

I only wish there was more colors

title: Love it - I use it every day
body:
One of the main reasons I was so interested in an iPhone was to utilize apps in order to help me get organized. After trying out and testing several check list apps, this is the one I'm finally committing to. Easy to use and simple. It's exactly what I needed. Nothing more nothing less. Make lists, add to your lists, swipe items off lists when done. No ads, no garbage. LOVE IT!

title: Best iOS calendar app. Needs Mac app.
body:
I'm AADD and self-employed. I NEED a ToDo app. I've tried them all: Things, Steps, Clear, Sooner, Orchestra, Carrot, Wunderlist,  and this is easily my favorite due to the intuitive and gorgeous UI, smart features like repeating tasks, speech to text input, location and context aware reminders and the ability to share lists with collaborators. 

What I like most is the lightness of it no matter how it's used. The other apps either felt too complicated (Things, Orchestra), were in fact too simplistic to do everything I need (Clear) or just felt kludgy and wrong somehow. I know that's not 

Any.DO nails the between too many features and not enough. But even more than that, it eliminates or comes as close to eliminating that feeling of Am I forgetting to do something with this ToDo list? as any app I've used to date. 

I can make a simple list of all my tasks in one place like Clear or I can nest them in complicated project folders with different deadlines and collaborators like Things without feeling like I'm using the software wrong or not getting the most of it.  It's always right just the way it is, with the next move, if I  want it, right there where I expect it to be. It's a very reassuring app. 

The only reason it gets 4 stars instead of 5 is the lack of a full-fledged Mac app. I use Chrome. I have the extension. I just don't like it. 

If the Any.DO people came up with a Mac app that sat in my menu bar, cost less than $100, synced with iCal/Fantastical, and worked just like the iOS version, I would literally stop paying attention to all other ToDo app development.

title: This is the BEST
body:
We all have some kind of fetish, well, mine is finding the perfect organizational tool. For years I used paper, and it was great. Franklin Covey worked for me. Then my Palm Pilot filled in just perfectly. However, when it came to organizational smartphone apps, my search has continued for years...until now. 

Calengoo is good; RTM is alright; Things is expensive, but Any.do is PERFECT. That's all I can say. It has all of the prerequisites such as syncing with Google Tasks, it has desktop extensions (the one for Google Chrome is especially nice), and it's beautiful on my Samsung S3 and my iPhone...yes, I have both, long story. I like the simplicity and the clean lines of the UI, and I love the way it asks me every morning, in a beautiful and subtle manner, if I would like to plan my day. If I say yes, then it runs down my list of tasks and I check off what I have done and what I still need to do, and when I do this each day at 5:15am, I appreciate the graceful and beautiful way rung hides me through what I need to get done for the day. Any.do then stays with me throughout the day as I either accomplish my goals or reschedule them. 

I don't work for the company. I don't know the developer. I'm just a very busy high school history teacher whose day is filled with energy, and appointments, and lessons, and meetings...and Any.do is there to help me get it done. I have literally been looking for a planning system since I had to retire my Palm Pilot almost 10 years ago and with Any.do, I have found it!

title: Love this app!
body:
I've checked out my fair share of productivity apps - I'm a list making fiend! I HAVE to make lists to keep my days & goals on track. Most apps have too many steps involved, too much clicking, & complexity. This app lets me do everything I want, & it lets me do it on a clean & simple interface in a few simple clicks. My 2 favorite features are the Any.Do Moment of the Day feature (&the fact that you can have an alarm on that) & the feature that lets you turn the phone sideways & see the calendar & allows you to EASILY maneuver when you're going to complete a task.

1. Any.Do Moment of the Day: I always take time to plan when I'm going to accomplish said to-do's in my today list but this app prompts me to do that AND helps me do it easily. It serves as somewhat of a reality check. When you actually plan when you'll do each item, it sometimes hits you that you put too much on your plate for one day.

2. The sideways view: I love that it lets me see at a glance how busy my week is. And when I want to change due dates, I don't want to have to click 16 times, I just want to hold and drag to when I wanna do it - & that's exactly what this feature lets me do.

Great work, developers!! Really love it :)

3 things I wish it had:
1. A repeat function on tasks
2. A way to sort &/or filter your to-dos (I.e. alphabetically by category)
3. A way to search your to-do list

It is something that lists tasks as important and urgent, important and not urgent, unimportant and urgent, and unimportant and not urgent. title: Simple and easy!
body: I have not been using this app for long (just downloaded it last week), but so far I'm loving it. Most organizer apps make you fit things into a calendar format, programming times of the day and everything. This one simply labels things, "Today, Tomorrow, Upcoming, Someday," so now I don't need to schedule an EXACT TIME to do a task. This is great for people like me who have flip-flopping work schedules, who can't always guarantee I'll be free at the scheduled time on calendar apps. It's also good for planning way ahead. The "Someday" section is great for when I need a reminder to pack certain things when I travel, though my trips won't happen for months. Overall, I find this app simple and easy to use, along with being well-designed and aesthetically pleasing.

To Do apps are a dime a dozen and are probably the most competitive apps in the store. I have the Omni app, Things and a few others which I have picked up over the years. This one is quickly becoming my favorite because it is so easy to use. The voice dictation is in need of improvement as it can not distinguish between 'right' and 'write' within the context of the sentence. The drag & drop, shake to clear completed tasks are but a few features that work nicely. I wish for this App to make it to the Mac App Store and the iPad with iCloud syncing. This rating will drop significantly if they end up charging for syncing and increased cost for the pending apps. Please don't go there with this very functional and easy to use app. 
Room to improve but with a great foundation to start.

title: Not bad
body: I do love the simplicity of this app's design. However, I want to suggest a couple things: one is to format the input/view of text so that it runs on multiple lines instead of the first couple words and then an ellipses ("....") That way tasks are more convenient to see when you first open the app and when you type tasks in (It's really awkward typing in ONE CONTINUOUS line). Then there should also be more of a "priority" option; maybe having the text in red AND capitals if its urgent and just red if its not as urgent. Compared to iPhone's default app, Reminders, Any.Do is...well, not bad. The looks are sleek, user friendly, but I think they could do better! Overall, I'm still glad that I found this app!

body: It's improved since I first downloaded but a few things drive me crazy.  You cant have recurring tasks. You can't access the calendar in portrait view.  While you are in landscape you cannot edit tasks.  When alarms go off, he banner goes away quickly if you are actively using the phone and choose not to click on it.  You can't snooze if you are busy.  If you want to cross it off, you click the banner and it takes you out of the app you are in and takes you to any.do, Then it leaves you there. When you cross something off, it stays in the folder it was in which would be better than disappearing (like it used to) but you cant edit it or uncross it.  It should dump into a completed or trash folder.  I keep updating this app and giving it another try and I spend more time scrolling around. I would love to be able to search for a task but its the other stuff I tear my hair out over.  Maybe the Any.do Moment will be better but I spend even more time managing tasks than I did using the built in apps.

title: A few suggestions
body:
I've tried many to-do apps and this is my favorite. 
A few suggestions though:
1. When entering in a time for something under Tomorrow, the date should default to tomorrow and not today. I've had a few things accidentally get put in my today stuff which is a bit annoying.
2. After swiping to cross out something that's completed, I'd rather it just stay in its same place on my list instead of dropping to the bottom. Most of the time I swipe to cross out and immediately want to X it out as well, it's annoying having to wait and chase it to the bottom of the list.
3. Is there a way to edit the date/time of an entry? I'm guessing that I'm missing how to do it, if its possible it's at least not intuitive enough for me to find even with some searching for that function.

Overall a great app, I'd personally love to see these small improvements but that's just my opinion.

title: We want an iPad version, and Siri
body:
Let me be clear, this is the best task organizer I have ever used. The iPhone app is flawless.

But, I really wish their was an iPad version with cloud syncing so I could finish tasks on my iPad and then check them off without having to go find my phone.

Also, I wish it worked with Siri. I imagine there is some juggernaut bureaucracy preventing the developer from doing so, but I hope they'll pursue it the best they can. Wolfram alpha, yelp, and open table did it, so can you. 

I am only so critical with my ratings because I see enormous potential for the app. I know my 2 stars won't be detrimental when lumped into the thousands of ratings this app has. BUT I hope it caught the attention of the developer so that they will pursue these lofty goals. 

Thanks for the best free app I've ever downloaded!

title: Superb! Simple, minimal & functional.
body:
Thanks for a great, simple, minimal & functional app. 

I love that you can call, email or text someone directly from within the app with just a tap on your task/reminder. 

Design is superb. Not heavy or cluttered. Great landscape layout. Very smart & slick!

SUGGESTIONS 
I suggest adding the following to make it heads & shoulders above the rest:

1. Ability to attach pictures & audio to your notes or tasks. This is so helpful for reference. 

2. Multiple reminders on same day. Need this to follow up on something important, so that if it's not done, it doesn't get forgotten. 

3. Native iPad app.

title: Right on little app!
body:
This app is sleek, intuitive and fun to use; all while offering users different  organizational display options -customizable to your liking!

I like the ability to view all categories (or dates-depending on your preference) all on one screen. 

Love the date choices: Today, Tomorrow, Upcoming and Someday.

Big bonus in visual aides is that next to each listing there are small blue icons for what type of task you've set. For example, make a call is a phone and text msg is a thought bubble. This makes it easy to be reminded on each task quickly.

I don't like that there is a preloaded folder, named Personal, in which you are unable to delete. You can create and/or delete as many folders as you like, except for this preloaded Personal folder. That bugs me because I don't use it.

I don't understand about the email reminders, sometimes that come through and other times they don't. I'd like that to be consistent.

Also wish there were different "reminder" sound options and the ability to set two alarms per listing.

Lastly, this app would be a 10 star if it was able to sync into my iCalander in a way where I was able to see it as a side listing per day; like a check list.

All-in-all I'd absolutely recommend this app! It has helped me stay more organized and productive! Thanks!!

title: Fabulous
body:
This is an excellent to-do app. I especially love its cross-platform availability.

The really killer feature for me, though, is the "Any.DO moments" (which desperately need a better name, to be honest). I can tell it to trigger at specific times on specific days of the week and it will go through my lists and have me set due dates.

This lets me easily take the first hour or two of my day to think about the things I'd like to accomplish. Then later, it will force me to set some deadlines. I find this to be an excellent workflow.

I'm giving this app 4/5 stars because there is ALWAYS room for improvement. I will not placate the developers by handing them a "perfect job". The app is fantastic, but they should always strive to do better. I highly recommend this app and can't wait to see what else it becomes in the future!

title: Incredibly picky when it comes to "To Do" lists
body: I've tried so many To-Do lists and none of them ever please me. I usually write out lists, but I waste so much paper making lists on a daily basis. This is the first app I have used that I am actually happy with. It is simple in its design, usage, and features. You simply just input what you want for your to do list, pick a folder (if you want. I have three: personal, work, and school.), set a time and location, create a note about it, set an alarm for it, make it high priority (turns the text red), and I guess 'tag' your contacts to them. The only feature I use is picking a folder. You can categorize your 'to-do's' by "Today" "Tomorrow" "Upcoming" and "Someday" which is BRILLIANT AND SIMPLE. This is perfect. There are things that I have to do tomorrow, and then there are things that can wait a few days so I really love the "upcoming" section. I don't really have much in Someday because I'm more of a 'Do-It-Now' type of person so I have my long term goals and dreams in here (ex: Vacation to Seoul & Tokyo). When you are done with a task, you simply cross it off the list. It will turn gray, or you can press a little 'x' next to it to completely remove it. The app also keeps a tally of your completed tasks. You can also view all your 'To-Do's' in a folder view which is useful. You can also see your completed tasks and delete them if you'd like. The only thing I dislike (a bit) about this app, is that it moves up tasks with day/week changes. It is useful for tasks I have to do for tomorrow, because when it becomes the next day they move to "today." That's actually really convenient. What I don't like is after a week goes by it moves the items under "Upcoming" to "today/tomorrow." I prefer if they stay in upcoming because they are small things that  aren't too important like "fix necklace" or "scan photos;" however, it's not too bothersome that I would not want to use this app. They also have a really convenient add-on if you use Google Chrome. So if you're extremely picky like me and want something simple then go with this great app!

title: Visually appealing, fluid, but not very useful and seems invasive
body:
App Version 1.7.2
iPhone 5, iOS 6.0.2
2013 January 07 :: Initial Review :: Two Stars

This app is very pretty and is fluid in its function. However, there are no Repeat functions as found in the Apple Reminders app which is built into the iPhone. The voice recognition works well but makes me leery because it evidently uses a web based interface to interpret the speech, which means that this third party has access to all of your transcribed to-do list items. (When Siri is disabled it still works but when Wi-Fi and Cellular Data are disabled it does not.) I am glad that it does not require you to create an account to use it like many other apps do, such as Orchestra, Producteev, WorkFlowy, and Cozi. However, this app is invasive as evidenced by Banners and Alerts still showing up in the Lock and Home screens even after the app is removed from the list of "In Notification Center" apps. Somehow it has worked around the iOS on this. The only way to prevent this is to both remove it from the Notification Center AND select Off for the View in Lock Screen option under the app's Notification Center options. Because of the lack of Repeat functionality, the risk of lack of privacy, and the apparent invasive nature of this app I gave it two stars and deleted it. So far I have found the Apple Reminders app more useful for the same functions that Any.Do offers and an app called "Errands" to be a decent app for to-do items that repeat on a day basis. (I.e. Every second Tuesday of the month. This is a Repeat function that the Apple Reminders does not currently offer.)

Dr. Evan Sundgren
Chiropractic Physician

body: I absolutely love Any.Do. My productivity has doubled since I started using this app. It is much better than the Reminder app that comes with the latest iOS on the iPhone. Any.Do is very functional, and it offers a very clean and user friendly look. The to-do list can be viewed by dates or customizable task folders i.e work, personal, exercise, etc. For iPhone users when you rotate your phone to change the screen orientation the app switches to a calendar view, which other top productivity apps either did not have or do as well. I standby this app.

title: Best and Simplest Task App
body:
Any.DO might not be the most powerful task app with the most features, but it has them all beat in it's simplicity and ease of use.

It has exactly what it needs, the UI and UX are extraordinary and one of the best I've seen of ANY app. 

Pull down to add a task, swipe to delete, and expand/contract folders to see what's most important.  It's drop dead simple and clean, I love everything about it!

I even love that you can send a task to someone even if they don't have the app!  And the auto-suggest is perfect.

There are a few minor improvements needed like sorting folders and editing some of the stuff that comes out of the box, but overall this is a first-class app!

title: Good design but buggy
body:
I love the simple design and way Any.Do uses gestures to move tasks and mark them as completed.  I use it all the time on my Galaxy Nexus and desktop, and it works great on both.  But the design on my iPad just makes it hard to use.  

If I put the iPad in landscape view, tapping on a task doesn't allow me to edit it or mark it as urgent.  It's also impossible to bring up the settings menu in Any.Do on the iPad without switching back to portrait view.  One of the great things about Any.Do in general is the way it simplifies prioritizing tasks by time--either I need to do it "today", "tomorrow", "this week", or "later".  But that simplicity is absent here--the only way to categorize tasks by time is to assign them to a specific date.  Finally, I would love it if the app took advantage of the iPad's screen size so I could see more tasks--that would make it way easier to move tasks between folders and days.  But alas, there's no iPad-optimized version of the app.

Any.Do has the potential to be my total go-to organization app.  But until they clean it up, I won't be using it too much on my iPad.

title: Minimal and functional, but it needs improvements
body:
In a very competitive market, Any.do stands out with its minimalism and good marketing and integration features. But when it comes to the big picture, there are a handful of of features and even minor tweaks they could offer that other Apps offer. If they did everything they did now and offer all of these features, it would be doubtful that anyone could compete with Any.do.

These features include:
•Google Calendar integration
•Setting reoccurring tasks
•Constant calendar view/mode (swipe right on the main screen to view calendar)
•Customized backgrounds( which can be done by integrating a simple RGB Color wheel) 
•The option to save multiple color themes. ( think of the color templates you can save with power point!)
•Also with the color schemes: offer the choice to change all 3 colors in Any.o (ei, the background, the link color, the priority color, the text etc etc.) 
•Google Drive integration, to pull up documents or files as reminders- setting links to files you need to work on.
•Saved "memory" so the next time you type out a task it remembers a task you did before and auto fills it at your convenience. 
•A simple option to monitor completed task, basic analytical data that is easy for the average user to view and get info from. It would go great with setting goals to get X amount of tasks done.
•Going off of that-integrate a way to monitor customized goals.

A lot of these features are existing in a lot of to do list apps, CRM software, and calendar. Again if these features were added and integrated in the minimalistic way the app works, it would be a sure fire way to make this the bet undisputed To do list app out there.

SGM

title: Almost Perfect
body:
In one sense it deserves a 5 just by virtue of the fact that it's the best to-do app (for me) that I know of.

The most important feature for me is the ability to add to-dos using the Chrome extension which then syncs to my phone. I also love the UI.

But it's got some issues:
1) You can't delete the initial folder even after you create others.
2) That wouldn't be such a big deal if I could at least rename it, but I can't.
3) When I get rid of completed to-dos, it flashes how many to-dos I've completed since using the app. I wish it reset every day, so I saw how many tasks I was completing that day - not forever.
4) I don't even use the time view b/c it's not that easy to set up deadlines for the to-dos. Instead I use folders that represent the different quadrants of a priority matrix and ignore the time feature.
5) Would be nice if I could be given a personalized email address that would allow me to email to-dos to myself (if I were on someone else's computer for example).

All in all, EXCELLENT though - 4.5 stars.

title: No way to turn off due dates, randomly resorts Google Tasks, requires additional ID and password
body:
There is no way to disable due dates, and the poor design of this was so frustrating that I've stopped using Any.DO as much as it's otherwise a good app, and I only check Any.DO again each time there's a new version, to check whether this feature's finally been added.

The problem is that you might have tasks such as "find a better barbershop", which don't have a due date, but you want them to appear on your list in the someday/maybe category which you review once in a while when you have time. But there's no easy way to do that in this app -- no matter how you try to prevent certain tasks from eventually appearing in the "DUE TODAY" notifier, they will eventually show up there, which is counter-productive. Moving tasks to another folder doesn't prevent this, and pushing back the date manually gets frustrating quickly when you have dozens of tasks and you need to do this manually ... I pushed things back for a while, but eventually I gave up on Any.DO.

Also, Any.DO will ravage your to-do list if you sync with Google, resorting things into an order which isn't based on anything you've set up in either the app or Google Tasks.

Unfortunately, Any.DO now requires you to set up a separate Any.DO account for your tasks if you want to sync online and to other devices, which means yet another ID and password. This makes little sense because Any.DO is made by Google developers, so why doesn't it simply take your Google ID and password?

Otherwise, this app is nicely polished, and if the above limitations won't affect you, you might find it to be the most intuitive task app available.

title: Potential to be the best...
body:
As a full time college student with 2 jobs, I'm an admitted to do app junkie. But the problem with apps like Things is that when I get really busy (when I need to do lists the most), they're just too complicated/time consuming to use. 

This app is the perfect combination of function and simplicity. All the crucial functions (alarm, subtasks, calendar view, sync) are there, but there's no fuss. And the interface is very intuitive. 

If a few issues are resolved, this will be the HG of to do apps. An iPad app is a must. Also, sometimes a few of the cool features (like the landscape mode calendar and auto-population of tasks) don't work. I have to fully restart the app to get them to work. That shouldn't be happening. 

That said, I really recommend this app. And I've tried them all.

title: Beautiful app! Perfect! Stunning!
body:
I would recommend this app to absolutely everyone! It is easy and fast to use, it doesn't take up a ton of room on my 8GB iPod touch and it doesn't look confusing and cluttered !! ❤👍

The only problems I have found are that  you can't hit the microphone button when you don't have an Internet connection, so say if you don't have wifi, you have to type in your to-do's 
Also, it crashes occasionally, 

❕👉not too often but please fix these minor problems!!!!!!👈

Don't let those problems make you think that this app is annoying or doesn't work though. 
It really is a perfect app and is amazing with keeping track of everything that's in your head that you don't want to forget! 

Any.Do has a reminder/alarm that can be silent if you want, different sections for your things for today, tomorrow, this week and later. To add a reminder/thing just pull down from the top and you can type in (or speak, which listens to what you said and types it in text form) what you want and hit add, or if you want, add a reminder, date/time or make it a higher priority ( makes text color red )

I hope you get this app 😊

title: Brilliant, if a tad buggy
body:
As a hardcore Omnifocus user, I was doubtful I'd ever need another to do app. Any.Do, however, does simple task lists so well and so quickly that it perfectly fits a niche that (by the very nature of its power) Omnifocus can not.

It also boasts what is arguably the best UI in an app, ever. If you need something more complex, get another app, as I would hope this one never loses its focus on simplicity.

The biggest downside, really, is that it's suspicious it's free, and that it has a number of weird glitches.

It's either not important or super important right now but some times things are in the middle so I'd think it be cool and useful if when you touched on the priorities icon it would have more colors that represent the task importance, far instance, tapping it once would change the task to yellow (important but low priority), twice orange (mid priority), three times red (high priority). title: Neat
body:
After using this for a while, I really like it for planning my near future. Quicker than OmniFocus, way more functional and useful than Clear, pretty, easy to add a note now and bulk out the details later. 

I am a little skeptical that it is free. How exactly do you plan to make money? By compromising my personal security and selling off my daily, weekly, and irregular habits? I try to be as generic as possible when making notes for this reason. Would pay for app if it gives the security that you won't sell me out. But I like it too much to quit it right now.

Issue with the recent update: notes don't move from list to list. I used to complain that they did move, but now that I'm using the app more effectively I find this not moving is a problem. Items due today are still on "tomorrow" or "later" lists. They display correctly in landscape, as another user noted.

title: Simple/great app but with some minor grievances
body:
It's great for the simplicity required in a to-do list. Syncing via cloud between multiple devices is also absolutely awesome. The interface is very intuitive and the voice-input rivals the accuracy of Siri.

My complaints, however, are quite critical:
Why in gods name does the computer app not allow sharing or easy syncing of notes to my mobile devices? My biggest complaint is the downright horrible implementation of the 'share' function. It doesn't work or if it does it excludes notes, dates and priority. My girlfriend and I live together and very frequently try to use an app like this to efficiently prioritize and get things done.. And when an integral function like this fails us, then it's just worthless and counter-productive.

We both use iPhones, an iPad and macs.. So it's not a cross-platform issue, but an app issue.

title: Horrible
body:
Everything written in this app must have a date associated with it. News flash: items that have a time associated with them belong in a calendar app, not a list app. You want a list of things to get done, not an agenda. That's what a calendar is for.

Secondly, this app doesn't really allow for multiple lists. Its use of folders and sublists is a poor substitute for having multiple lists.

The third thing a to-do list app needs is syncing. It has to sync your phone, tablet, and computer. That way you can access, write and edit your to-do list no matter where you are, and choose the method of entry that's most efficient for you. (For instance, I type on my computer much faster than on my phone.) If syncing is allowed, desktop apps are much better than web sites: they're faster and don't depend on the site's availability. So, for this app syncing is a FAIL.

title: This will help you get things done
body: One of the first things I observed about project management is that schedules are a lie.. Long term ones that is. This app by default encourages you to make your list based on what you are going to do today, tomorrow, this week, and and later. This is great for GTD and pomodoro fans. One of the more amazing features is how it will scan your contact list and suggest people from it as you type. I try every ToDo list app and this is my new everyday list. Personally I supplement this app with toodledo which has a ton of features but in my opinion not light weight enough for everyday regular use.

title: It's okay, needs a bit more work
body:
I tried testing it out by setting a non-important reminder (wash clothes) to see if that works. The first time, no alarm, noise, or beep went off to notify me when the time came for it to do so. Only until I went back, reset the time for 5 minutes later, & changed its priority did it actually notify me. Hopefully that doesn't happen again say I forget to make a task a priority.

Additionally, when I set it up in my notification center, I put it so that when it notifies me, it'll be at the top of my notifications. However, after trying multiple times, when I move it to the top of my notifications in my settings menu, and then leave the settings menu, when I go back it's at the bottom of my notifications again. I'm not sure if that's my phone making that happen or if it's the app, just a heads up though. 

Other than that, the app is amazing. Exactly what I'd want out of a planner/reminder type of app. It's a little buggy, but it's free, and it's new, so as expected it's supposed to have a few issues... That I hope will be fixed soon.

title: Great, but needs work
body:
I've been a TeuxDeux loyalist for over a year, and thought I'd never need another to do app. But there are still a few lingering bugs with TeuxDeux that I've begun to notice as a heavy user, and that team doesn't seem interested in continuing to work on that app. 

So Any.DO looked like the ideal replacement, and in a lot of ways it is. The best feature it shares with TeuxDeux is the ability to organize to do items by day -- something that's oddly rare. It's a must-have for me. Any.DO also looks amazing and it's synching with Chrome (and its web page coming soon) is everything I want and need. 

But christ this thing is buggy. While I've encountered a fair number of crashes and weird things, the fatal flaw is that tasks in "tomorrow" don't automatically move to "today". Which in many ways just ruins the app. 

It's free, so how much can I complain, but until they work these bugs out the app is barely usable for me.

Try adding notes to a to-do item, for instance. Instead of seeing the entire note at once, it displays as a tiny single line of text that slowly scrolls across. 

This app asks for Facebook credentials EVERY TIME it launches. Why would anybody want to integrate their to do list with Facebook? 

If you want a fiddly little interface to play around with, this is the app for you. If you want to get something done? Look elsewhere.

title: Drag and drop todo, finally!
body:
I've struggled for years to find a todo app that allows simple drag and drop reordering an date selection.  Dinally there is an app to do it (and a nice Google Chrome companion plugin as well!)

The landscape view might be a little tricky at first, but with some practice you can drag a task from the list onto any other date in the month calendar!  No more needless modal dialogs and "edit" buttons to do one simple
operation. 

HINTS:
- Notes field allows dictation of text too!
- Subtasks?  YES (sort of). Just add several notes to a task. These can be the individual actions needed to complete the main task
- Install Any.do in google chrome, sync chrome plugins to multiple PCs, and you can have your todos everywhere!

So many other todo apps have so many "features", but havent taken full advantage of the iPhone form factor and touch screen interface like Any.do has

title: Not what it used to be
body:
Two years ago I would have 5 starred this app - I even used to pay for premium for about four years - but the amount of changes and "improvements" that have been brought to this application have completely changed the way it used to function and have forced a number of drastic changes without giving us proper settings to disable the new changes. 

For example, you used to just be able to sort your tasks into any order without having to deal with setting a time for each task, but now every time you move something around or say, push something to next week, the app automatically assigns it a date and time that I don't get to set the default for, and most importantly, I can't disable it. Moving a task to tomorrow WILL put it in your calendar whether you like it or not, requiring you to manually disable each one. There are a number of other similar minor but massively inconvenient and forced changes are at the core of this 1 star. Another would be the way they force default list orders on you. It used to work perfectly, then once we were used to how it worked, they just changed everything without even giving us a choice.

If the developers give us a sorely overdue overhaul of the application settings and give us the ability to make things function as they always did going back the last two years, I'll come back and fix this review, hell, even pay for premium again, but it's doubtful that they will even see this given how non existent their premium "priority" support was. In the meantime I'll just be using a pen and a pad of paper because it's so much less inconvenient.
